# Next move: E5-CEILING (KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v1), amended per the refuters

Read-only session: nothing in `/home/user/KOD-Machine` was modified, no harness run, no network pull. HEAD is now `c380678` (orchestrator handoff commits on top of `e635e22`; harness code unchanged). Draft protocol written outside the repo at `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-KOD-Machine/74d3ac27-b8ad-5917-a6c3-ea51c410b250/scratchpad/E5_CEILING_protocol_draft.json`.

## 1. State in one paragraph

Across 11 experiments on 4 branches, detection of the +30%/5-session event is real but non-tradeable, and the reason is now located. The return-triggered detectors have validated lift (F1_ARA 9.3x, G2_RET30 US 5.4x, crypto 4.6x vs matched random, p at the 0.005 floor) with tiny recall (9.8% / 0.9% / 0.1%) and a median 5-session path after the flag of about -10% vs 0% for matched names; every long plan on them loses (IDX -4.06% vs -0.53%; US -3.65% vs -0.60%, best repair -0.97% vs -0.75%; crypto -1.90% vs +1.42%), 108 IDX plans and 144+288 crypto short plans admitted nothing that survived a second year, the breakout baseline is flat (D=-0.04pp, p 0.86), and the one frozen regime plan failed 2023 (34 scored, -1.50%, 3 liquidations). The decisive fact, verified by all three refuters from `trades.csv.gz`, is that the GROSS mean is already negative in every recorded run (IDX -3.67% gross / -4.06% net; crypto -1.51% / -1.90%; US -3.19% / -3.65%; US fill-B -0.10% / -0.97%): cost, fill and quarantine reruns moved magnitudes, never signs, so execution work cannot rescue these flags. The only pre-event separator ever measured is 20-session volatility (AUC 0.68 / 0.78 / 0.56), which is symmetric; nothing has tested whether any combination of daily-bar features carries direction, nothing has tested pre-move structure, and nothing has joined non-price information. Every validation year is consumed, the holdouts are sealed, and prospective evidence is one scored outcome (a correct rejection). Edge, if it exists for this lab, can therefore live in only three places: (a) a daily-bar feature combination with direction, never tested; (b) pre-move tape structure, never tested; (c) timestamped information inputs (EDGAR acceptance times), never joined. The cheapest decisive test covers (a) and screens (b) with data already on disk; (c) needs data not in the repo.

## 2. The next move

**Recommendation: run proposal #4 (E5-CEILING) as the single next experiment, restructured into an information stage and an execution stage, with the pre-spike features and the KOD VOLUME_CREEP row grafted from #1 and the paired-excess machinery grafted from #5/#2.** It answers the question every other proposal presupposes ("is there any daily-bar T-0 information with direction?") before anyone builds another scanner, and it gives #1's hypothesis its pre-screen at zero extra runs. Judges 1 and 2 ranked it first; its two "refuted: true" verdicts are fixable in the protocol and are fixed below.

Honesty rule: this experiment does not promise edge. Its likely outcome, by the lab's own prior, is a null. The null is the valuable result: it closes the tape-only detector family on information grounds (for this learner and feature list) and redirects effort to information inputs. A pass would be the first located direction in the program, still provisional on a once-seen year, and would license only a prospective paper policy.

### Protocol draft (ready to freeze as `research/E5/protocol.json`)

**Question.** At the close of session t, does any pre-registered combination of daily-bar features carry tradeable direction for t+1..t+5 over the full evaluable universe, beyond matched controls, or is the validated "detection" variance detection? Secondary: does multi-session pre-move structure (creep / quiet / contraction / re-base), including the KOD-DET-v0 VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET definition, carry +30% information?

**Family.** MOONSHOT_E5, new module `idx-signals/idxsig/rules/moonshot_e5.py`, long only, VERSION v1, candidate ids `E5_CAND_<MARKET>_<ARM>`, selected `MOONSHOT_E5_<MARKET>_D1`. FEATURE_ARGS = close, prev, high, low, volume, value, present, tradeable, lock_up, open.

**Features** (all from RULE_FIELDS; per-session cross-sectional percentile rank among names present and tradeable at that session, masked by `present` BEFORE ranking so the prefix-first check passes, NaN rank -> 0.5, plus squared rank; binaries enter as 0/1):
- E1/E2 weak-signal list verbatim (E1-SIGNALS-v1 / E2-SIGNALS-v1): ret1, rel1, ret5, ret20, volr, valr, rngr, cpos, vol20, dd60, up5, zero20, age, logval20; brk60 (binary); gap (US/CRYPTO); ara (IDX, binary).
- Pre-spike block grafted from #1: creep5v20 = median(volume t-4..t)/median(volume t-24..t-5); rngr5 = median(rngr t-4..t); vc10_60 = vol10/vol60; quiet = rngr5 <= 1.0 and |ret5| <= 2·vol20·sqrt(5) (ZEALAND `price_facts.py` verbatim, frozen 2026-10-08); not_repriced = ret20 < 0.30; rebase = a session s0 in [t-40, t-6] with ret1 >= 0.30 (IDX: lock_up & tradeable, because a +30% close is impossible above Rp200 under ARA bands), level(t) <= pre + 0.5·(peak-pre), min level(t-4..t) >= pre.
- WARMUP = 60 literal: `compute()` returns NaN for the first 60 sessions of its view; every harness window starts 60 sessions before the period so features are warm at period start (IDX warm-up falls in TIER_2, features only, no trades, declared).

**Labels.** U = max level(t+1..t+5)/level(t) >= 1.30 (E30 on the reference chain). D on US/CRYPTO = min level(t+1..t+5)/level(t) <= 1/1.30. D on IDX = rate-matched threshold fixed once on discovery so P(D) = P(U); IDX Arm B is diagnostic only (ARB was 7% flat through all of discovery and changes 2023-06-05 and 2023-09-04; IDX directional results reported by ARB regime). Labels require t+5 inside the period. Crypto unit resets (close/prev >= 20 or <= 1/20) censor labels for t-5..t of that name; the known 2020-2023 cases (COCOS 2021-01-23, DREP 2021-04-02, SUN 2021-06-18, LUNA 2022-05-31, VIDT 2022-11-09, BNX 2023-02-22, QUICK 2023-07-21, BTCST 2021-03-19 to verify) are listed in the protocol.

**Learner.** L2 logistic regression, numpy IRLS 25 iterations, lambda = 1e-3·n, all positives + 10% seeded negative subsample weighted 10 (seed 20261015), one fit per (market, label) = 6 fits. Arm A score = logit_U; Arm B = logit_U − logit_D. Threshold = discovery 99.5th percentile of each arm's score (top 0.5%, comparable to F1_ARA's 0.54% 2023 flag rate), never searched. Debounce: a signal only on the first session a name enters the top 0.5% after >= 5 sessions outside it (trailing, prefix-safe). Coefficients and thresholds committed as module-level literal tuples; the rule hash covers them.

**Descriptive detectors (no trading run unless gated).** A0_CREEP_QUIET = creep >= 1.5 AND quiet (exact `kod/detectors.py:72-86` logic); A1 = A0 AND not_repriced (#1's reference member). Each gets debounced flags, base rate, precision, Wilson bounds, lift vs volatility-matched controls on discovery: the population row KOD doctrine lines 79-81 require. A1 gets ONE trading run under the market plan only if its lift >= 2.0 at p < 0.05 on discovery. A univariate matched-set AUC/lift table for every ranked feature is written (the pre-screen #1's refuter demanded; the single-day proxy already on record predicts lift about 1.1 / 0.96 / 0.95).

**Plans.** One per market, the recorded one, no plan search. IDX: next close -> 5th close, fill C primary (A sensitivity), ca_mode registry, Rp10m, lot 100, plus a one-tick-per-side cost sensitivity (rule and controls alike). US: next open -> 5th close on `panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z` (sha 8d3b7ce4), units as_traded, fill B primary (A as_traded sensitivity), quarantine none (unit_schedule as sensitivity), +1.5%/side stress reported, $5,000. CRYPTO: next open -> 5th close on `panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z`, fill A primary (as E2/E4), jump_ratio = 10 (EXCLUDED_DATA_JUMP for rule and baselines, PR #7 code), sensitivities = fill A at participation 0.05 with doubled costs, and entry at the close of t+1 via a CRYPTO_CLOSE profile variant (latency-pessimistic); costs stated as 0.1% fee + 0.1% tier = 0.2%/side (the recorded config, not 0.3%).

**Markets.** IDX TIER_1 (decisive for Arm A: survivorship-complete), CRYPTO (decisive for Arm B: no price limits, 190 delisted pairs present), US (survivor-only: every US result diagnostic; a US-only pass is not decision-grade).

**Periods.** Discovery IDX 2021-01-22..2022-12-30; US/CRYPTO 2020-07-01..2022-12-31. Validation 2023 (IDX ..12-29; US/CRYPTO ..12-31), one recorded run per admissible arm. Holdout never loaded: IDX guarded by `backtest.HOLDOUT`; US/CRYPTO by PR #7's GLOBAL_HOLDOUT plus an assert in `e5.py` that end <= validation end before any RunConfig. Declared leak: 2023 is once-seen for the univariate siblings of E5's features (ara via E1, ret1 via E2, brk60 via US_BREAKOUT_v1; episode tables with ret5/ret20/volr/rngr/vol20/dd60 sit on disk under the E1/E2 validation directories), so any 2023 pass is PROVISIONAL.

**Costs.** Profiles unchanged (IDX 0.15%/0.25%; US tier 1.5%/0.5%/0.15%/0.05% + SEC fee; CRYPTO 0.2%/side); gross and net both reported.

**Matched controls.** Trading stage: new additive `controls.VERSIONS['v3']` = price_band, liquidity quintile, volatility QUINTILE, market_cap (IDX mirror era), momentum, drawdown, listing_age, relaxed to MIN_POOL 5; v2 reported for comparability (on the recorded IDX run 28% of attempts were never matched on volatility under v2). Detection stage: `e1.Study` pool extended to volatility quintile, with the US band on the as-traded close (unit_factor attached), closing the ERRATA.md wrong-band defect. Paired statistic: per-signal excess = rule outcome minus the mean of its 200 matched controls (new additive `trades.csv` columns `matched_mean_net_return`, `same_session_mean_net_return` in `backtest.run`), session-cluster bootstrap over signal sessions (10,000 resamples, seed 20261015), one-sided p. The harness's draw-distribution p is reported, not judged (it is anti-conservative when the rule's trades are more volatile than the controls': implied size 14-27% on the recorded runs).

**Admissibility.**
- Stage 0 reproduce: pinned runs re-run from their recorded configs (IDX 20261009T050040Z fill C; US 20261008T115656Z fill B as recorded; CRYPTO 20261008T005732Z); REPRODUCED/DEVIATES on record; only the known 4th-decimal matched deviation (controls.py bcb89f0) is accepted.
- Stage 1 information (discovery, fill-independent): for each arm, the plan-window return on the reference chain (entry level at close t+1 IDX / open t+1 US-CRYPTO, exit at the 5th close) for flags and matched controls alike, no fill, lot, lock or cost filter; plus AUC_U, AUC_D, E30/D30 precision and lift, directional ratio with cluster-bootstrap CI, pre-move split (ret1 < 10%). Gate to Stage 2: debounced flags >= 200; paired gross excess > 0 with cluster-bootstrap p < 0.025 (Bonferroni over the two primaries P1 = IDX Arm A, P2 = CRYPTO Arm B); excess > 0 in every discovery year with >= 50 flags. Everything else (IDX B, CRYPTO A, US A/B, A0/A1) is diagnostic with pre-declared reporting.
- Stage 2 execution (discovery, only for arms that passed Stage 1): `e3.admissibility` verbatim (scored >= 200, avg net > 0, harness p < 0.05, avg net > 0 each year with >= 50 scored) AND paired net excess p < 0.025 AND every sensitivity keeps rule-minus-matched > 0 AND admissibility holds on trades with exit-session participation <= 10% (exit-capacity diagnostic: 21.9% of the recorded IDX trades sold more than 10% of exit-day volume and averaged -6.4%).
- Freeze: coefficients/thresholds into `moonshot_e5.py` literals, SELECTED per market, committed; validation refuses unless literals == `discovery/model.json`.

**Validation criteria (2023, once per Stage-2-admissible arm).** Scored >= 100 (US >= 200), avg net > 0, paired net excess > 0 with cluster-bootstrap p < 0.025, harness p < 0.05, sensitivities agree in sign, detection Wilson lower bound > 2023 base rate. Claim level PROVISIONAL.

**Consequence if passed.** Freeze MOONSHOT_E5_<MARKET>_D1; a new POLICY_ID (PAPER-POLICY-v5) wires it through `paper._detector`; no paper BUY until >= 100 prospective scored E5 decisions show paired excess > 0; holdout stays sealed until then. The coefficient vector names which features carry direction.

**Consequence if failed.** Stage 1 fails in both primaries: daily-bar T-0 direction is not detectable by this learner over this feature list where it can be measured; stop building tape-only detectors; next protocol is information timing (8-K acceptance, proposal #0) after the SEC probe; the KOD tape feed is not stood up unless the A1 row's lift CI excludes 1. Stage 1 passes but Stage 2 or validation fails: information exists but is not executable under daily-bar plans; next work is an execution contract (limit-on-open, capacity, exit liquidity), not plan search.

**Refuter demands incorporated:** paired per-signal test with session clustering; controls v3 with a finer volatility bucket; IDX D label regime-aware and demoted; crypto fill-B sensitivity replaced by executable sensitivities; information verdict split from execution verdict; debounce; present-mask before ranking; WARMUP; US on the causal repair panel in as-traded units as primary; exit-capacity diagnostic; universe-wide p* clause dropped (in-flag break-even p* kept as a descriptive bound); jump_ratio on crypto; cost text corrected; search size stated.

**Refutations not fixed, proceeding anyway:** (1) 2023 is once-seen: no clean in-repo year exists; mitigated by pre-registration, Bonferroni, provisional claim level and the prospective sidecar. (2) US survivorship: no point-in-time universe on free data; US demoted to diagnostic. (3) A null from one bounded learner is "not found by this learner", not a proof; the consequence is a management decision stated as such; a second learner is a new protocol. (4) IDX closing-auction spread: one-tick sensitivity only; a panel-v3 with the mirror's bid/offer depth is deferred. (5) Crypto legacy panel carries 2 future-informed row deletions (LUNA 2022-05-13 in discovery): declared, not rebuilt, because a rebuild would make the precondition DEVIATE. (6) Daily bars cannot model intraday latency; the close(t+1) crypto leg bounds it.

**Runners-up and why they are not the next move:** #1 is grafted (features, A0/A1 rows, univariate pre-screen) rather than run as a 72-run grid, because its refuter showed the single-day proxy lift is about 1 and its IDX re-base members are confined to the <=Rp200 band; the grid runs only if the A1 gate passes. #2 (delayed entry) is a sound, cheap, optional parallel experiment (E6) once PR #7 lands, but only with jump_ratio=10, as_traded US units, a tail-robustness co-criterion and a relative-by-year verdict; it is a fourth plan search on consumed flags and is lower priority than knowing whether any direction exists. #5 (breadth regime) is a second look at the same consumed 2023 for the frozen detectors; its paired-excess column is grafted; it should run, if at all, after E5 says whether direction exists. #0 (8-K timing) is the designated follow-on, not the next move: its data is not on disk, SEC reachability and the acceptanceDateTime timezone are unpinned, and the ticker-to-CIK map is survivor-only. #3 (full STRICT KOD feed) is deferred: 48h of infrastructure for about 30 cases in three months, with committed-sqlite growth of 3-4 MB/day, before any evidence that its one tape detector has lift.

## 3. Infrastructure prerequisites, landing order

1. **Merge PR #7** (`origin/claude/e4-fade-short-side` @ 2b26197): merge-tree clean, CI green, no policy change. It supplies GLOBAL_HOLDOUT for US/crypto (`backtest.py:85,296`), `jump_ratio` / EXCLUDED_DATA_JUMP, open-entry conditional plans, the `e4.py` market-loop pattern to clone, and the RUNS.jsonl line E5 must append after. Blocks every E5 crypto run and the code-level holdout guard. Owner decision.
2. **Additive harness commits on base+#7** (all committed before any run; `write_run` refuses a dirty tree): `controls.py` VERSIONS v3; `backtest.run` per-trade matched-mean columns; `e1.py` accept `panel-global-v2-units` (line 100), guard the IGNITION lookup (line 190), attach unit_factor for as-traded band matching; `profiles.py` CRYPTO_CLOSE variant; `rules/moonshot_e5.py` skeleton (SELECTED None), registry entry in `rules/__init__.py:61-64`; `e5.py`; `cli.py` e5-reproduce / e5-discovery / e5-validation; `tests/test_e5.py`. Blocks Stage 0.
3. **Data builds, no network**: rebuild `panel-20261013T194245Z` with `idxsig build-panel` from the on-disk mirror `bc0ac7712ce5` (975 files present) and check sha a924921a / registry 33f81beb; if it does not reproduce, pre-register the on-disk fallback `panel-20261007T225823Z` + `ca_registry-20261007T230210Z` with E3's DEVIATES note. US repair and crypto panels are on disk. Blocks Stage 0 for IDX only.
4. **Freeze** `research/E5/protocol.json` + PROTOCOL.md (sha recorded) -> Stage 0 -> Stage 1 -> Stage 2 -> freeze literals -> validation. Each stage a new `exist_ok=False` directory.
5. **PR #5** (codex retention protocol): additive and clean; not a prerequisite; land whenever the author renames its "E3" label (collides with base E3) and accepts it frozen.
6. **PR #3** (us-pipeline): last and not a prerequisite for E5. It conflicts in `cli.py`, `execution.py`, `paper.py` (4 hunks), reuses the PAPER-POLICY-v4 id already on 18 ledger lines, and removes E3 machinery; it must be rebased onto base+#7 with union resolution, its policy renumbered to a new id, and its README paragraph rewritten. It is needed only when a paper policy for a validated E5 arm wants the EXEC-US-v2.1 account model.

Note on collisions: four proposals claim `moonshot_e5.py` / `research/E5`; this protocol takes E5; E6 is reserved for the delayed-entry grid, E7 for 8-K information.

## 4. Parallel track

Do not start KPF-v1 now. Start two cheap prospective things that need no policy change and no KOD case:

- **E5 prospective sidecar** (about 4h, from the freeze commit onward): `tools/paper_e5_sidecar.py` runs after each paper scan, computes the frozen E5 ranker scores and the A0/A1 facts for every name in the scan's eligible universe from the scan's own 200-day bar pull (`data/raw/*_recent`), and appends one hash-chained, RFC 3161-stamped line per scan to `research/E5/prospective/sidecar.jsonl` (append-only under `tools/check_append_only.py`); `decide()` never reads it; joined to later bars at reporting time. This is the prospective evidence E5's pass rule requires and it accrues whether or not the backtest passes.
- **SEC submissions probe** (about 2h; needs owner authorization for a network pull and a real `IDXSIG_SEC_USER_AGENT`): 50 random 8-K filings, `data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json` reachability from the routine host, `acceptanceDateTime` vs filing-index "Accepted" field to pin the timezone, written to the scratchpad. It de-risks #0 as the next experiment if E5 returns a null.
- **KOD scan feed**: stand up a scan-only `kod scan` of the daily paper universes (no STRICT cases, gzip bodies, US 20% hash cohort) under a new scanner id only if the A1 row's discovery lift CI excludes 1; otherwise VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET is closed at KOD-DET-v0 thresholds and the feed waits for a document source.

## 5. What we will know after

- **Stage 1 fails in both primaries (IDX Arm A excess <= 0 or p >= 0.025; CRYPTO Arm B likewise), A0/A1 lift about 1:** no daily-bar T-0 direction for this learner; the 9.3x/5.4x/4.6x "detection" is variance detection if Arm A's D30 lift sits inside its E30 lift CI; tape-only detector building stops; E7 (8-K timing) is next after the SEC probe; KOD tape feed closed; paper ledger keeps accruing.
- **Stage 1 fails but A1's lift CI excludes 1:** pre-move volume structure detects without direction; stand up the scan-only KOD feed; A1 gets its one gated trading run.
- **Stage 1 passes in a primary, Stage 2 fails (costs, fills, exit capacity, sensitivities):** information exists but is not executable on daily bars under fixed-notional plans; next work is an execution contract, not another plan search; the sidecar keeps scoring the frozen ranker.
- **Stage 2 passes on discovery, 2023 validation fails:** regime-bound or over-fit; family closed (no second design pass); the prospective sidecar is the only remaining path for this ranker.
- **Validation passes:** first located direction in the program, provisional; PAPER-POLICY-v5 wires MOONSHOT_E5_<MARKET>_D1 into the ledger; >= 100 prospective scored decisions with positive paired excess before any BUY; holdout-final only after that.
- **Pre-move split, in every case:** whether any lift exists before the first +10% day, the only kind a retail participant could act on.

## 6. Effort, runtime, owner decisions

Build about 40-48h over 6-8 working days: harness additive changes 10h, rule module + `e5.py` 16h, tests 8h, protocol/docs 4h, IDX panel rebuild 2h, sidecar 4h, review slack. Runtime under a day: six fits in minutes (US matrix about 2.7M rows x about 45 columns with the seeded subsample); harness runs at most about 24 (IDX seconds each per E3's 108-run precedent; US fill-B runs on the 4.4M-row panel are the slow ones, tens of minutes each). Owner must decide: (1) merge PR #7; (2) authorize a branch `claude/e5-ceiling` and its push; (3) accept that a 2023 pass is provisional and that the holdout stays sealed; (4) authorize the IDX panel rebuild (no network) and the SEC probe (network); (5) whether E6 (delayed entry, about 2 engineer-days with the fixes) runs in parallel; (6) confirm KPF-v1 waits for the A1 row.

proposals.title: E5_US_INFO_v1 (KOD-US-E5-v1): 8-K information timing - documented vs undocumented +30% days, and filing-type triggers as detectors
proposals.angle: INFORMATION/CATALYST: condition on and detect primary-document timing (SEC EDGAR 8-K acceptance timestamps, item-typed) joined causally to the US daily panel; no tape threshold is changed, no new tape signal is searched.
proposals.thesis: Every detector run so far (E1 F-family, E2 G-family, E3 plans, E4 shorts, US_BREAKOUT) read the tape only, and every PASS in the paper ledger literally says 'no news or filing was read' (idx-signals/idxsig/paper.py:574). The KOD doctrine says repricings follow information and that a primary document before price is the detector-grade fact; the only test of that idea is one retrospective event (ZEALAND) and four retrospective cards. Hypothesis H1 (Track A, the +30% day with vs without a document): among G2_RET30 flags (day return >= +30%, code copied verbatim), the flags whose session carries an 8-K accepted by EDGAR between the prior close and 15:45 ET of the flag session ('documented spikes', I1_DOC_RET30) reprice again (+30% max close within t+1..t+5) more often and lose less under the E2 plan than flags with no 8-K in the last six sessions ('undocumented spikes', I2_NODOC_RET30). Mechanism: a documented move is a repricing of a public fact that other holders have not finished digesting (post-event drift), whereas an undocumented +30% day in a survivor-only US micro-cap universe is more often a liquidity/pump episode that mean-reverts; the matched controls cannot see this because docs are not a control feature. Hypothesis H2 (Track B, filing-type trigger alone): an item-typed 8-K (1.01 material agreement, 2.01 completed transaction, 7.01 Reg FD, 8.01 other events) accepted while the price is still quiet (|ret1| <= 5%, volume <= 2x median) - the population form of KOD-DET-v0 PRIMARY_DOC_BEFORE_PRICE - has E30 precision at least 2x matched random controls (same session, price band, liquidity quintile, volatility tercile). Both are tested with discovery 2020-07..2022, one validation pass on 2023, and a prospective sidecar log that records the same doc fields for every live US paper decision from the day the protocol is frozen.
proposals.why_not_already_falsified: Different information source: E1/E2/E3/E4 and the breakout baseline used only the 12 exchange fields a rule may see (idx-signals/idxsig/rules/__init__.py:89-90); no experiment has ever joined a filing, a press release or an earnings date to the panel, and controls.py v2 cannot match on documents, so the document dimension is orthogonal to every lift and every loss recorded so far. Different structure: Track A is a pre-registered two-arm contrast of an exogenous binary (EDGAR clock), not a new threshold or plan - E3 searched 108 plans and E4 288 short plans on the same tape; E3_US_RETENTION (unrun) conditions on close(t+1), still tape. Track B has no tape trigger at all; the only earlier non-tape detector evaluation is KOD-DET-v0 on 4 retrospective cards (all NO_SIGNAL) and the single ZEALAND event, which the pilot itself says cannot estimate a rate and which is excluded here by construction (US only, 2020-2023). The map's one pre-event separator (20-session volatility, AUC 0.78 US) is matched away in this design's detection controls (E5-MATCH-v1 adds the volatility tercile to E1-MATCH-v1), so a filing lift cannot be 'volatile names file more'. The expected sign is not foregone: E2's pooled result (median 5-session return -10.3% after a G2 flag, US 2023) is consistent with both 'documented spikes drift' and 'documented spikes are complete at the open'; either outcome changes what the paper policy may say in a PASS reason, and a null kills the doctrine's document criterion as a daily-bar US detector input.

I2_NODOC_RET30: ret1 >= 0.30 AND doc_any(t)=0 AND doc_last(t) > 5 (no 8-K in sessions t-5..t); names without a CIK map are NaN (not evaluable) in both arms
I3_PREDOC_RET30 (descriptive only, not tested): ret1 >= 0.30 AND doc_pre(t)=1 (8-K accepted in (16:00 ET t-1, 09:30 ET t]: the move began as a gap on the document)

protocol.plans: exactly one plan, E2's, for every rule and every control: buy at the open of s+1 (US profile entry_price='open', entry_lag 1), sell at the close of the 5th session after entry (holding_days 5), no stop, overlap skip, $5,000 notional, lot 1. No plan grid is searched (E3/E4 showed plan search on these tapes is exhausted; this experiment isolates the information variable).
protocol.discovery_period: 2020-07-01 .. 2022-12-31 (E2's discovery window; in-sample for G2_RET30's threshold, which is not re-tuned; the document split is new information never joined to any outcome)
protocol.validation_period: 2023-01-01 .. 2023-12-29, one pass, after the freeze commit. Track B (information-only detector) treats 2023 as a clean validation year: no filing-based rule was ever selected on it. Track A is labelled explicitly 'a stratified re-read of a year whose pooled G2_RET30 outcomes were seen (E2, 9 reruns)': the direction is fixed by doctrine before any number so it cannot be chosen on 2023, but its evidential weight is lower than Track B's and the decisive Track A evidence is the prospective sidecar (see admissibility).
protocol.admissibility: Track A (contrast, discovery): both arms >= 200 flags, else NOT EVALUABLE (reported, neither supported nor falsified). Supported on discovery iff (a) P(E30|I1) - P(E30|I2) >= +3.0 pp with one-sided two-proportion z p < 0.05 in the pre-registered direction I1 > I2, and (b) avg net(I1) - avg net(I2) under the one plan > 0 with session-block bootstrap p < 0.05 (2,000 resamples, seed 20261007). I1 is additionally an executable candidate only if it meets E3's rule: scored >= 200, avg net > 0, one-sided p < 0.05 vs matched random, avg net > 0 in every discovery year with >= 50 scored. Track B (information-only, discovery): admissible iff flags >= 200, Wilson 95% lower bound of E30 precision > base rate, lift vs E5-MATCH-v1 matched random >= 2.0 with one-sided p < 0.05 (200 draws per flag, floor 0.005); the admissible candidate with the highest lift is selected (ties by flags); trading run only for the selected one, judged by E3's rule above; I8 must show lift <= 1 or the item-class mapping is flagged as suspect (reported, not judged). Validation 2023 (one pass): Track A passes iff the same (a) and (b) hold; Track B selected passes iff detection Wilson lower bound > base rate, lift >= 2.0, p < 0.05 AND trading scored >= 100, avg net > 0, p < 0.05 vs matched. Prospective arm: from the freeze date the US paper routine appends, for every US DECISION, the same doc fields retrieved from data.sec.gov at decision time (retrieval time recorded, hash-chained, never read by decide()); first prospective contrast reported at 200 scored US decisions, judged by (a) only. Consequence if passed: a new paper policy version may cite the document fact in US decisions; no BUY until the executable plan also passes. Consequence if failed: EDGAR 8-K timing is dropped from the detector roadmap; holdout stays sealed.
protocol.costs_model: profiles.US unchanged: per side 1.5% under $1, 0.5% $1-5, 0.15% $5-20, 0.05% above, SEC fee on sales, no impact, no dividends; fill model B (FILL-B-v1: 10% of the 20-session median as-traded volume through the signal, decision-time), units as_traded from the repair panel's unit_factor, quarantine none (the repair_v3 finding that quarantine is outcome-correlated), with quarantine unit_schedule reported as a sensitivity, not judged. Unverified pre-2023 split units affect cost tier and lot size only (max 1.45% per side); both arms and all controls share it.
protocol.matched_controls: Trading stage: controls v2 exactly as the harness computes them (same session; price band, liquidity quintile, market cap quintile [one bucket for US], volatility tercile, momentum tercile, drawdown tercile, listing age; relaxed to >= 5 names), 200 draws per attempted signal, executed under the identical plan, plus the same-session uniform baseline. Detection stage: E5-MATCH-v1 = E1-MATCH-v1 (same session, price band, liquidity quintile) plus 20-session volatility tercile, relaxed in that order, 200 draws per flag; the doc share among drawn controls is reported so contamination is visible. For Track A the primary comparison is arm vs arm; each arm's matched baseline is reported beside it.

proposals.falsifier: On discovery 2020-07-01..2022-12-31, with both arms >= 200 flags: P(E30 | I1_DOC_RET30) - P(E30 | I2_NODOC_RET30) < +3.0 pp or its one-sided two-proportion z-test (direction I1 > I2) gives p >= 0.05; AND no information-only candidate among I4..I8 with >= 200 flags reaches E30 lift >= 2.0 vs E5-MATCH-v1 matched random at one-sided p < 0.05. That exact pair of results means 8-K timing carries no detectable information about a +30% repricing at the daily-bar level in this universe; no validation run is made, the family is closed, and EDGAR timing leaves the detector roadmap. (If either Track A arm has < 200 flags the contrast is recorded NOT EVALUABLE, which neither supports nor falsifies H1.) If discovery passes, the 2023 pass fails and the hypothesis is rejected when the contrast's sign reverses or p >= 0.05, or when the selected Track B detector's Wilson lower bound on 2023 does not exceed the base rate.
risks: Look-ahead in filing timestamps: (1) EDGAR file_date rolls to the next business day for acceptances after 17:30 ET, so file_date is never used for attribution, only acceptanceDateTime; (2) the submissions JSON acceptanceDateTime carries a 'Z' suffix whose meaning (UTC vs the Eastern time shown on filing-index pages) must be pinned on a 50-filing sample before the freeze, else every attribution can be off by one session; (3) acceptance precedes public dissemination by seconds to minutes during 06:00-22:00 ET, hence the 15-minute pre-close cutoff (15:45 ET) and the 15-minute buffer are pre-registered; (4) the 8-K is an upper bound on the public time: the wire press release can precede the furnished 8-K by hours or days (issuers have four business days), and some releases are never furnished, so 'no document' means 'no EDGAR document', a misclassification that biases Track A toward the null (a positive finding is conservative, a null is weaker evidence).

Survivor-only universe (Nasdaq Trader 2026 snapshot): names delisted 2020-2026 are absent, and pump-type undocumented spikes are plausibly over-represented among delistings, so the I2 arm is the surviving subset; the sign of the bias on the contrast is unknown and is stated, not corrected.

CIK discontinuities (de-SPACs, re-domiciliations, holding-company reorganisations): 8-Ks filed under a predecessor CIK are missed, misclassifying those sessions as undocumented; the info-panel manifest reports mapped/unmapped counts and formerNames, but the residual is unknown.

Reachability and rate limits of data.sec.gov from the sandbox are untested (only companyconcept was reached before); ~6,000 requests at 5/s; fallback is the bulk submissions.zip; a placeholder User-Agent (HANDOFF item 8) must be replaced before any pull.

Harness change surface: extending RULE_FIELDS and Market.FIELDS touches the causal contract; a defect there could leak information to every rule, so the lookahead test (doc at d+1 must raise LookaheadError) and the reproduce stage (recorded E2 run byte-identical on the info panel) are preconditions, not afterthoughts.

Multiplicity: 8 candidates and one contrast; controlled by freezing the family, the lift >= 2.0 floor, the +3 pp materiality floor and a single validation pass; broad information-only detectors (I4/I6 may have tens of thousands of flags) are kept out of the trading stage by the lift floor, which also bounds compute (the detection evaluate loop at e1.py:334-376 is per flag).

Track A's 2023 validation is a consumed year for G2_RET30's pooled trading outcome; the pre-registered direction cannot be gamed but the weight of a 2023 pass is lower than a clean year; the prospective sidecar is slow (about 200 US decisions a month at the observed scan rate, doc share unknown), so a first prospective contrast with ~+/-5 pp half-width is months away.

Item-class map is a judgement fixed before data (1.01/2.01/7.01/8.01 as 'material', 2.02 earnings, 3.01/3.02/1.03/2.04/4.02/5.03 as 'distress/dilution'); if I8 shows lift > 1 the map is flagged suspect (reported), not re-cut.

Execution realism unchanged from E2: daily bars, assumed tier costs, no auction size, no LULD halts; a positive Track A trading contrast is a difference between two arms under the same assumptions, not a tradeable edge until the executable plan passes E3's rule and APPROVAL-v2.

Crypto and IDX cannot be covered now (no reachable announcement or disclosure history), so this is one market, one document type; a null does not falsify the doctrine for IDX disclosures or crypto listings.
proposals.directive_compliance: Holdout: the info panel is derived from the repair panel, which ends 2023-12-29, so it physically contains no 2024+ rows; the SEC filing table is truncated at 2023-12-31 before any join and the builder refuses any attributed session after 2023-12-29; every US run passes --end explicitly because HEAD lacks the GLOBAL_HOLDOUT code guard (present only on PR #7); the prospective sidecar records live 2026 decisions, which are not holdout data. No re-tune: G2_RET30's threshold and code are copied verbatim (tested identical); the document split is an exogenous binary defined by the EDGAR clock, not by outcomes; the direction of the contrast and the item classes are fixed in protocol.json before the submissions pull; Track B is a new family selected on discovery only, with one validation pass; the frozen detectors MOONSHOT_E1_D1, MOONSHOT_E2_*_D1, MOONSHOT_E4_D1 are not edited. Consumed-year honesty: Track A's 2023 result is labelled a stratified re-read of a year whose pooled G2 outcomes were seen and carries lower weight; the decisive Track A evidence is prospective. No manufactured results: every number above comes from the project map or is marked unknown (doc share among G2 flags, 8-K counts, timezone convention, reachability); no probability, trade or outcome is asserted. Pre-registration: research/E5_US_INFO_v1/protocol.json is committed with its sha256 before any statistic, every stage stamps the sha, directories are created once (exist_ok=False), results go through results.write_run into the append-only RUNS.jsonl, and the reproduce stage must pass (or be explicitly accepted as DEVIATES) before discovery. No orders, no ASTRA/production change, no paper-policy change (the sidecar is never read by decide()); real network pulls happen only when the owner starts the experiment.
proposals.expected_information_value: Whatever the sign, the experiment answers three questions the lab has never asked with a population and non-events: (1) does a primary document on the spike session change the post-spike path (if I1 > I2: information-conditioned detection is the next detector axis and the paper PASS reason gains an evidence-based catalyst field; if I1 = I2: 8-K timing is not operational at daily-bar resolution for US micro-caps and the document criterion leaves the roadmap; if I1 < I2 significantly: documented spikes are complete by the next open and undocumented ones carry the continuation, which points the E4 short family at I1 and a long family at I2, both new protocols); (2) the leak diagnostic (share of undocumented spikes followed by an 8-K within five sessions and their E30 rate) measures whether pre-announcement informed trading is a visible mechanism in this universe, a fact KOD's VOLUME_CREEP and PRIMARY_DOC detectors depend on; (3) Track B tells whether any filing-type trigger has detection lift net of volatility matching, i.e. whether PRIMARY_DOC_BEFORE_PRICE can ever be a scanner input rather than an operator fact, and I8 calibrates the item-class map. It also delivers reusable infrastructure: a point-in-time 8-K timing column with provenance, a tested RULE_FIELDS extension path for any future non-price input, and a prospective catalyst log attached to every live US decision, which is the watchlist source the KOD reader says the lab lacks.

proposals.title: E5 PRE-SPIKE TAPE (KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v1): accumulation, re-base and contraction detectors that fire WITHOUT a big up day, in IDX, US and crypto, with the KOD VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET definition as the frozen reference member
proposals.angle: NEW TAPE FAMILY: a tape-only detector family whose members require the ABSENCE of a move on the signal day (quiet band, not repriced) and read multi-session volume structure, post-fade path structure, or volatility contraction, instead of the day return / ARA lock / breakout / volume-surge-with-return triggers that every E1 (F1..F10) and E2 (G1..G11) member uses.
proposals.thesis: Every detector this lab has validated (F1_ARA, G2_RET30, the E3 plan grid, the E4 shorts, US_BREAKOUT_v1) triggers on the signal day's own return, so detection is real (9.3x/5.4x/4.6x matched random) but the executable edge is negative because entry comes inside a move whose median next-5-session path is -10% (E1/E2 REPORT.md; r5_median -10.3% US, -11.5% crypto). The hypothesis: a subset of future +30% moves is preceded, in daily bars, by a tape structure that is informative WITHOUT a return: (A) a multi-session volume creep (median volume of the last 5 sessions >= 1.5x the median of the prior 20) while price stays inside its own noise band and is not yet repriced (ret20 < +30%), the pre-markup accumulation signature of an operator working a thin IDX float ('goreng') or of informed buying ahead of a catalyst in US/crypto; (B) a re-base 6-40 sessions after a faded +30% day, where price gave back at least half the spike-to-peak gain but has held above the pre-spike level for five sessions in a quiet band (the holders left after the fade are sticky, so a second leg needs less supply); (C) a volatility contraction (10-session vol <= half of 60-session vol) in a historically volatile name that has not collapsed (supply exhausted before expansion). The mechanism that would make it true is that coordinated or informed buying shows in volume and path structure before it shows in price. The harness's v2 matched controls remove the price state (volatility tercile, momentum tercile, drawdown tercile, liquidity, price band, market cap, listing age), so a positive result is attributable to the volume/path structure and not to the already-known fact that volatile, beaten-down names reprice more often (vol20 AUC 0.68/0.78/0.56, dd60 0.40/0.25/0.41). The reference member A1_CREEP_QUIET is the KOD-DET-v0 VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET tape definition exactly as frozen on 2026-10-08 in kod-machine/research/ZEALAND_PILOT_v1/01_protocol/protocol.json and 03_card/price_facts.py (creep = median vol t-4..t / median vol t-24..t-5 >= 1.5; quiet = median rngr over t-4..t <= 1.0 and |ret5| <= 2*vol20*sqrt(5); not repriced = ret20 < 0.30), so its thresholds were fixed before this experiment for a different purpose and have never been tuned on any moonshot outcome; running it through the harness gives the KOD doctrine the population base rate and non-events (doctrine lines 79-81) it has never had for that detector (one retrospective case, NO_SIGNAL).
proposals.why_not_already_falsified: Signal family: all 21 frozen E1/E2 members need a move on the signal day (ret1 >= 3..30%, ARA lock, close above the 60-session high, open gap >= 10% held, 5-session return >= 30%) or a single-day volume surge (G4_VOL10 at 10x, G3/G5/G11 with a return or vol20 condition); none has a quiet condition, none uses a 5-session volume median against a prior-20 median, none excludes repriced names, none reads the post-spike path 6-40 sessions later, none measures vol10/vol60 contraction. A4_RVOL_FLAT explicitly requires |ret1| <= vol20 and no 60-session breakout, the opposite of G6/brk60. Information source: E1/E2's weak-signal tables (research/E1/discovery/signal_stats.csv; research/E2/REPORT.md) measured SINGLE-DAY ratios at the session before an episode start (volr 0.50, valr 0.50, freqr 0.50, rngr 0.49) and never computed the 5-session creep, the quiet band, the re-base path or the contraction on any panel, so 'volume surges carry no information on the start day' does not test multi-session accumulation that may precede the move by 1-20 sessions. Structure: E3 (108 plans) and E4 (144+288 short plans) searched execution plans for the SAME big-day detectors; US_BREAKOUT_v1 is a move trigger (close > prior 60-session closing high); E4 shorted the fade within 5 sessions of the spike while B1/B2 fire only after the fade has completed and price has re-based, a state no experiment has looked at. The volatility finding (the only pre-event separator) is used only as a conditioning tercile in A3/C1 and is neutralised by the matched controls, so the test asks what the structure adds beyond it. Unknown (not falsified, not confirmed): whether any member reaches 200 flags with E30 lift, whether the flagged population has the negative drift of the moonshot-prone names, whether a 5/10/20-session hold captures a move that arrives later; nothing in the repo answers these, which is why the experiment is needed.

protocol.family: MOONSHOT_E5 family, idxsig/rules/moonshot_e5.py, VERSION v1, long only, 8 members in three mechanism groups, thresholds fixed in protocol.json before any flag is computed. Common features (column d uses sessions <= d only; all from RULE_FIELDS close/prev/high/low/volume/present/tradeable/open): ret1 = close/prev-1 on tradeable sessions with prev>0; level = reference chain exp(cumsum log(close/prev)) as moonshot_g; ret5/ret20 on level; logret for vol; vol20 = std of logret over d-19..d (min 15), vol10 over d-9..d (min 8), vol60 over d-59..d (min 40); rng = (high-low)/prev where high/low present; rngr = rng / median(rng over d-20..d-1) (min 10); rngr5 = median(rngr over d-4..d) (5 values required); v5 = median(volume over d-4..d) on present sessions (untraded = 0), v_base = median(volume over d-24..d-5) (min 15 present), creep = v5/v_base where v_base>0; volr = volume/median(volume d-20..d-1) as moonshot_g; brk60 = level > max level over d-60..d-1 (min 20); dd60 = level/max level over d-59..d - 1; quiet(d) = rngr5 <= 1.0 and |ret5| <= 2*vol20*sqrt(5) [KOD price_quiet_vs_own_range verbatim]; not_repriced(d) = ret20 < 0.30 [KOD price_already_repriced = false]; hivol20(d) = vol20 >= 67th percentile of vol20 across evaluable names at d (cross-section at d only, as E1 uses the cross-sectional median); hivol60(d) likewise on vol60. Rules must pass rules/audit.py (numpy/pandas only, literal module constants) and the prefix-first LookaheadError check (all windows trailing).
detectors: A1_CREEP_QUIET: creep >= 1.5 and quiet and not_repriced (KOD-DET-v0 VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET tape facts, thresholds frozen 2026-10-08; the protocol's reference detector)
A2_CREEP2_QUIET: creep >= 2.0 and quiet and not_repriced
A3_CREEP_QUIET_HIVOL: A1 and hivol20 (the only known pre-event separator as a conditioning tercile; neutralised by the matched controls' volatility tercile so the matched test isolates the creep)
A4_RVOL_FLAT: volr >= 3 and |ret1| <= vol20 and not brk60 and not_repriced (a single-session volume-without-price day that is not a breakout)

B1_REBASE: there is a session s0 in [d-40, d-6] with ret1(s0) >= 0.30 (take the most recent); pre = level(s0-1); peak = max level over [s0, d-1]; level(d) <= pre + 0.5*(peak-pre) (at least half the spike-to-peak gain given back); min level over [d-4, d] >= pre (held above the pre-spike level for 5 sessions); quiet(d)
B2_REBASE_CREEP: B1 and creep >= 1.5
C1_CONTRACT: vol10 <= 0.5*vol60 and hivol60 and dd60 >= -0.5 and not_repriced (contraction in a historically volatile name that has not collapsed)
C2_CONTRACT_CREEP: C1 and creep >= 1.5
protocol.plans: Primary grid per detector: entry fixed with entry_lag 1 (IDX: next close, as E1/E3; US/CRYPTO: next open, as E2/E4) x exit fixed x holding_days {5, 10, 20} = 3 plans (24 (detector, plan) pairs per market, 72 harness runs in all; every run reported in <market>/discovery/plans.csv). Optional second exit stop_ref (sell at the first close in entry+1..entry+h-1 at or below the signal session's reference close) is included for every market only if the experiment runs on a tree that expresses close-referenced exits for open-entry markets (origin/claude/e4-fade-short-side generalises conditional rules; HEAD execution.py:365-366 restricts them to close entries, i.e. IDX); the protocol records at freeze which of 3 or 6 plans applies per market, before any number. holding_days 10 and 20 are new to the lab and are there because an accumulation signal need not resolve within 5 sessions; overlap 'skip' per name applies (backtest.py:302-316). No conditional entries (there is no move to confirm or pull back from). Reference row per market: A1_CREEP_QUIET|fixed1|fixed|h5, reported beside the grid as the population test of the KOD tape detector.
protocol.discovery_period: IDX 2021-01-22..2022-12-30 (TIER_1, panel-20261013T194245Z rebuilt from the pinned mirror commit, registry ca_registry-20261013T194256Z, as E3); US and CRYPTO 2020-07-01..2022-12-31 (US: panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z, causal-close-v2 with unit_factor, 4,878 names, read_through 2023-12-29; CRYPTO: panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z, 683 pairs incl. delisted). Per-year admissibility uses calendar years 2021, 2022 (IDX) and 2020 (from July), 2021, 2022 (US/CRYPTO).
protocol.validation_period: IDX 2023-01-02..2023-12-29; US and CRYPTO 2023-01-01..2023-12-31; one recorded harness run per market of the frozen pair (write_run -> results/runs, RUNS.jsonl) plus the detection evidence from e1.Study.evaluate on validation. Justification for re-using 2023: the outcomes seen on 2023 belong to return-triggered detectors (F1_ARA, G2_RET30, breakout) and their plans; no E5 member's flags have ever been computed on any panel, so 2023 is out-of-sample for this family; the only leakage is knowledge of the 2023 base rates and of big-day behaviour, declared in the protocol, and the protocol bans any E5 computation on 2023 before SELECTED is committed. The holdouts (IDX 2024-01-02..2025-02-21; US/CRYPTO 2024-01-01 on) are never loaded: the Study ends its market at the last validation session (e1.py:105-107) and every RunConfig sets end explicitly (on HEAD there is no GLOBAL_HOLDOUT code guard for US/CRYPTO; merging PR #7 first adds it). The prospective paper ledger is the forward arm if a pair validates (new POLICY_ID, not a change to PAPER-POLICY-v4).
protocol.admissibility: Discovery, per market, two gates both pre-registered. Detection gate per detector (E1 detector_table rule, e1.py:306-323, on the family module): flags >= 200 and E30 Wilson 95% lower bound > the period base rate; evaluate() also reports lift vs 200 matched random draws per flag and the one-sided p (floor 0.005), recall, median lead, r5_median vs matched. Trading gate per (detector, plan) (E3 rule, e3.py:99-115, applied verbatim): scored >= 200; average net return > 0 after fees/tiers; above the matched-random distribution with one-sided p < 0.05 (200 draws, floor 0.005); average net return > 0 in every discovery calendar year with >= 50 scored. Selection: among pairs whose detector passes the detection gate AND whose plan passes the trading gate, the highest average net return; ties by scored trades, then grid order (e3.select); at most one pair per market; none admissible = SELECTED stays None for that market and MOONSHOT_E5_<market>_D1 is never created. Freeze: the selected (detector, entry_rule, entry_window, exit_rule, holding_days) per market is written into moonshot_e5.SELECTED and committed (Rule.plan, rule hash covers it) before any validation number. Validation pass per market: scored >= 100, average net > 0, one-sided p < 0.05 vs matched random under the same plan (E3 validation rule) AND detection p_one_sided_vs_matched < 0.05 with lift > 1 on validation (what paper.decide's detection gate reads). Reported, not judged: hit rate, median net return, fill rate and status counts, same-session random baseline, per-price-band precision, flags on consecutive sessions per name, the share of FILL-C scored IDX trades exceeding 10% of entry-session volume (CORRECTION_01 diagnostic), US results under the unit_schedule quarantine as a sensitivity, horizon-20 repricing rate (E30 at t+1..t+20) if the Study horizon parameter is added. Search size is 8 detectors + 24 pairs per market and is stated in every output.
protocol.matched_controls: Trading stage: harness controls v2 (controls.py:71-74): for each attempted signal, 200 draws on the same session from evaluable names in the same price band, liquidity quintile (20-session median traded value), market-cap quintile (IDX mirror era only), volatility tercile, momentum tercile, drawdown tercile and listing-age bucket, relaxed from the last feature until >= 5 names, executed under the identical plan, fill model, costs and lot rules; plus the same-session uniform baseline; seed 20261007 (matched seed+1). Detection stage: E1's matched pool (price band, liquidity, market cap), 200 draws per flag, seed 20261008 (e1.py:215-227, 334-355). Because volatility, momentum and drawdown terciles are matched, the A3/C1 volatility conditions and the known 'volatile, drawn-down names reprice more' effect are removed from the comparison; a pass therefore attributes to the volume/path structure.
protocol.costs_model: Per-market harness profiles unchanged (profiles.py): IDX fee 0.15% buy / 0.25% sell, lot 100, notional Rp10,000,000, max_participation 0.10, fill model C (FILL-C-v1 decision-time capacity, registry-scaled; the CORRECTION_01 limitation that C never checks the entry session is reported as a diagnostic, not corrected here), ca_mode registry (rights issues and unresolved resets exclude the trade), ARA lock refuses entry; US: $5,000 notional, fee 0 / SEC fee, price-tier cost per side 1.5% (<$1), 0.5% ($1-5), 0.15% ($5-20), 0.05% (>$20) on the as-traded price, units as_traded, fill model B (FILL-B-v1 decision-time 20-session median volume), quarantine none (every name kept; repair_v3 showed the quarantine is outcome-correlated), ca_mode adjusted; CRYPTO: $5,000, 0.1% fee + 0.1% slippage per side, fill model A (ex-post 10% of entry-session volume, as E2/E4's recorded runs, labelled), ca_mode adjusted, UTC days. No price impact, no dividends, no carry on longs, daily bars only. Precondition stage re-runs the recorded reference runs on E5's panels (IDX 20261008T000401Z or FILL-C 20261009T050040Z; CRYPTO 20261008T005732Z; US 20261008T115656Z) and records REPRODUCED/DEVIATES as E3/E4 did.

code_changes: idxsig/rules/moonshot_e5.py (new rule module, same shape as moonshot_g.py): VERSION 'v1'; FEATURE_ARGS = ('close','prev','high','low','volume','present','tradeable','open') so e1.Study._signals and paper.scan_frame can call features(*args); features() returns the moonshot_g keys (ret1, rel1, ret5, ret20, volr, brk60, dd60, cpos, gap, hold, vol20) plus creep, rngr5, quiet, vol10, vol60, hivol20, hivol60, rebase_pre_ok/rebase_retrace_ok; family_flags(f) returns the 8 members; FAMILY = 8 (name, text) tuples; SELECTED = (('IDX', None), ('US', None), ('CRYPTO', None)) frozen later per market; rules() emits E5_CAND_<market>_<name> (hold 5, plan None) while unselected and MOONSHOT_E5_<market>_D1 with Rule.plan after the freeze (pattern: moonshot_e3.rules / moonshot_e4.selected_plan). Rebase member vectorised with trailing lags only: for k in 6..40, spike_k = lag(ret1 >= 0.30, k), pre_k = lag(level, k+1), peak_k = lag(rolling_max(level, k), 1); most recent k via masked argmax; min level over d-4..d via rolling min. Cross-sectional percentile uses np.nanpercentile over column d of evaluable names (as moonshot_e1's cross-sectional median). Module imports only numpy/pandas; all module-level values literals (rules/audit.py).

Only after a market validates (out of scope of the experiment itself): paper.py _detector() hook for moonshot_e5 plus a new POLICY_ID (PAPER-POLICY-v5, prospective date) and a validation_evidence path for research/E5/<market>/validation; no change to PAPER-POLICY-v4 records.
proposals.falsifier: Kill result, per market, any of: (1) on discovery no member reaches 200 flags with an E30 Wilson lower bound above the base rate (the family carries no +30% information beyond chance, including the KOD VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET definition); (2) on discovery no (detector, plan) in the 24-pair grid has average net return > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 against 200 matched random draws under the same plan AND positive average net in every discovery year with >= 50 scored (the structure detects but the flagged population's drift eats it, as with E1/E2); (3) the frozen pair's single 2023 validation run has scored < 100, average net <= 0, p >= 0.05 vs matched, or detection p >= 0.05 / lift <= 1. The exact result that kills the family outright: in all three markets the reference row A1_CREEP_QUIET|fixed1|fixed|h5 has average net return at or below the matched-random mean AND no pair is admissible on discovery; then pre-spike tape-only detection on daily bars is falsified for this lab across accumulation, re-base and contraction mechanisms, the KOD tape detector gets a negative population lift row, and the protocol's written consequence is that the next early-detection effort must use information inputs (filing acceptance times, catalyst calendars), not tape.
risks: Coverage: B1/B2 (a prior +30% day AND the re-base path) and C-members may produce fewer than 200 flags or 200 scored, especially on IDX (906 names) and crypto; reported in detector_selection.csv/plans.csv, never loosened after the fact.

Adverse population: the names most prone to +30% days have negative drift (US reverse-split/dilution names: 60% of E2 flags; IDX 'goreng' names with 0.55 untraded days in 20); a pre-spike flag may select them, giving E30 lift with negative average return ('detects but loses'); the per-year rule and matched controls make this visible rather than hiding it.

Repeat flags: creep and contraction persist for several sessions, so one name yields consecutive flags; overlap skip per name reduces scored trades at h10/h20 and detection precision counts ticker-days, so effective n is smaller than the flag count (reported).

Undefined features: IDX high/low missing on 12.5% of mirror rows and volume 0 on 12.5% make quiet/creep NaN (no flag) and bias coverage toward liquid names; crypto 24/7 sessions make rngr a UTC-day construct.

Multiplicity: 8 detectors and 24 pairs per market, 3 markets; p floor 0.005; mitigated by the per-year rule, the Wilson detection gate, one validation per market, and the full grid on record; a single market passing at p ~0.03 is weak evidence and the protocol says so.
2023 re-use: base-rate and big-day knowledge from E1/E2/E4 on 2023 is a declared leak; the pre-registration and the prospective paper arm are the mitigation, not a cure.

Fill models: IDX fill C can score infeasible entry-session fills (CORRECTION_01) and fill A/B are daily-bar proxies; a long hold (20) exits can roll over untraded/ARB-locked sessions; survivor-only US panel flatters longs.

Compute: 72 harness runs with 200 matched draws each, the US ones on a 4,878 x 1,006 panel, plus 24 Study.evaluate calls; the signal cache keyed by rule sha keeps signals to one computation per detector, but wall time is unmeasured (E3 ran 108 IDX runs; E4 288 crypto runs).

Expressibility on HEAD: stop_ref exits for US/crypto need PR #7's open-entry conditional machinery; on HEAD the grid is fixed-exit only for those markets; the choice must be fixed in protocol.json at freeze.

The hivol cross-sectional tercile depends on the listed universe at d; prefix-first checking guarantees causality but a US survivor universe shifts the tercile boundary relative to what was observable in real time.
proposals.directive_compliance: Holdout: the Study seals its market at the last validation session (e1.py:105-107) and every RunConfig sets end = 2023-12-29/31 explicitly; IDX runs touching 2024-01-02.. are refused by backtest.HOLDOUT; for US/crypto the protocol relies on explicit windows on HEAD and recommends merging PR #7 (clean merge-tree) first so GLOBAL_HOLDOUT refuses them in code; no holdout row is read, summarised or computed. No re-tune: no frozen detector (F1_ARA, G2_RET30, E3 candidates, E4 SELECTED) is touched or used as a candidate; the only prior-art definition reused (A1) was frozen 2026-10-08 for the Zealand card before any moonshot outcome was seen under it; all other thresholds are round numbers fixed in protocol.json before any flag is computed, and the admissibility/selection rules are copied from E1/E3 verbatim. No manufactured results: this proposal computes no statistic on any panel (no flag count, no return); every number will come from recorded harness runs (results/runs, RUNS.jsonl, write_run refusing a dirty tree) and Study outputs in append-only research/E5/<market>/ directories created with exist_ok=False; nothing historical is presented as prospective and the protocol's claims block says so. Pre-registration: protocol.json committed before the first run, sha256 stamped in reproduce/discovery/validation outputs; precondition reproduce stage first; SELECTED committed into the rule module before validation (hash covers the plan); one validation run per market; consequence_if_failed written in advance; the search size is visible in plans.csv and detector_selection.csv; read-only for this session (nothing created or run now).
proposals.expected_information_value: Either way the lab learns something it does not know: (1) the first population-level test of the KOD-DET-v0 tape detector VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET across ~1.4M eligible ticker-days in three markets, with base rate, precision, matched lift and non-events, which the KOD doctrine (lines 79-81) requires and which a single retrospective NO_SIGNAL card cannot give; (2) whether ANY pre-move tape structure on daily bars carries +30% information beyond the volatility/drawdown state, a question E1/E2's single-day weak signals at t-1 could not answer (they never measured multi-session creep, the quiet band, the re-base path or contraction); (3) a positive result in any market is the lab's first long detector whose entry precedes the move, with a validated executable plan that PAPER-POLICY-v5 could carry into the prospective ledger (today every paper decision is PASS because no (detector, plan) pair is validated); (4) a negative result in all three markets, written in advance as the consequence, closes the tape-only early-detection branch (accumulation, re-base, contraction) and justifies redirecting effort to information inputs with point-in-time timestamps (EDGAR acceptanceDateTime, Nasdaq Nordic releaseTime), which the data map identifies as the only unexplored dimension reachable for free; (5) the per-year and per-market tables show whether any effect is regime-bound (2021 hot years) as E3/E4 found, and the h5/h10/h20 comparison shows whether accumulation resolves on the 5-session horizon the whole lab has assumed.

proposals.title: E5-PATH: delayed-entry long after the fade. A pre-registered entry-timing x horizon grid on the frozen G2_RET30 flag (crypto primary, US secondary) with matched controls under each plan
proposals.angle: STRUCTURE/EXECUTION: keep the frozen detector, change only WHEN the long is entered (open of t+1, t+2, t+3, t+6, t+11) and HOW LONG it is held (5, 10, 20 sessions). The grid is simultaneously a tradeable-plan search and the first pre-registered post-flag return path map beyond t+5, measured against matched controls executed under the identical plan.
proposals.thesis: Every long-side statistic in the repo stops at t+5 and every long entry is at t+1: E2 found that buying the next open after a +30% day loses (US -3.65% vs -0.60%; crypto -1.90% vs +1.42% on 2023; median 5-session return about -10% vs 0% matched), and E3/E4 showed the fade is real and the right tail is fat. Nobody has measured what the flagged names do AFTER the fade. Hypothesis (mechanism): the +30% day carries information about further repricing (the flag's E30 lift of 5.4x/4.6x vs matched is validated detection), and the t+1..t+5 fade is a transient positioning unwind (chasers and day-traders exiting) rather than a reversal of the information; once the unwind completes, flagged names drift up relative to matched names, so a long entered at the open of t+3, t+6 or t+11 and held 5-20 sessions earns a positive net return that beats matched random entries under the same plan, in every discovery year. The rival mechanism (lottery/MAX-effect decay: names with extreme daily returns underperform for the following month; dilution and pump-and-dump structure in sub-$5 names) predicts every delayed cell is negative versus matched and the loss keeps compounding with horizon. The grid distinguishes the two with one frozen protocol: the lag-1 cells reproduce the known fade; the lag-6/lag-11 cells test whether the names stop losing once the unwind is over. On crypto the entry open is the prior close (median |open/prev-1| = 0.04% pre-2024), so the test is a clean close-to-close path; on US it includes the real opening gap.
proposals.why_not_already_falsified: E1/E2 traded only entry t+1 (close on IDX, open on US/crypto) and exit t+5; E2's detection statistics (r5, r5max, lead to peak) stop at t+5. E3 (IDX, 108 plans) varied the entry RULE inside s+1..s+3 with close entries and holds 2/3/5; it never delayed an unconditional entry beyond s+1 and never held beyond 5 (research/E3/protocol.json plans; e3.harness_config hard-codes entry_lag=1). E4 (crypto, 144+288 plans) was the SHORT side with holds 1/2/3/5; by symmetry its reference rows (E4/CRYPTO/discovery/plans.csv G2_RET30|fixed1|fixed|h1..h5: short +1.36%/+0.84%/-0.09%/-102% with 2021 negative and 2022 positive) imply the lag-1 LONG cells at h<=5, not any delayed entry or any horizon beyond t+5. US_BREAKOUT_v1 used a different signal (60-session breakout) with a 5% stop and a 5-session time exit. PR #5 (E3_US_RETENTION_v1, unrun) conditions on close(t+1) >= close(t) and enters at open t+2 hold 5 on US only; its unconditional arm B equals exactly one cell of this grid (US lag-2/h5) and its arm C is not in this grid. Signal family: unchanged (G2_RET30 copied verbatim, as E3 copied E1 and E4 copied E2). Information source: unchanged (price/volume only). What is new: the entry-timing axis (t+2..t+11) and the horizon axis (10 and 20 sessions), in both open-entry markets, with the harness's matched controls under each plan. Regime-conditioned longs were considered and rejected as the primary idea: the existing 2023 numbers already quasi-falsify a BTC-bull-gated long on crypto (E2 crypto 2023 unconditioned long -1.90% vs +1.42% matched while E4 v2's BEAR-regime shorts on the same flags were -1.50%, i.e. the bear-regime longs were roughly flat and the bull-regime longs carried the loss), and a regime chosen after seeing 2021-vs-2022 is the design pattern that failed in E4 v2.

protocol.family: G2_RET30 (MOONSHOT_E2 family, moonshot_g.py; the frozen selected detector for US and CRYPTO), long side only, code copied verbatim into idxsig/rules/moonshot_e5.py exactly as moonshot_e3.py copied moonshot_e1.py; no threshold, feature or regime change; candidate rule id E5_CAND_G2_RET30 (hold 5, no plan) for discovery, MOONSHOT_E5_D1 after the freeze
detectors: G2_RET30 (one detector; G1/G7/G10 and any _BEAR/_BULL variant deliberately excluded to keep the cell count at 15 per market)
protocol.plans: entries: fixed open entry at session s+k for k in {1,2,3,6,11} (protocol JSON entries [["fixed",1],["fixed",2],["fixed",3],["fixed",6],["fixed",11]], the existing E3 schema where the second element is the lag for a fixed entry, matching ExecConfig.plan and plan_text 'buy at ... session s + {w}'); exits: fixed only (close of entry+h, rolled forward while untraded, EXIT_DATA_END at the last traded close if the name leaves the data, INCOMPLETE if the target is beyond the window); holds h in {5,10,20}; 5 x 1 x 3 = 15 cells per market, 30 discovery runs plus 2 reproduce runs plus the US stress reruns of any admissible US cell plus at most 2 validation runs. The lag-1/h5 cell is the reference row (E2's plan; its 2023 outcome has been seen) and is NOT selectable. Conditional entries/exits (confirm, pullback, stop_ref, first_down) are excluded: E3 showed stops do not help the long side and conditional open entries exist only on the unmerged E4 branch.
markets: CRYPTO (primary): panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z (sha 3dc12749...), on disk; Binance spot USDT, 683 pairs incl. 190 delisted; entry at the UTC-day open (= prior close); notional $5,000; fees 0.1%+0.1% slippage per side plus the 0.1% tier (profile CRYPTO); fill model A (10% of entry-session volume, as E2/E4); ca_mode adjusted; overlap skip; data_end_exit last_close

US (secondary): panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z (sha 8d3b7ce4..., causal-close-v2, 4,878 names, read_through 2023-12-29), on disk; units 'panel' (split-adjusted returns are internally consistent across a trade window), quarantine 'none' (repair_v3 showed name quarantine is outcome-correlated), fill model A, notional $5,000, profile cost tiers per side (1.5% <$1, 0.5% $1-5, 0.15% $5-20, 0.05% above, plus SEC fee); STRESS RULE: a US cell is admissible only if it is still admissible when every trade is charged an additional flat 1.5% per side on top of its tier (the largest possible unit-induced tier error is 1.45% per side; 2020-22 units are unverified); survivor-only universe is a declared, uncorrected flattering bias for longs
protocol.discovery_period: 2020-07-01..2022-12-31 (E2's discovery window for G2_RET30; in-sample for the detector, as PR #5's addendum notes, which is why only PLANS are searched and the detector is never touched); per-year rule applies to 2020 (H2 only), 2021, 2022
protocol.validation_period: 2023-01-01..2023-12-31, one recorded harness run (results.write_run) per market of MOONSHOT_E5_D1 with the frozen cell; the harness slices the study market at `end` (backtest.run L275/L300) so no 2024 session is ever loaded; pass if scored >= 100, avg net > 0, one-sided p < 0.05 vs matched random (E3's validation rule). Declared caveat: the lag-1/h5 outcomes on 2023 are already known from E2 (both markets) and US 2023 has been replayed many times (PR #5 calls it 'spent'); a US pass is therefore one-year evidence on previously replayed data and a crypto pass is one-year evidence on a year whose lag-1/h5 outcome was seen. Consequence of a pass: a new paper policy version may score the validated delayed plan prospectively from decisions the ledger already records (no new scans needed, no real orders); consequence of a fail: the unconditional long plan family for G2_RET30 is exhausted at every entry timing to t+11 and every horizon to t+31 in that market.
protocol.admissibility: On discovery, per market, per cell (E3's rule verbatim plus two additions): scored >= 200; average net return > 0; one-sided p < 0.05 vs matched random (200 draws, seed 20261007/+1, floor 0.005); average net return > 0 in every discovery calendar year with >= 50 scored trades (by signal year, as backtest.by_year keys it); [new] US only: still admissible under the +1.5%/side stress costs; [new] the lag-1/h5 reference cell is excluded from selection. Selection: the admissible cell with the highest average net return, ties by more scored then grid order; at most one cell per market; frozen into moonshot_e5.SELECTED (per-market tuple like moonshot_g.SELECTED) and committed before any validation statistic. Precondition stage (as E3/E4): re-run the recorded E2 trading runs on the chosen panels with their recorded configs and record REPRODUCED/DEVIATES before any grid number: CRYPTO 20261008T005732Z_MOONSHOT_E2_CRYPTO_D1_v1 (same panel sha 3dc12749, expected exact), US 20261008T100745Z_MOONSHOT_E2_US_D1_v1 (R1c: panel 8d3b7ce4, units panel, quarantine none, fill A, 1,101 scored, -3.745% vs -0.624%). Descriptive, non-decision outputs frozen in the same protocol: (a) path.csv per market: mean and median of open(t+1)->close(t+j) for j = 1..21 over the attempted lag-1/h20 signals and over the deterministic matched-control tickers (controls.matched_draws re-derived with the same seed), before costs, split by discovery year; (b) an equal-notional ledger of all scored trades of each cell aggregated by exit session (cumulative P&L, max drawdown) for the rule and for the pooled matched draws, labelled descriptive. Multiplicity note recorded in the protocol: 14 selectable cells per market, highly correlated (same flags); the per-year positivity rule and the single validation are the guards, as in E3/E4.
protocol.matched_controls: Harness controls v2 exactly as every recorded run computes them: for each attempted signal, 200 names drawn on the same session from names where the rule was evaluable, matched on price_band, liquidity quintile, volatility tercile, momentum tercile, drawdown tercile and listing_age at the signal session (market_cap only where listed_shares exist; relaxed from the last feature until >= 5 names match), executed under the identical ExecConfig including the entry lag and hold (backtest.run L333-344 passes exec_cfg to _baseline; overlap-skip at L304 uses s + entry_lag). Same-session uniform baseline recorded as secondary. One-sided p = (1 + #draws with mean >= observed)/201.
protocol.costs_model: CRYPTO: 0.1% fee + 0.1% slippage per side plus the profile's 0.1% tier; no carry on longs; liquidation/jump_ratio not applicable (long, 1x, no leverage); redenomination jumps are the same risk E2 accepted (LUNA/NFP spike rows already dropped by the panel). US: SEC fee on sale + price-tier cost per side from the adjusted price, plus the pre-registered +1.5%/side stress rerun as an admissibility condition. Both: fixed notional $5,000, whole units, fill model A (10% of entry-session volume, labelled ex-post as in E2/E4), no price impact, no dividends, daily bars only (no intraday path; irrelevant here because the plan has no stop).

data_needed: idx-signals/data/panel/panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z.csv.gz (on disk, manifest committed, sha 3dc12749...); the run passes end=2022-12-31 / 2023-12-31 explicitly so the 2024+ rows in the file are never sliced into the study market
idx-signals/data/panel/panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z.csv.gz (on disk, manifest committed, sha 8d3b7ce4..., read_through 2023-12-29)

No network pulls, no new panels, no registry; no holdout rows read at any stage
code_changes: idxsig/backtest.py resolve_plan (L87-92) and run (L231-250): carry the entry lag of a fixed plan into ExecConfig.entry_lag (for entry_rule == 'fixed', entry_lag = the plan's entry_window; explicit RunConfig.entry_window/--entry-lag take precedence; default stays 1 so every recorded run reproduces unchanged). ExecConfig.plan (execution.py L127-130) and ENTRY_TEXT['fixed'] already encode the lag as entry_window, so plan ids ('G2_RET30|fixed6|fixed|h10') and plan_text need no change. Add tests in tests/test_plans.py: a ('fixed', 3) plan on an open-entry market enters at the open of s+3, the matched baseline shares the lag, overlap-skip uses s+3, reproduce-equivalence of a lag-1 run.

idxsig/rules/moonshot_e5.py: verbatim copy of moonshot_g.py's features/family_flags/FAMILY (the module may import nothing from the package; passes rules/audit.py), RULE_ID 'MOONSHOT_E5_D1', VERSION 'v1', CANDIDATES = ('G2_RET30',), SELECTED = None until the freeze then a per-market mapping {'CRYPTO': ('G2_RET30','fixed',k,'fixed',h), 'US': (...)} (pattern: moonshot_g.SELECTED per market + moonshot_e3.selected_plan), selected_plan() -> {'entry_rule':'fixed','entry_window':k,'exit_rule':'fixed'}, rules() emitting E5_CAND_G2_RET30 (hold 5, no plan) and MOONSHOT_E5_D1 (hold h, plan) with 'Selected: ...; plan: ...' in the rule text so the rule hash covers the plan; register the module in idxsig/rules/__init__.py registry() tuple (L61-64).

idxsig/e5.py modelled on e4.py (which already generalises e3.py to markets): protocol() reading research/E5/protocol.json with sha256 stamped into every stage output; plan_grid via e3.plan_grid (entries list carries the lag); harness_config(proto, market, rule_id, period, plan) building RunConfig with entry_lag = plan['entry_window'] for fixed entries, market-specific notional/fees/units/quarantine from the protocol; run_reproduce (the two E2 runs named in protocol['precondition'], REPRODUCED/DEVIATES as e3.run_reproduce); run_discovery (15 cells per market through backtest.run with the signal cache; plans.csv, reference_summary.json for lag-1/h5, summary.json with admissible flags, selected_tuple and freeze instruction; US stress reruns of admissible cells via RunConfig fee_buy/fee_sell += 0.015 recorded as plans_stress.csv); admissibility = e3.admissibility + stress condition + reference-cell exclusion; select = e3.select over selectable rows; run_validation requiring moonshot_e5.SELECTED[market] == discovery selected_tuple, one write_run-recorded run on the validation period, result.json with passed and consequence (e3.run_validation pattern).
