idxsig/cli.py: subcommands e5-reproduce / e5-discovery [--accept-deviation] / e5-validation --market CRYPTO|US, refusing a dirty idxsig/ tree exactly like e3-*/e4-* (cli.py L326/L345/L379 pattern); for US/CRYPTO the driver sets start/end from protocol.json periods (never the panel's source_boundary), and if PR #7 is merged first the GLOBAL_HOLDOUT guard (e4 branch backtest.py L85, L296-300) refuses any mistake in code.

research/E5/protocol.json + PROTOCOL.md (frozen, committed, sha recorded before any statistic; research/ is append-only under tools/check_append_only.py); tests/test_e5.py: grid has 15 cells per market, lag mapping, admissibility including the stress and reference-cell rules, selection excludes lag-1/h5, validation refuses when SELECTED mismatches.

Out of scope until a validation passes (and then a new POLICY_ID): a paper-score-v4 scorer for a delayed plan reading the DECISION records already in paper/ledger.jsonl (entry at the open of session+k, exit at close+h), so prospective evidence accrues without new scans.
proposals.falsifier: Discovery: in BOTH markets, no selectable cell (any lag in {2,3,6,11} with any hold, or lag 1 with hold 10/20) is admissible, i.e. none has scored >= 200, avg net > 0, p < 0.05 vs matched random under the same plan, avg net > 0 in each discovery year with >= 50 scored (and, for US, survives +1.5%/side). That result kills the hypothesis that the fade is a transient unwind around retained information: the flagged names keep losing versus matched names at every entry timing to t+11 and every horizon to t+31, which is the lottery/MAX-decay mechanism, and the unconditional long plan family for G2_RET30 is closed. Validation: if a cell is selected and the single 2023 run of MOONSHOT_E5_D1 shows scored < 100, or avg net <= 0, or p >= 0.05 vs matched, the family is exhausted for that market (E3/E4's consequence_if_failed), with no second design pass on 2023. A specific pre-stated pattern that would also count as falsified even with a stray admissible cell: the path map showing mean rule-minus-matched still declining from j=6 to j=21 in every discovery year (persistent decay) while the admissible cell's edge is confined to 2021.
risks: Prior is against the hypothesis: the academic MAX/lottery effect and E2's lag-1 losses both predict negative delayed cells; the experiment is more likely to close the long side than to open it (that is still decisive information, see expected_information_value).

Contamination declared: the lag-1/h5 cell's 2023 outcomes were seen in E2 (both markets) and E4 v2 saw 2023 crypto short outcomes; the delayed cells are correlated with them through the same flags. Mitigation: the reference cell is excluded from selection, the protocol is frozen before any delayed number exists, selection is on discovery only; US 2023 is 'spent' per PR #5's addendum, so a US pass is weaker than a crypto pass and the clean confirmation is prospective scoring from the ledger.

Multiplicity: 14 selectable cells per market; E3's p < 0.05 is kept for comparability; the per-year rule and the single validation are the guards; the orchestrator may prefer p < 0.01 on discovery (pre-register either, not both).

Sample attrition at long horizons: hold-20 cells lose the last ~31 sessions of each period to INCOMPLETE and overlap-skip removes consecutive-day re-flags of the same name; crypto 2023 (298 flags) may fall below 100 scored at h20, which is a fail 'for the right reason' (E4 v2 regime_note pattern), not a reason to relax.

US data: 2020-22 split units unverified (cost tiers may be mis-stated by up to 1.45%/side, hence the stress rule); survivor-only universe flatters longs by an unknown amount; opening gaps are real on US (36% of days > 1%) so US lag-k entries pay a gap the crypto cells do not.

Crypto data: 49 pre-2024 pairs stop trading > 20 sessions before 2023-12-31 (EXIT_DATA_END at the last traded close, as E2 accepted); pairs Binance dropped from exchangeInfo entirely are absent; redenomination-style prints are handled by the panel's spike drops only (no jump_ratio on the long side).

Harness plumbing: resolve_plan must carry the lag without changing any recorded run's reproduction; the precondition reproduce stage catches a regression before any grid number (E3's DEVIATES precedent shows the harness records, not hides, such drift).

Per-trade averages with fixed notional: a positive cell could rest on a few large winners (fat right tail); the descriptive equal-notional ledger and max drawdown are reported but are not decision criteria, so a pass remains 'one year under assumed costs and daily-bar fills' and never prospective performance.
proposals.directive_compliance: Holdout: never read; both panels contain 2024+ rows but backtest.run slices the study market at the protocol's end (2022-12-31 / 2023-12-31; backtest.py L275/L300), the driver takes start/end from protocol.json periods (never source_boundary), and merging PR #7 first adds the GLOBAL_HOLDOUT code guard for US/CRYPTO. No re-tune: G2_RET30's code is copied verbatim (the E3/E4 method); nothing in the rule, its threshold, features or regime changes; only the execution plan (entry lag, hold) is searched, on discovery only, and the one cell whose 2023 outcome is known (lag-1/h5) is barred from selection. No manufactured results: this proposal states no expected return; the cells' values are unknown until run; the precondition reproduce stage must pass or be recorded as DEVIATES before any grid number; every stage output carries the protocol sha, panel sha and rule sha (e3/e4 _stamp pattern); results are written by write_run into append-only, hash-verified directories. Pre-registration: research/E5/protocol.json and PROTOCOL.md are committed before any statistic (run refuses a dirty tree; research/ frozen by tools/check_append_only.py); admissibility, selection, the reference-cell exclusion, the US stress rule, the validation pass rule and both consequences are fixed in the JSON; the descriptive path map and ledger are declared non-decision in advance. No real orders, no ASTRA/production change; a pass can only create a new paper policy version that scores the plan prospectively from ledger decisions. This session was read-only: no file was created or modified and no harness run or network pull was started.
proposals.expected_information_value: Either way the repo gains its first pre-registered, matched-controlled post-flag return path beyond t+5 (15 windows per market spanning t+1..t+31, by year, under a frozen protocol), which pins the mechanism the repo currently labels 'plausible, not demonstrated': if the lag-6/lag-11 cells sit at or above matched while lag-1 cells are negative, the fade is a transient unwind of an informational move and a delayed long is a candidate plan with a clear prospective scoring path from the existing ledger decisions; if every delayed cell stays below matched and the gap widens with horizon, the flagged population decays persistently (lottery/MAX structure), the long side of G2_RET30 is closed at every entry timing and horizon (not just t+1/t+5), PR #5's retention arm inherits a strong negative prior (its arm B is a cell here), and the remaining structural question moves to the horizon of the short side, which E4 never tested beyond 5 sessions and which would be a new protocol. The grid also measures, for the first time, how much of the known 5-session loss is the t+1 open gap (US lag-1 vs crypto lag-1, where the open is the prior close) versus later drift, and gives the descriptive aggregate P&L/drawdown shape of equal-notional ledgers versus pooled matched draws that the 'portfolio-level' question needs before anyone builds a capital-constrained control arm.

proposals.title: KPF-v1: daily tape-fed prospective KOD pipeline (whole-universe scan + STRICT signal/control cases) in IDX, US and crypto
proposals.angle: KOD PROSPECTIVE PIPELINE: open and close AUTHORITATIVE prospective KOD cases every day from the bars the paper-scan routines already pull, with T-24H discipline, KOD-EVIDENCE-v2 objects, RFC 3161 anchoring, GitHub receipts and mechanical outcome scoring; no trades, no backtest.
proposals.thesis: Two claims, one infrastructure. Scientific claim (the only KOD-DET-v0 detector whose inputs are tape-derivable): VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET, evaluated at T-24H with the ZEALAND_PILOT_v1 fact definitions frozen 2026-10-08 (median volume of the last 5 sessions / median of the 20 before >= 1.5; median range ratio over 5 sessions <= 1.0 and |ret5| <= 2 x vol20 x sqrt(5)), precedes a >= +30% close-to-close repricing within the next 5 sessions more often than the base rate of the same universe. The mechanism that would make it true is informed accumulation ahead of an undisclosed catalyst (the H-B observation in kod-machine/research/ZEALAND_PILOT_v1/05_findings/FINDINGS.md, recorded as untested). Infrastructure claim: the full STRICT-v3 chain (evidence stamped before the cutoff, card opened within the hour, anchor pushed, GitHub push-run receipt dated before the window) can run unattended once per market per session, so that the doctrine's floor of 30 closed prospective cases is reached in about two weeks of operation instead of never, and the KOD scan log supplies the prospective base rate and the non-events that doctrine lines 79-81 require. Each case asks one pre-registered question: given the T-24H tape facts for SYMBOL (through session d-1) and no document facts (UNKNOWN), will the close reprice by >= +30% (REPRICED_UP) or <= -30% (REPRICED_DOWN) relative to the close of session d within sessions d+1..d+5?
proposals.why_not_already_falsified: Signal family: E1/E2 measured a single-day volume surge (volr = volume / prior-20-session median, matched-set AUC 0.50-0.52) and 20-session volatility (0.68/0.78/0.56); neither measured the KOD conjunction (5-vs-20 median volume creep AND range quiet relative to the name's own median AND |ret5| inside 2 sigma), and E1/E2's prior is if anything against it (quiet names reprice less), so the result is informative either way. Information source and structure: every existing experiment is a backtest on consumed discovery/validation windows; this is prospective, on 2026 live sessions that are not holdout, with a whole-universe scan base rate (never measured prospectively for any market) and matched control cases, which no backtest in the repo can produce for a KOD detector because KOD facts are not RuleView fields. The paper ledger tests the opposite population (post-spike G2_RET30/F1_ARA continuation, 1 scored outcome so far); E3/E4 test execution plans on those same post-spike detectors; the breakout baseline is a 60-session closing-high rule. KOD's own record is 0 prospective cases, 0 scans, 0 GitHub receipts (kod-machine/var/kod.db: cases 4, scan_runs 0, remote_timestamp_receipts 0), so nothing about KOD-DET-v0 has been tested or falsified, and the chain itself has only run with tests/support.py FakeTimestamper and FakeGitHub.

protocol.family: KPF-v1 (KOD prospective feed). Scanner id KPF-TAPE-v1 per market, logged with `kod scan`; cases KOD-CARD-v3 STRICT-v3 opened with `kod open`; detectors KOD-DET-v0 unchanged (kod-machine/kod/detectors.py, sha256 0a0e0a73...; require_detector_unchanged refuses otherwise); fact definitions copied verbatim from kod-machine/research/ZEALAND_PILOT_v1/01_protocol/protocol.json fact_definitions and 03_card/price_facts.py measures(); protocol frozen as kod-machine/research/KPF_v1/{PROTOCOL.md,protocol.json,FREEZE.json} with RFC 3161 tokens (the ZEALAND 01_protocol pattern) before the first evidence object, protocol sha written into every scan's notes and every card's story_hypothesis (hashed).
detectors: VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET: the tested detector; inputs volume_creep_before_story and price_quiet_vs_own_range computed at the last session at or before the T-24H cutoff (session d-1) from the stamped snapshot chain
COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE: evaluated; SIGNAL by construction (reconstruction_status PARTIAL_PUBLIC: vendor daily bars only, no filings/news/order book)

DATED_CATALYST_KNOWN, PRIMARY_DOC_BEFORE_PRICE, NARRATIVE_WITHOUT_MECHANISM: INSUFFICIENT_DATA by construction in v1 (document facts dated_catalyst_known, primary_document_public, narrative_only, mechanism_in_primary_docs are null = UNKNOWN; price_already_repriced is computed and cited but its partner fact is null). Populating them needs a v1.1 document feed (EDGAR acceptance times from Archives headers for the US cohort) under a new scanner id, not a KOD-DET edit
FLAG:KPF-TAPE-v1 (the scanner flag row): VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET SIGNAL at T-24H AND price_already_repriced false; hit_label REPRICED_UP
protocol.plans: No trade plan: KOD claims no fill, no MFE/MAE as profit (doctrine lines 74-77). Outcome plan, pre-registered in protocol.json and in each card: reference price = close(d), the last close before the decision cutoff; REPRICED_UP iff max close over sessions d+1..d+5 >= 1.30 x close(d); REPRICED_DOWN iff min close over d+1..d+5 <= 0.70 x close(d); if both, the one crossed first by session order; otherwise NO_REPRICE; CENSORED if fewer than 5 post-d sessions of bars exist 10 sessions after d (delisting, halt, untraded); UNKNOWN if units cannot be established (US: any provider split record effective after d that is not SEC-VERIFIED under us-actions-v2, exactly paper-score-v3's UNSCORABLE rule; any market: a close/previous ratio > 10 or < 0.1 inside the window; the snapshot close(d) not reconciling with the scoring bars within rtol 1e-3). window_return_pct = close(d+5)/close(d) - 1 (descriptive only). Timing per market (all UTC; decision_cutoff must be within 1 hour of the open and the window must start after both, ledger.py:195-217): US paper scan 22:53Z -> snapshot evidence as_of 23:30:00Z d -> scan and cards decision_cutoff 23:30:00Z d, T-24H 23:30Z d-1, T-72H 23:30Z d-3, T-30D 23:30Z d-30, window start 00:00:00Z d+1, end 00:00Z of the calendar day after the fifth weekday after d; IDX paper scan 10:26Z -> as_of/cutoff 11:00:00Z d, window start 12:00Z d; CRYPTO paper scan 00:25Z d+1 (UTC day d) -> as_of/cutoff 01:00:00Z d+1, T-24H 01:00Z d (last complete kline = day d-1), window start 02:00Z d+1, end 01:00Z d+6. A late routine (stamp after the slot) logs the scan but opens no cases that day (pre-registered skip, never a shifted cutoff). Case selection, deterministic and outcome-blind: per market per session K=2 signal cases = flagged entries ranked by sha256(scan_id + '|' + symbol), plus K=2 matched controls (below); disposition WATCH for all (templated critic note: loss path = base-rate NO_REPRICE or a down repricing; missing evidence = every document fact; invalidation = the pre-registered outcome rule); story_hypothesis carries the question text, the numeric features at T-24H, the control/signal role and the protocol sha.
markets: CRYPTO: universe = every name the paper scan marks eligible on the Binance USDT spot panel (about 480/day); 2022 discovery-session sizing count: 7.4 flags/day of 314 evaluable (2.4%), VOLUME_CREEP SIGNAL 2.7%

IDX: universe = every eligible name of the IDX paper scan (about 830/day); sizing count on 2022: 31 flags/day of 602 evaluable (5.2%), SIGNAL 5.5%; names without high/low are INSUFFICIENT_DATA and never selected

protocol.discovery_period: None. No historical outcome is read or computed. The only historical numbers are flag COUNTS per day on 2022 discovery sessions (US repair panel, crypto panel, IDX panel rows dated 2021-10-01..2022-12-31 for warm-up), taken to size the pipeline; they are not an outcome statistic and selected nothing.
protocol.validation_period: Prospective only: from launch (target 2026-10-27 after a SIMULATED dress rehearsal) for 60 sessions per market (pre-registered readout at the first `kod report` after 60 AUTHORITATIVE closed scans: about 2026-12-26 crypto, 2027-01-26 US/IDX). The sealed holdouts (IDX 2024-01-02..2025-02-21; US/crypto 2024 onward) are never loaded; 2026 live bars are not holdout under research/E2/protocol.json's wording but the proposal reads nothing before launch day except the 60-session history object H0 built from the routines' own recent pulls (data/raw/*_recent, 200 days), which does not touch 2024-2025 rows because the pulls start 2026-03-28 or later.
protocol.admissibility: Acceptance criteria (infrastructure, evaluated at launch + 20 trading days): A1 >= 30 AUTHORITATIVE closed prospective cases with a scored label (not UNKNOWN/CENSORED) in kod report (score.py PROMOTION_MIN = 30; AUTHORITATIVE per verify.py:96-133 = STRICT card, anchor commit ancestor of HEAD, GitHub push run created before outcome_window.start); A2 every KPF scan AUTHORITATIVE and closed within 3 sessions of its window end (scan_overdue_unclosed = 0); A3 `kod verify` ok and CI green (tools/check_append_only.py --all) throughout; A4 share of UNKNOWN outcomes <= 20% per market. Pre-registered scientific readout R1 per market at 60 closed scans, on the scan lift table for VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET with REPRICED_UP: s = signal hit rate (n_s expected about 440 crypto, 1,700 US-cohort, 1,860 IDX), b = no-signal hit rate; SUPPORTED iff the Wilson 95% lower bound of s > b (lift > 1 established); FALSIFIED iff the Wilson 95% upper bound of s < 2b (minimal interesting lift 2 excluded); otherwise INCONCLUSIVE and the feed continues another 60 sessions without any change. The case detector_table (signal vs matched-control cases) is reported alongside and is never the decision statistic at n = 30. Promotion is out of scope: doctrine line 65 requires complete coverage and v1 cases are PARTIAL_PUBLIC; a SUPPORTED readout can only motivate KOD-DET-v1 with a new cohort.
protocol.matched_controls: Two layers. (1) Scan base rate: every universe name is a scan entry with the same T-24H facts and the same outcome rule, so each detector and the FLAG row get both sides and a lift (score.py lift_table). (2) Control cases: for each signal case, one NO_SIGNAL case (VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET NO_SIGNAL with both facts non-null, price_already_repriced false) drawn by the same hash rank from the same session's universe in the same price band (profile band edges: IDX 200/5,000; US 1/5/20; CRYPTO 0.01/1/100, from idxsig/profiles.py) and the same liquidity quintile (adv20_value from the paper features file, quintiles within the day's universe); relaxed to band only, then to any, with the relaxation written into the story. Controls are opened as STRICT cards under the identical outcome plan.
protocol.costs_model: None. KOD records no entry, fill, cost or profit; window_return_pct is a descriptive close-to-close number. Execution feasibility of anything found is a separate idxsig protocol (EXEC-US-v2.1 / E3-style plan grid) with its own matched random baseline.

proposals.falsifier: Infrastructure falsifier: 20 trading days after launch, kod report shows fewer than 30 AUTHORITATIVE closed prospective cases with a scored label, or any KPF scan that is not AUTHORITATIVE, or kod verify not ok. That kills the claim that the STRICT chain can be run unattended at this cadence, and the causes (TSA refusals, pushes landing after window start, UNKNOWN units) are visible in the excluded_prospective table. Scientific falsifier (pre-registered R1): at 60 AUTHORITATIVE closed scans in a market, the Wilson 95% upper bound of VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET's signal hit rate for REPRICED_UP is below 2 x the no-signal hit rate of the same market; if that holds in all three markets, the tape half of the KOD hypothesis is dead at KOD-DET-v0 thresholds and no threshold is touched on these outcomes (a new threshold set is KOD-DET-v1 with a new cohort). Expected n at 60 sessions: about 440 signal entries crypto (base about 2.4%), 1,700 US-cohort (about 1.3%), 1,860 IDX (about 1.2%), which excludes lift 2 when the observed signal rate equals the base rate.
risks: Storage: each scan entry is about 1.5 KB of registry JSON plus 6 rows in the committed var/kod.db; at 480+830+1,100 entries/day the database grows roughly 3-4 MB/day (about 200 MB over the 60-session pilot, more if git deltas are poor); the US cohort cap and gzip scan bodies bound it, but the full US universe (5,600/day) is not affordable in this ledger design

Timestamp authorities: both freetsa and sectigo down at the slot refuses every open that day (anchor.py:135-137); 40 stamps/day may hit unknown rate limits; a missed slot means no cases (never a shifted cutoff)

Receipts: the anchor push must reach GitHub before outcome_window.start (30-60 minutes after the cutoff); a failed or delayed push makes the case REMOTE_TIMESTAMP_LATE/UNVERIFIED and it is excluded; GitHub Actions run records expire after about 410 days, so reports must be taken before then

The 24-hour staleness built into KOD loses one session between the last fact (d-1) and the first outcome session (d+1); E2 found a median lead of 1 session to peak in the US, so one-session-lead events are structurally invisible to this design

Units and data: US survivor-only universe (new listings enter the cohort by hash; delisted names vanish, CENSORED); Yahoo bars revised after the snapshot make reconcile failures (UNKNOWN); IDX names without high/low are never evaluable; holidays are unmodelled so closes wait for bars

Multiplicity: three markets and two lift rows (FLAG and detector) are read at R1; the readout rule is per market and pre-registered, but a single-market SUPPORTED result is weak evidence and must not be sold as validation
Operational: the routine host needs a GitHub token with actions:read and SEC egress; the repo has no scheduler, so the wiring lives outside the repository and its failure modes are invisible to CI
The scan FLAG row and the VOLUME_CREEP detector row overlap by construction (FLAG adds only price_already_repriced false); readers must not count them as two findings
proposals.directive_compliance: Holdout: never loaded; the feed runs on 2026 live sessions from launch day forward, the history object H0 comes from the routines' 2026 recent pulls, and the only historical computation in this proposal was a flag count on 2022 discovery rows with no outcome read (IDX 2024-01-02..2025-02-21 and US/crypto 2024-2025 rows untouched). No re-tune: KOD-DET-v0 code (sha 0a0e0a73..., bound in detector_versions and enforced by require_detector_unchanged) and the ZEALAND fact definitions frozen 2026-10-08 are reused verbatim; the cohort hash, K, matching rule, outcome thresholds and the readout rule are fixed in protocol.json before the first evidence object; a SUPPORTED or FALSIFIED readout changes nothing in detectors.py, and any new threshold is KOD-DET-v1 on a new cohort. No manufactured results: this proposal reports counts, not probabilities; the only expected numbers are sample sizes and base rates quoted from E1/E2 validation as historical reference, and the prior from E1/E2 (volume surge AUC 0.50) is stated as unfavourable. Pre-registration: protocol frozen and RFC 3161-stamped (ZEALAND FREEZE.json pattern) before any scan or card; every card is hashed, anchored, stamped and pushed before its window; outcomes are appended only after window end with the card_sha from the open; registry and research directories are append-only under tools/check_append_only.py; no real orders, no ASTRA or paper-policy change, no edit to idxsig/paper.py.
proposals.expected_information_value: Either way the lab gets its first AUTHORITATIVE prospective records: a proven end-to-end STRICT chain (or a documented list of where it breaks), prospective per-market base rates for +30%/5-session repricings on the full eligible universe (never measured outside backtests), and the first both-sides hit-rate table for a KOD-DET-v0 detector. If R1 is FALSIFIED in all three markets, the quiet-volume-creep hypothesis is closed at these thresholds and KOD's remaining detectors are known to require a document feed (EDGAR acceptance times) rather than more tape work. If R1 is SUPPORTED in any market, it is the first pre-event separator found prospectively in the project (E1/E2 found only prior volatility, on seen data), which would justify a KOD-DET-v1 cohort and, separately, an idxsig execution-plan protocol with matched random baselines on the same flags. The infrastructure outlives the hypothesis: the same snapshot-evidence, scan, card and close steps carry any future scanner id (document-fed or tape-fed) at a marginal cost of one routine step per market. Timeline estimate: build 48 hours over about 8 working days from 2026-10-15, protocol freeze 2026-10-24, SIMULATED rehearsal 2026-10-26, first real opens 2026-10-27, 12 cases/day across markets so 30 cases are open by the third session; windows end 5 sessions after each signal day and closes run on the next routine, so 30 AUTHORITATIVE closed cases are expected by about 2026-11-06 (crypto) and 2026-11-09 (IDX/US), conditional on TSA, push and receipts succeeding; the 60-session readout R1 falls around 2026-12-26 (crypto) and 2027-01-26 (IDX/US).

proposals.title: E5-CEILING (KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v1): pre-registered T-0 predictability ceiling for the +30%/5-session event from daily bars, with a directional (up-minus-down) ranker as the kill test
proposals.thesis: Null (what I expect): there is no long edge in daily-bar public-price signals after costs because the +30%-in-5-sessions event is a variance event in a fat-tailed cross-section, not a directional one. Daily-bar features can identify names whose variance is about to be high (the only pre-event separator ever found is 20-session volatility, matched-set AUC 0.68 IDX / 0.78 US / 0.56 crypto, E1/E2 REPORTs), but variance is symmetric and high-variance names carry flat-to-negative drift, so every detector built from bars inherits a non-directional lift: P(+30%) rises together with P(-23%) and the mean 5-session return stays at or below matched controls. The recorded evidence is consistent with this and not with a cost story: in every recorded trading run the GROSS mean is already negative (IDX 20261008T000401Z gross -3.67% vs net -4.06%; crypto 005732Z gross -1.51% vs net -1.90%; US 060443Z gross -3.19% vs net -3.65%; US 115656Z fill B gross -0.10% vs net -0.97%), i.e. the cost drag is 0.4-0.9pp of a 1-4pp loss. The decisive and cheapest test is therefore not another plan search but a ceiling: give a frozen, pre-registered learner the entire daily-bar information set (the E1/E2 weak-signal lists already pre-registered as E1-SIGNALS-v1 / E2-SIGNALS-v1), fit it once on discovery over the whole evaluable universe (not conditioned on any frozen detector), freeze the coefficients as literals in a rule module, and trade its top 0.5% of ticker-days under the original harness plan against matched controls. Arm A (E30 ranker) tests the detection-to-profit link the program assumed; Arm B (directional ranker: logit P(up 30%) minus logit P(down 23%)) tests whether ANY daily-bar feature combination at T-0 carries tradeable direction. The mechanism that would make the thesis true is that some combination of features (e.g. quiet price with creeping volume, drawdown plus rising range, breakout in a low-vol name) separates the coming up-moves from the coming down-moves; the mechanism that would make the null true is that every such combination predicts both tails equally.
proposals.why_not_already_falsified: (1) Signal family: E1 (F1..F10) and E2 (G1..G11) are hand-written one- or two-threshold rules; all admissible members are inside-the-move by construction (ret1>=30%, ARA lock, 5-session +30%). No experiment ever combined features, ranked the cross-section, or used the one pre-event separator (vol20) as an input (G11_HIGHVOL_ACTIVE was admissible in E2, US 9.7x, and never selected or traded). (2) Information source: the weak-signal AUCs (E1/discovery/signal_stats.csv, E2 REPORT.md line 38) were univariate, discovery-only, and computed against controls matched on price_band/liquidity/market_cap only (idxsig/e1.py Study._pool, keys line 220), never turned into a detector. (3) Structure: E3 (108 plans) and E4 (144+288 short plans) searched execution, not information; US_BREAKOUT_v1 is a single feature; E3_US_RETENTION_v1 is a one-feature filter on G2 flags. None measured the DOWN-event rate of any detector's flags, so 'variance detector vs direction detector' is untested. (4) The gross-vs-net decomposition above (from recorded trades.csv.gz gross_return/net_return columns) shows the failures are gross, so repair_v3's cost-bound rerun and further fill-model work cannot change signs; the remaining degree of freedom is the information set, which E5 exhausts for daily bars. (5) The oracle/break-even bound has never been written down: E1 validation gives capturable_median 0.0% for F1_ARA flags, but no run has computed E[net | E30] and E[net | not E30] under the plan to state the precision a detector would need to break even against matched controls.

protocol.family: MOONSHOT_E5 (idxsig/rules/moonshot_e5.py, new): per market two pre-registered logistic rankers over the full evaluable universe. Features (all from the 12 RULE_FIELDS, causal, per-session cross-sectional percentile ranks plus their squares; NaN rank -> 0.5): ret1, rel1, ret5, ret20, volr, valr, rngr, cpos, vol20, dd60, up5, zero20, age, logval20, brk60; plus gap (US/CRYPTO only) and ara (IDX only). Definitions verbatim from research/E1/protocol.json weak_signals (E1-SIGNALS-v1) / research/E2/protocol.json (E2-SIGNALS-v1); freqr, turn, logmcap excluded (not live-computable from Yahoo fields). Labels on the reference chain (e1.Study.level, HORIZON 5): U = max close t+1..t+5 >= 1.30 x close t (= E30); D = min close t+1..t+5 <= close t / 1.30. Learner: L2 logistic regression, lambda fixed in protocol.json (1e-3 x n), IRLS 25 iterations in numpy, all positives plus a 10% seeded negative subsample weighted 10 (seed 20261015), one fit per (market, label). Arm A score = logit_U; Arm B score = logit_U - logit_D. Threshold: the discovery-period 99.5th percentile of each arm's score (top 0.5% of evaluable ticker-days, comparable to F1_ARA's 0.54% flag rate in 2023); fixed, never searched. Coefficients and thresholds are committed as module-level literal tuples (audit.py allows literals) so the rule hash covers them.

protocol.admissibility: Stage 1 (discovery, in-sample, per arm): report AUC_U, AUC_D, flags, E30 and D30 precision and lift vs matched random (e1.Study.evaluate pattern extended with a D30 block), directional ratio lift_up/lift_down with 1000-resample bootstrap CI, and the harness trading run with matched controls. An arm is admissible for validation only if, on discovery: scored >= 200, avg net > 0, one-sided p < 0.05 vs matched random (200 draws, floor 0.005), avg net > 0 in every discovery year with >= 50 scored (e3.admissibility reused verbatim). An arm that fails IN-SAMPLE is dead without a validation run (cheapest kill). Stage 2 (validation, one run per admissible arm, recorded via write_run): pass iff scored >= 100 (US >= 200), avg net > 0, avg net > matched mean, one-sided p < 0.05 vs matched, and the sensitivity fill model does not flip the sign of (rule minus matched). Primary endpoint = Arm B per market; Arm A, the D30 diagnostic, the ret1<10% (pre-move) vs >=10% split, gross vs net, capturable median, and the ORACLE bound (E[net|E30], E[net|not E30] under the plan and the implied break-even precision p* = (matched - E[net|not E30]) / (E[net|E30] - E[net|not E30])) are reported, not judged. proposals.falsifier: The skeptic's null is falsified if, in any market, Arm B (directional ranker, frozen before validation) passes 2023: scored >= 100 (US >= 200), average net > 0, average net above the matched-random mean with one-sided p < 0.05 (200 draws), and the sensitivity fill model (C for IDX, B as_traded for US, B for crypto) keeps rule-minus-matched positive. The moonshot thesis (daily-bar T-0 information is tradeable) is falsified if Arm B fails in-sample admissibility on discovery or fails the 2023 run in all three markets; the sharper reading that detection is variance detection is confirmed if, in addition, Arm A's D30 lift vs matched is within the bootstrap CI of its E30 lift (directional ratio CI covers 1) and the ORACLE break-even precision p* exceeds the highest E30 precision ever recorded for a daily-bar detector (23.55%, F1_ARA discovery).
risks: 2023 is a once-seen validation year: outcomes of the frozen detectors' 2023 flags are known to the researchers, so a pass is pre-registered but not virgin and must be confirmed prospectively (paper ledger) before any policy change; the holdout stays sealed

A rank-logistic with squared terms is a bounded learner: a null means 'no edge findable by this pre-registered learner', not a proof; a second learner would be a new protocol (KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v2), not a retune
Fill model A is ex-post optimistic (E2 repair: 224 fills accepted only on final entry-session volume averaged -7.03%); hence the sensitivity requirement under B/C before any consequence
Multiplicity: 3 markets x 2 arms; mitigated by declaring Arm B primary and reporting Arm A; no threshold, lambda or feature search

Daily bars cannot prove an opening fill at size and model no intraday path (quality.py:27); the result bounds daily-bar information, not intraday information
proposals.directive_compliance: Holdout: every window ends 2023-12-29 (IDX) / 2023-12-31 (US, crypto); IDX runs are refused by backtest.HOLDOUT unless --holdout-final, which E5 never passes; US/CRYPTO --end is pinned in protocol.json because HEAD has no code guard (backtest.py:251-252); no holdout row is read, labelled or scored; the holdout remains reserved for one final test after prospective evidence. No retune: E1 F1_ARA, E2 G2_RET30, E3 candidates and E4's plan are not touched; E5 is a new family whose only inputs are the pre-registered E1/E2 weak-signal definitions, fitted on discovery alone with no model, threshold or feature search; validation is one run per arm. No manufactured results: every number comes from backtest.run with 200 matched draws under the identical plan, recorded through write_run into results/runs and RUNS.jsonl (append-only, dirty-tree refusal); the ORACLE arm is labelled a bound and is never recorded as a run or presented as performance; gross-vs-net figures quoted here were read from recorded trades.csv.gz and are historical. Pre-registration: research/E5/protocol.json is committed before any statistic, its sha256 is stamped in every stage file, stage directories are created once (exist_ok=False) under the append-only guard, and the freeze (coefficients as rule-module literals) is committed before validation so the rule hash covers the model. No real orders, no ASTRA change, no paper-policy change: a pass would only justify a later, separate POLICY_ID wired through paper._detector and judged prospectively.
proposals.expected_information_value: Either way the program learns something it cannot learn from another plan or cost rerun. If Arm B fails in-sample on discovery in all markets (likely, and the cheapest outcome: no validation run needed), the whole daily-bar price-only detection family is closed on information grounds, not execution grounds, and the only remaining places for edge are non-price timing data (EDGAR acceptanceDateTime, Nasdaq Nordic releaseTime, both reachable in principle per the data map) or intraday order flow, neither of which the repo has; the honest consequence is 'stop the daily-bar moonshot family; do not build more scanners on it'. If Arm A passes detection with high E30 lift but fails trading while its D30 lift is equally high, the mechanism behind E1/E2's 9.3x/5.4x/4.6x 'detection' is nailed down as variance detection, and the ORACLE break-even precision p* gives a closed-form reason why 15-23% precision loses: future proposals can be rejected by arithmetic. If Arm B passes in a market and survives the fill sensitivity, the coefficient vector names which daily-bar features carry direction (the first located edge in the program), and the next step is a prospective paper policy for MOONSHOT_E5_<MARKET>_D1, still without the holdout. The pre-move/inside-move split tells, in every case, whether any remaining lift exists before the first +10% day, which is the only kind a retail participant could act on.

proposals.title: E5 (KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v1): own-event spike-breadth regime as a pre-registered partition of the frozen long detectors (F1_ARA, G2_RET30) under their recorded plan, in IDX, US and crypto
proposals.angle: REGIME / CROSS-MARKET: one regime variable fixed by convention before any number (cross-sectional frequency of the detector's own event, smoothed 20 sessions, versus its trailing 120-session median), applied as a label to the existing frozen signals with the plan unchanged; discovery gate requires the regime effect to hold WITHIN each discovery year (so that "regime" is not a renamed calendar-year effect); one validation run per cell on 2023; Bonferroni over 3 markets x 2 tests; cross-market lead-lag (US breadth -> crypto next UTC day / -> IDX next session) declared as a follow-on that needs a harness field and is NOT part of this test.
proposals.thesis: Every long run of the frozen detectors loses in aggregate, but the sign of the post-flag drift has moved with the market state: on IDX the E3 reference plan was +1.28% vs +0.26% matched in 2021 and -1.56% vs +0.03% in 2022 (research/E3/discovery/reference_summary.json); on crypto every one of 144 short plans was negative in 2021 and 143/144 positive in 2022 (E4 v1), and the BTC-bear short was admissible on discovery; E4 v2 then failed on 2023 because its regime was scarce there. Hypothesis: the drift after a flag is continuation when the market is in a speculative-participation state and reversal when it is not, and the cheapest decision-time measure of that state is the detector's own cross-sectional firing rate (ARA-lock count/tradeable names on IDX; +30%-day count/tradeable names on US and crypto), smoothed over the harness's standard 20 sessions and compared with its own trailing 120-session median (HOT if above, strict; COLD otherwise). Mechanism: when many names are locking limit-up or printing +30% days at once, attention and retail flow are broad, a flagged name is one of a cohort and the next sessions see follow-through; when spikes are isolated, the flagged name is an idiosyncratic pump or news print and the fade dominates (the mechanism E2/E4 measured: median 5-session move -10% vs 0% matched). The test is the interaction I = (rule - matched)_HOT - (rule - matched)_COLD under the plan already recorded for each detector, so the question is whether the flag's EXCESS drift over matched names depends on the state, not whether HOT markets go up. Design-time check of the regressor only (no returns computed; parameters fixed before the check; script in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-KOD-Machine/74d3ac27-b8ad-5917-a6c3-ea51c410b250/scratchpad/breadth_feasibility.py): crypto discovery 1,495 flags = E4's count exactly, HOT 1,052 / COLD 443 (2020 106/35, 2021 645/254, 2022 301/154); IDX discovery 1,919 flags = E3's count exactly, HOT 929 / COLD 990 (2021 728/612, 2022 201/378); US discovery (repair panel) 3,343 flags, HOT 1,947 / COLD 1,396 (2020 313/488 + 117 unlabelled in the 14 sessions before the trailing window is warm, 2021 758/567, 2022 876/341). Breadth is NOT the year dummy: only 54% of IDX 2021 flags are HOT and 72% of US 2022 flags are HOT, so the within-year interaction gate is a real test, not a replay of E3/E4's year splits.
proposals.why_not_already_falsified: (1) Signal family unchanged but information source new: no experiment has ever conditioned a LONG run of F1_ARA or G2_RET30 on any market-state variable; E1/E2/E3 trading results and the nine US repair reruns are aggregates over all sessions. (2) E4 v2's regime was a different variable (BTC close vs its 50-session mean, an index-trend proxy), a different side (short), a different plan family (pullback3/first_up/h2 under liquidation) and one market (crypto); its validation failure was a scarcity failure (34 scored). Breadth is own-event cross-sectional frequency, computed inside every market from its own panel (no BTC row needed, no index/ETF needed: ETFs are dropped from the US universe by idxsig/sources/us_universe.py line 42, so an index-trend regime on US is not even available), and its trailing-median construction gives roughly half the sessions in each cell (HOT session share 0.50 crypto, 0.37 IDX, 0.44 US on discovery) instead of a regime that mostly waits. (3) The E3 REPORT (research/E3/REPORT.md lines 63-67) names exactly this condition for IDX ("trade only when the market-wide ARA count is above its trailing median ... designed without looking at 2023 and tested once on it") and the project map lists it as never run; E5 is that proposal generalised to the three markets with the admission and testing rules written down. (4) The per-year numbers that motivated the hypothesis are NOT what the test measures: the discovery gate requires the interaction inside each calendar year, and the feasibility counts show breadth splits each year roughly 55/45 to 70/30, so a pass cannot be produced by the 2021-vs-2022 difference alone. (5) The crypto long on 2023 (E2: -1.90% vs +1.42% matched) was mostly a BTC-bull year, which approximately falsifies "index bull -> long" there; it says nothing about own-event breadth, which varies inside 2023 by construction.

protocol.family: KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v1: regime partition, not a plan search. Rule module idxsig/rules/moonshot_e5.py copies the detector code verbatim (moonshot_e1 features/flags for IDX, moonshot_g for US/CRYPTO, as moonshot_e3/e4 do; tests check flags identical to the originals) and exposes, per market base detector X, three rules: E5_X_ALL (= X; reproduces the pinned run), E5_X_HOT (= X & HOT_d), E5_X_COLD (= X & regime evaluable & ~HOT_d). Regime definition frozen in research/E5/protocol.json before any statistic: B_d = (# tradeable names with the base event at d) / (# tradeable names at d), with event = lock_up & tradeable on IDX and ret1 >= 0.30 & tradeable on US/CRYPTO (the frozen flag itself, no new threshold); S_d = mean(B_{d-19..d}) (20 = controls.LOOKBACK, the harness convention); M_d = median(S_{d-120..d-1}) with all 120 values required (120 chosen because it is the longest window warm by the US discovery start; 250 was considered and is declared NOT run); HOT_d = S_d > M_d (strict; ties COLD); sessions where M_d is undefined are unlabelled and their flags belong to neither cell (expected: US 2020-07-01..2020-07-21 only). The regime is session-level, uses sessions <= d only (prefix-first causal check applies), returns NaN where not tradeable so controls draw from every tradeable name on the same session exactly as for the base rule. Stages (idxsig/e5.py cloned from e3.py/e4.py, each stage a new exist_ok=False directory under research/E5/<market>/): e5-reproduce (precondition: re-run the three pinned runs on the current panels; REPRODUCED/DEVIATES recorded; --accept-deviation allowed only for the known 4th-decimal matched-baseline deviation from controls.py bcb89f0, as E3 did), e5-regime (writes research/E5/regime/<market>/calendar_discovery.csv: date, B, S, M, HOT, flags_count; sha256 stamped into every later output; committed before discovery; no return in the file), e5-discovery (3 rules x 1 plan per market = 9 harness runs; plans.csv; partition_check.json; gate), e5-validation (the same 3 rules per market on 2023 as recorded write_run runs, 9 runs, one pass; validation calendar computed at this stage only). Partition check (abort on failure): every attempted trade of the ALL run appears in exactly one of HOT/COLD with identical ticker, signal_date, status, entry/exit and net_return; trades present in HOT u COLD but not in ALL must be exactly the ALL run's SKIP_OVERLAP signals (overlap='skip' is per name, so a COLD hold cannot block a HOT signal in the HOT-only run); counts reported.
detectors: F1_ARA (IDX; MOONSHOT_E1_D1 v1.1 code verbatim) -> E5_F1_ARA_ALL / _HOT / _COLD
G2_RET30 (US; MOONSHOT_E2_US_D1 v1 code verbatim) -> E5_G2_RET30_ALL / _HOT / _COLD
G2_RET30 (CRYPTO; MOONSHOT_E2_CRYPTO_D1 v1 code verbatim) -> E5_G2_RET30_ALL / _HOT / _COLD
protocol.plans: The plan already recorded for each detector, unchanged, one per market, no grid: IDX entry at the next close (entry_lag 1), exit at the 5th close, fill model A, ca_mode registry, Rp10,000,000, 10% participation, config pinned to results/runs/20261008T000401Z_MOONSHOT_E1_D1_v1.1 (config sha 34a0d8d7...); CRYPTO entry at the next UTC-day open, exit at the 5th close, fill A, ca_mode adjusted, $5,000, pinned to 20261008T005732Z_MOONSHOT_E2_CRYPTO_D1_v1 (86bd8d48...); US entry at the next open, exit at the 5th close, fill B, units as_traded, quarantine unit_schedule, repair panel panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z (sha 8d3b7ce4...), pinned to 20261008T115656Z_MOONSHOT_E2_US_D1_v1 (the run the live paper decisions cite). Discovery uses the identical config on the discovery window. No entry/exit rule, window, hold, fill model, notional or cost may differ between ALL/HOT/COLD or between stages. 200 matched draws, seed 20261007, controls v2, overlap skip, data_end_exit last_close (as every pinned run).
protocol.discovery_period: IDX 2021-01-22..2022-12-30 (TIER_1); US and CRYPTO 2020-07-01..2022-12-31 (E2 periods); regime warm-up read from the panel start (IDX 2019-07-29, US 2020-01-02, CRYPTO 2020-01-01) for B/S/M only. Discovery is in-sample for the base detectors (E2/E3 addenda) and is used here as a GATE, not for selection: there is nothing to select.
protocol.validation_period: IDX 2023-01-02..2023-12-29; US and CRYPTO 2023-01-01..2023-12-31 (E2/E3 validation windows, VALIDATION_WINDOWS in paper.py). Explicitly declared: the 2023 AGGREGATE outcomes of all three base runs are already recorded (IDX -4.06% vs -0.53%; CRYPTO -1.90% vs +1.42%; US -0.97% vs -0.75%), no regime-split statistic of any of them exists anywhere in the repo, and crypto 2023 has already carried one regime-conditioned test (E4 v2, short, BTC regime). Prior regime looks per validation set: IDX 0, US 0, CRYPTO 1. Holdout (IDX 2024-01-02..2025-02-21; US/CRYPTO 2024-01-01 on) never loaded: e5.py asserts end <= the validation end for every market before building a RunConfig (HEAD has no GLOBAL_HOLDOUT code guard for US/CRYPTO; merging PR #7 first adds it).
protocol.admissibility: Tests per market, all one-sided, family-wise alpha 0.05 Bonferroni over 3 markets x 2 tests = 6 -> alpha_adj = 0.00833 (above the 200-draw floor 0.004975, so attainable). T1 (information): I = (avg_net_HOT - matched_mean_HOT) - (avg_net_COLD - matched_mean_COLD) > 0, p < alpha_adj from a pre-registered calendar-week block bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 20261015) over per-trade excess returns (net_return - per-trade matched mean over the 200 draws, the new trades column), one-sided p = share of resamples with I* <= 0. T2 (tradability of the HOT cell, E3/E4 rules unchanged): scored_HOT >= 200 on discovery / >= 100 on validation, avg_net_HOT > 0, avg_net_HOT > matched_mean_HOT, harness p_one_sided_vs_matched < alpha_adj, and on discovery avg_net_HOT > 0 in every discovery year with >= 50 scored. DISCOVERY GATE (validation is run in a market only if it passes): T1 on the pooled discovery window AND I_y > 0 (point estimate, from by_year rule and random_matched means) in every discovery calendar year with >= 50 scored in both HOT and COLD (expected from the feasibility counts: 2021 and 2022 in all markets; 2020 in crypto COLD ~35 flags may fall below 50 and is then not required). If the gate fails, the market's validation is NOT run and 2023 is not touched for it. VALIDATION PASS: T1 at alpha_adj. T2 is reported in every market but may be CLAIMED only where its discovery version also passed. CLAIM LEVELS declared in advance: IDX and US (first regime look on their 2023) = validation-grade; CRYPTO (second regime look on its 2023) = 'informative, needs prospective confirmation' whatever the p. CONSEQUENCES: pass -> no paper BUY and no policy change from this result alone; it licenses (a) a new PAPER-POLICY version that records the HOT/COLD label on every DECISION (computed from the scan's own 200-day bar pull with the identical 20/120 rule; label only, decisions unchanged) and pre-registers the prospective test (E30 rate and r5 of HOT vs COLD decisions, >= 100 scored HOT decisions before any reading), (b) a holdout-final test only after that prospective evidence, per E4 v2's own closing statement. Fail -> own-event breadth carries no decision-time information about the flag's excess drift for that detector; this protocol states that NO other regime variable may be tested on that market's 2023 for these detectors (the regime look is spent) and any further regime idea is prospective-only. Regime-variable budget declared: candidates considered at design time were (i) own-event breadth [tested], (ii) index trend (BTC 50d / equal-weight panel index) [not tested; E4 v2 tested the short side of it on crypto], (iii) cross-sectional volatility (VIX proxy) [not tested], (iv) cross-market US breadth [not tested; needs a harness field]; only (i) is run and (ii)-(iv) are barred from 2023 by this protocol.
protocol.matched_controls: The harness's own matched random baseline unchanged: for each attempted signal, 200 draws on the SAME session from tradeable names in the same price_band / liquidity / market_cap (IDX) / volatility / momentum / drawdown / listing_age buckets (controls v2, relaxed to >= 5 names), executed under the identical plan. Because the regime is a session-level variable and controls are drawn on the signal's session, every control shares the signal's regime by construction, so (rule - matched) inside a cell is the flag's excess drift given the state, and I is the regime x flag interaction net of the state's effect on all comparable names. Same-session uniform baseline reported as secondary. Known non-match: sector (not point-in-time); HOT episodes can be sector frenzies, which the controls do not hold fixed (declared limitation).
protocol.costs_model: Exactly the pinned runs' profiles (idxsig/profiles.py): IDX fees 0.15% buy / 0.25% sell, lot 100, ARA lock refuses entry; US price-tier cost per side (1.5% <$1, 0.5% $1-5, 0.15% $5-20, 0.05% above) plus SEC fee on sales, no borrow (long only); CRYPTO 0.1% fee + 0.1% slippage per side. No price impact, no dividends. Long only (the short side is declared exhausted on crypto by E4 v2 and not realistically borrowable for US microcaps).

proposals.falsifier: Discovery kill (no 2023 touched): in a market, I <= 0 on the pooled discovery window, or I_y <= 0 in any discovery calendar year with >= 50 scored trades in both HOT and COLD cells -- i.e. the flag's excess drift over matched names is not larger in HOT than in COLD inside the year, so "regime" was only the calendar year. Validation kill (the exact result that ends the regime idea for these detectors): on 2023 in IDX and in US (the first-look markets), I <= 0 or the calendar-week block-bootstrap one-sided p >= 0.00833; equivalently, the HOT-cell rule-minus-matched is not better than the COLD-cell rule-minus-matched by more than block-resampling noise. A HOT cell with fewer than 100 scored trades fails T2 for the right reason and is recorded as such (not retried with another window). Any of these outcomes closes own-event breadth as a decision-time switch for F1_ARA/G2_RET30, bars every other regime variable from these validation sets, and leaves only prospective evidence for any regime claim.
risks: Consumed validation year: the 2023 aggregates of the three base runs are known to everyone on the project; the regime split is new but it is a conditional analysis on seen data. Mitigations are structural (parameter-free-by-convention regime, calendar committed before any outcome, partition of already-recorded trades, discovery gate that can kill before 2023) and the claim levels are downgraded accordingly (crypto explicitly a second look). A sceptic may still weigh IDX/US passes below a fresh-year pass; the protocol says so and routes any pass to prospective confirmation before the holdout.

Cell size in 2023 is unknown by design (not computed here); if a market's HOT cell has < 100 scored trades the tradability test fails for the right reason (E4 v2 precedent) while T1 can still be read.

US leg inherits E2's repair limitations: pre-2023 unit factors are provider records not SEC-corroborated (discovery gate on unverified units, declared); the 669-name quarantine is outcome-correlated (repair_v3 SELECTION_NOTE) and is the same filter in both cells but not guaranteed regime-neutral; survivor-only universe flatters longs in both cells.

Matched controls do not hold sector fixed; HOT episodes may be sector frenzies (e.g. microcap AI in 2023) whose cohort momentum the controls partly miss, which could bias I upward; the same-session baseline and a declared post-hoc descriptive (no claim) by price band are the only checks.

Overlap='skip' makes HOT u COLD a superset of the ALL run's attempted trades by exactly the ALL run's SKIP_OVERLAP signals (IDX 67, US 82, CRYPTO ~6 on 2023); the partition check reports them and they are kept in the cells (declared), so cell sums do not reproduce the ALL average to the last trade.

Mechanical bias: the signal's own flag enters B_d on one of the 20 smoothing sessions (1/4,300 US, 1/690 IDX, 1/250 crypto per flag); negligible but declared; the alternative (exclude the own name) would make the regime name-specific and break the shared-session control property.
IDX precondition will DEVIATE in the 4th decimal of the matched baseline (controls.py bcb89f0, as E3 found); accepted only for that known cause; any deviation on the rule side aborts.

Harness change (two new trades.csv columns) touches backtest.run; must be committed and tested before any E5 run because write_run refuses a dirty tree and the rule hash/verify-runs must stay valid; old runs unaffected.
Compute: 21 harness runs (3 reproduce + 18), the six US runs on the 4.4M-row repair panel with 200 draws are the slow ones; IDX panel must be rebuilt first (build-panel refuses if raw hashes differ).

Interpretation risk: a positive I with negative avg_net_HOT means the regime is informative but not tradeable under this plan; the protocol separates the two claims so neither can be dressed as the other, and no plan search is allowed afterwards on these windows.
proposals.directive_compliance: Holdout: never loaded; every RunConfig end is asserted <= 2023-12-29 (IDX) / 2023-12-31 (US, CRYPTO) inside e5.py, the IDX HOLDOUT guard in backtest.py applies, and merging PR #7 first adds the GLOBAL_HOLDOUT code guard for US/CRYPTO; nothing in this proposal reads, summarises or computes on 2024+. No retune: detector code copied verbatim (E3/E4 pattern, test-checked), no threshold searched (the regime event IS the frozen flag), regime parameters fixed by convention and justified before any statistic (20 = harness LOOKBACK, 120 = longest window warm at the US discovery start, strict > median), the discovery-window regime calendar is committed before discovery, the plan is the recorded one, and HOT/COLD are a partition of trades the harness already recorded. No manufactured results: this proposal contains no return, hit rate or p from any window; the only numbers computed were flag and session counts by regime on discovery windows (regressor distribution, no outcomes), reported as such with the script path. Pre-registration: research/E5/protocol.json with sha stamped in every stage output, stages created exist_ok=False under the append-only research/ guard, dirty-tree refusal, the six tests and alpha_adj = 0.00833 fixed in advance, claim levels and the regime-variable budget declared, consequences on pass (label-only policy version + prospective test, then holdout-final) and on fail (regime family closed for these detectors on these windows) written before the first run. Read-only session: nothing in /home/user/KOD-Machine was modified; the feasibility script lives in the scratchpad.
proposals.expected_information_value: Either way the project learns whether the time variation that every long and short run has shown (hot 2021 vs cold 2022; E4's bear-only admissibility) is a market state knowable at the decision from the panel itself. Pass (I > 0 at alpha_adj in IDX/US): the paper ledger gains a legitimate, pre-registered on/off label for the three live scans and a concrete prospective test (HOT vs COLD E30 rate and r5 over the next ~6 months at the observed ~95 IDX / ~200 US / ~65 crypto decisions per month), which is the first path to a paper BUY that does not require a new detector family; it also tells E3-style plan work where to look (HOT cell only) if ever reopened on new data. Fail: the last cheap regime idea for the frozen detectors is closed with a documented look, the year effects are shown not to be forecastable from own-event breadth, and the regime-variable budget statement stops the drift toward a second and third regime variable on the same 2023 data; effort then goes to prospective evidence or genuinely new signal families (prior-volatility early detection, catalyst feeds). The within-year gate adds a third outcome: breadth tracks the year but not the within-year variation, which would say the regime is slow (yearly) and not actionable at 20-session resolution. The experiment costs about three working days and no new data, and it leaves the holdout and the prospective ledger untouched.

scores.rationale: The one proposal that changes the information set rather than the plan: a pre-registered multivariate ranker over the already-registered E1/E2 weak signals, a directional (U minus D) arm, the first D30 measurement, and a closed-form break-even precision. Its central factual premise is exact: on scored rows gross/net are IDX -3.67/-4.06, crypto -1.51/-1.90, US 060443Z -3.19/-3.65, US 115656Z -0.10/-0.97, so the failures are gross and no cost rerun can flip signs. judgments.notes: Judge 1 (quant/backtest-failure lens). All scores are from reading the proposals against the repo at HEAD (branch claude/idx-signals-test-repo-ds0jw7) plus origin/claude/e4-fade-short-side and origin/codex/e3-us-retention-protocol-v1; nothing was modified, no harness run or network pull was started; the only computations were read-only pandas checks on recorded trades.csv.gz/summary.json files and a re-run of proposal 5's scratchpad counting script on discovery windows (no outcomes). No proposal reads the holdout and none re-tunes a frozen threshold, so none scores 0 on compliance; #5 is the nearest to the line (regime gate on frozen detectors, tested on consumed windows), #2 and #0 Track A are plan/stratification searches on frozen flags over consumed windows (declared, E3 pattern). Verified facts that change weight: (1) #4's gross-vs-net numbers are exact on scored rows, which is the strongest argument in the whole set that another plan/cost rerun cannot help and that the information set is the remaining degree of freedom; (2) #2's harness claim is over-stated in its favour: RunConfig.entry_lag and holding_days already exist, so it is a driver-only experiment (~30 runs) and could run in parallel with anything; (3) #5's HOT/COLD counts reproduce exactly; (4) #0 cannot start now (no 8-K data on disk, placeholder User-Agent, needs ~6,000 EDGAR requests); (5) #3's infrastructure cost is far out of proportion to the information it can return in 3 months, and the committed-sqlite growth makes the design unsustainable at the stated universe sizes. Recommended next move if the owner wants execution now: freeze and run #4 first (cheapest decisive kill; swap the repair panel to primary for US before the freeze), run #2 in parallel since it needs no harness change, then #1 as the first pre-move family. Hold #0 until the arm definition is fixed (document by the t+1 cutoff, entry open t+2) and the SEC pull is authorised; treat #5 as a declared second look that should only run after #4 says whether any daily-bar direction exists; defer #3 until #1 gives A1 a historical lift row, then decide if prospective cases are worth the operational cost. Unknowns I could not verify: the 8-K doc share among G2 flags, the submissions endpoint's acceptanceDateTime timezone convention, and whether the IDX panel-20261013T194245Z rebuild from the on-disk mirror reproduces its manifest sha.

Directive compliance: no proposal re-tunes a frozen detector or reads the holdout; #0 Track A, #2 and #5 all test on 2023 where the frozen detectors' pooled outcomes were seen (#2 follows the accepted E3/E4 select-on-discovery pattern with the known cell barred; #5 is a parameter-free partition but its hypothesis came from seen per-year splits; #0 Track A is an exogenous binary with its decisive test prospective), hence 9/7/7 rather than 0. Ranking for a one-week ship: #2 first (two days of work, all inputs present, decisive either way), #1 second (highest-value new family but 40-50h and the largest rule-module build), #4 third (sharpest kill test, heavy runs and an unrepaired primary US panel), #5 fourth (easy build, lowest novelty and nearest the consumed-data line), #3 and #0 last because neither produces a result this week: #3 needs weeks of live operation and #0's data is not in the repo.

refuted.title: E5-CEILING (KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v1): pre-registered T-0 predictability ceiling for the +30%/5-session event from daily bars, with a directional (up-minus-down) ranker as the kill test

reasons: [Corporate actions / provider, crypto, VERIFIED] The pinned crypto panel (panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z) records token redenominations and the Terra token swap as genuine price moves, and the harness cannot see them: Market.build detects resets from last_close/previous, but global_panel sets previous = prior close, so ca_ratio is always 1 and crypto runs use ca_mode='adjusted' (nothing scaled, nothing excluded). One-bar ratios beyond x20 through 2023 (read directly from the panel): COCOS 2021-01-23 0.000695->0.9003 (x1,295), DREP 2021-04-02 0.0263->2.828 (x107), SUN 2021-06-18 27.57->0.033 (/834), LUNA 2022-05-12 close 0.00032 then next row 2022-05-31 close 8.87 (old LUNA -> LUNA 2.0, x27,700; LUNC is a separate base from 2022-09-09), BNX 2023-02-22 175.5->1.585 (/111), QUICK 2023-07-21 74.2->0.0597 (/1,243). For E5 these are fake U labels for the 5 sessions before COCOS/DREP/LUNA (discovery fit) and fake D labels before SUN (discovery) and BNX/QUICK (validation 2023), and a long held across BNX or QUICK is scored at about -99% (5,000 USDT notional): one such trade moves a ~600-trade validation average by ~0.17pp and a ~300-trade one by ~0.33pp, enough to decide 'avg net > 0' in a marginal arm, and the D30/directional-ratio diagnostic on crypto counts them as real down-events. E2's crypto run was not hit (its only QUICK trade was 2023-02-20..02-25), but a high-volatility ranker is far more exposed than G2_RET30. The proposal's protocol does not mention unit changes on crypto.

[Look-ahead in the primary fit data, VERIFIED] panel_us-20261008T004105Z and panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z are format panel-global-v1, built with the legacy _finish that deletes a row when the NEXT session's close reverts (manifest qa.spike_rows_dropped 177 US, 2 crypto; the crypto one is LUNA 2022-05-13 inside discovery; the repair manifest's qa_reverting_spike_rows=23 shows 23 US deletions fall inside 2020-01..2023-12). The repo itself classifies this as a future-informed deletion kept 'only as _finish_legacy_v1 for forensic reproduction' and built the causal panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z (causal-close-v2, read_through 2023-12-29). Each deletion removes both label tails (+200% at t-1, -67% at t) and the catastrophic trade entered at open t. The magnitude is tiny (23 of ~3.8M rows) but E5 proposes to fit coefficients, set the 99.5% threshold and run validation A on the legacy panels while a causal panel is on disk, so the primary numbers would carry a documented look-ahead. e1.Study refuses the repair panel's format ('panel-global-v2-units'), so e5.build_dataset cannot route through Study's format check unchanged.

[Provider re-adjustment, US primary run, VERIFIED via ERRATA.md item 1] In the original US panel every price level is in 2026-10 units. A rank-logistic ranker over vol20/dd60/zero20 will concentrate its top 0.5% in sub-$1 names, which are the names that later reverse-split (60% of E2's G2 flags): under the proposal's primary fill A / units=panel their cost tier is too cheap, SKIP_LOT drops names whose adjusted price exceeds the $5,000 notional, and the controls' price_band is the wrong band. ERRATA re-costed E2 from -3.65% to -4.47% from this alone. The proposal relegates as_traded to a sign-only sensitivity; the wrong-way bias sits in the primary.

[Protocol cannot be executed as written, VERIFIED] The crypto fill-B sensitivity is impossible at HEAD with the named panel: execution.execute requires fill B => units='as_traded' (line 383), backtest.run requires a unit_factor column for as_traded (lines 258-261), the crypto panel has no such column, build_us_repair is US-only, and the proposal forbids changes to backtest.py/execution.py. So the crypto pass rule ('sensitivity fill model does not flip the sign') can never be evaluated and no crypto verdict is possible under the protocol's own criteria. E4's crypto protocol (origin/claude/e4-fade-short-side research/E4/protocol.json) used fill A only.

[Survivorship contaminates the rank features and the threshold, US] Unlike one-threshold rules, every E5 feature is a per-session percentile rank over the panel cross-section, which for US is the 2026-10-08 listing snapshot (survivor-only, ~4,800 evaluable names per 2023 session). Ranks of vol20/dd60/etc. at any 2021-2023 session are therefore taken against a cross-section purged of the names that later died (a function of 2026 survival), the D label is under-represented for the feature profiles that precede delisting (inflating logit_U - logit_D exactly where the learner looks), and the frozen 99.5% threshold is calibrated on the purged cross-section and does not transfer to a live cross-section that still contains the future dead. Matched controls (same survivor panel, tercile buckets) absorb part of the label effect but not the within-bucket extreme a squared-rank learner targets. The proposal calls a US-only pass 'weak evidence' yet its FALSIFIER says the null is falsified by an Arm B pass 'in any market': internally inconsistent. Magnitude of the missing cross-section is unknown from the repo (no delisting list).

[Label-generating process changes inside IDX validation (exchange rules, not leakage)] market.REGIMES: ARB 7% from 2020-03-13 to 2023-06-02, 15% from 2023-06-05, symmetric 35/25/20 from 2023-09-04. The whole IDX discovery window (2021-01-22..2022-12-30) is under ARB 7%, where D (-23% within 5 sessions) needs at least four consecutive limit-down closes ((0.93)^3 = -19.6% is insufficient); from 2023-06-05 it needs two sessions and from 2023-09-04 one. COEF_D and the Arm B threshold are thus fitted on a regime where D is mechanically rare and validated on a year whose second half has a different D process; the 'directional ratio' diagnostic on IDX is confounded by this and the protocol does not mention it.

[Window cold-start mismatch between fit and harness, not leakage but a fidelity gap no prior run exposed] backtest.run slices the market to [start, end] before causal_signals (lines 279-287), so inside each harness window the rule's rolling features start cold: vol20 (min 15), dd60 (min 20), med_val shift-1 (min 10), zero20 (20 full), age (= sessions since window start). The fit dataset computes them warm on the full panel. The first ~60 sessions of every discovery and validation run (~25% of 2023) score a feature vector (NaN -> 0.5 rank) the model never saw. F1_ARA and G2_RET30 needed only prev/lock_up, so no recorded run has hit this.

[Minor, IDX fidelity] Market.build applies the special-monitoring-board 10% lock to every one-price bar on all dates although the board exists only from 2023-06-12; in 2021-22 a thin name's single print at +10..34% is treated as ARA-locked, entering E5's `ara` feature and refusing the fill. Inherited by E1-E3; symmetric for rule and controls.

[Checked and sound] Cross-sectional features (medians, ranks) pass the prefix-first check: E2's recorded runs with rel1 report lookahead mode prefix-first-v1, and NaN rows for not-yet-listed names do not change pandas pct ranks. Labels require t+5 inside the period, so no label touches validation from discovery or the holdout from validation; US/crypto windows are sliced before execution so no 2024 row is read (HEAD indeed has no GLOBAL_HOLDOUT; the E4 branch does). Quoted gross-vs-net figures reproduce from trades.csv.gz (-3.67/-4.06, -1.51/-1.90, -3.19/-3.65, -0.10/-0.97). Yahoo volume is split-adjusted (repair/conventions.json, AMZN volume_rel_diff 0), so value, logval20, valr and volr are unit-free (the proposal's 'logval20 not unit-free' is over-cautious). The pinned IDX mirror commit bc0ac7712ce5 is on disk (975/975 manifest files present), so rebuilding panel-20261013T194245Z (sha a924921a, registry 33f81beb bound to it) needs no network; the fallback panel-20261007T225823Z has registry ca_registry-20261007T230210Z bound. E1 vol20 AUC 0.679 verified. The ORACLE arm reads only the label matrix and is not recorded.
verdicts.fix: Amend KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v1 before any statistic is computed: (1) Fit, threshold and validate US on the causal panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z (read_through 2023-12-29) with units=as_traded as the PRIMARY (fill B primary, fill A as_traded as the sensitivity), quarantine mode declared in protocol.json; e5.build_dataset must bypass e1.Study's format check (accept panel-global-v2-units) while reusing its level/r5max/elig code. (2) Rebuild the crypto panel from the on-disk raw Binance pull with the causal _finish (no network, no external data), adding a unit_factor column fixed at 1.0 so the fill-B sensitivity can run without touching backtest.py/execution.py, and a pre-registered unit-reset flag: a bar whose close/previous is >= x20 or <= 1/20 marks a unit change; labels for sessions t-5..t of that name are NaN (measurement censoring, not a signal input), trades held across it are not scored on either side (apply the same mask to control draws in e5 before the baseline statistics are read), and the six 2020-2023 cases (COCOS, DREP, SUN, LUNA, BNX, QUICK) are listed in protocol.json as the known set. (3) Rewrite the FALSIFIER so the null is falsified only by an Arm B pass on IDX TIER_1 or on crypto; US Arm A/B are reported as diagnostics (survivor-only cross-section), never as a pass. (4) Declare the IDX ARB regime split (2023-06-05, 2023-09-04) in protocol.json and report IDX validation and the D30/directional-ratio diagnostic by regime; optionally define D on IDX as the regime-equivalent limit-down count rather than a fixed -23%. (5) Add a literal WARMUP=60 to moonshot_e5 (compute returns NaN for the first 60 sessions of its view) and start every harness window 60 sessions before the period so signals are confined to the period with warm features; this passes the prefix-first check and needs no backtest change. (6) Note the special-board anachronism in RISKS. With these, the design (frozen rank-logistic rankers, in-sample kill gate, one validation run per arm, ORACLE bound) is sound under this lens.

reasons: PRIMARY TEST IS ANTI-CONSERVATIVE FOR A VARIANCE-SELECTING RANKER. The pre-registered pass rule ('avg net > matched mean with one-sided p < 0.05 from 200 matched draws') places the rule's mean in the distribution of matched-portfolio means (idxsig/backtest.py _baseline, dist(): p = share of draws >= observed). That distribution's spread is sigma_matched/sqrt(n), while the rule's own mean has SE sigma_rule/sqrt(n). Whenever the rule picks names more volatile than their matched controls (coarse tercile matching, see next point), the nominal 5% test has a larger size under the null of equal means. Measured on the recorded runs (results/runs/*/trades.csv.gz vs random_draws.csv, SKIP_OVERLAP excluded): IDX 000401Z rule per-trade std 0.189, SE 0.0094 vs draw-mean SD 0.0061 -> implied size 14%; crypto 005732Z 0.349/0.0215 vs 0.0081 -> 27%; US 060443Z 0.346/0.0104 vs 0.0059 -> 18%; US fill-B 115656Z -> 23%; IDX FILL-C 050040Z -> 20%. E5's arms select the top 0.5% by predicted tail probability (vol20 is the dominant univariate separator, AUC 0.68/0.78/0.56), so the variance mismatch will be at least as large as for F1_ARA/G2_RET30. With three markets each tested at an effective size of ~15-25%, the family-wise chance of 'Arm B passes in some market' under the null is roughly 40-50%, and the FALSIFIER ('the null is falsified if, in any market, Arm B passes') would be met far too often by noise. The fill-model sensitivity run (same trades, different fills) is highly correlated with the primary and does not restore size. No Bonferroni or per-market correction is declared.

MATCHED CONTROLS ARE OFTEN NOT MATCHED ON VOLATILITY ON IDX AND CRYPTO. controls.py v2 orders keys (price_band, liquidity, market_cap, volatility, momentum, drawdown, listing_age) and relaxes from the last key when fewer than MIN_POOL=5 names match; volatility is a tercile. In the recorded IDX run 000401Z, 291 of 1,042 attempts (28%) were matched on price_band / +liquidity / +market_cap only (match_level_used: 63, 52, 176), i.e. not on volatility at all; crypto 005732Z: 90 of 270 (33%) not matched on volatility; only US matched fully (1,224/1,496). The proposal's central claim 'because the controls match volatility tercile, a ranker that merely picks high-vol names is compared against high-vol names: that is the point' is therefore only partly true on the decisive market (IDX), and a tercile is far coarser than a 0.5% tail. The proposal also forbids any change to controls.py, which removes the obvious fix (a v3 ordering with a finer volatility bucket ahead of market_cap).

ARM B ON IDX IS A REGIME-MISMATCHED LABEL. idxsig/market.py: ARB was 7% flat from 2020-03-13 to 2023-06-05, 15% from 2023-06-05, symmetric with ARA from 2023-09-04. The whole IDX discovery period (2021-01-22..2022-12-30) sits under ARB 7%, where a -23% move in 5 sessions needs >=3-4 consecutive limit-down closes. Computed read-only on the on-disk IDX panel (panel-20261007T225823Z), discovery only, e1-style eligibility: U = 6,076 (1.879%, matches E1), D = 2,185 (0.676%), U&D = 0 (never co-occur), and 1,993 of 2,185 D events (91%) have >=3 lock_down closes in t+1..t+5. So logit_D on IDX is a predictor of ARB-7% lock-down cascades, a mechanism that is partly removed in June 2023 and wholly removed in September 2023, i.e. in the middle of the validation year. The directional score logit_U - logit_D is then fit on one limit regime and validated on three; a pass or fail on IDX Arm B cannot be attributed to T-0 information. (For reference, computed on discovery only: crypto U 5.56% / D 6.19%, US survivor-only U 1.13% / D 1.05%; no such limit artefact there.)

THE CRYPTO FILL-B SENSITIVITY CANNOT RUN AS WRITTEN. execution.execute raises 'fill model B is defined for open entries in as-traded units' unless units='as_traded', and backtest.run raises 'units=as_traded needs a panel with a unit_factor column' (backtest.py:258-261). panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z.csv.gz has no unit_factor column (only panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z does), and no crypto repair panel or build step exists; the E4 branch's crypto protocol also used fill A only. The proposal both requires this sensitivity for any policy consequence and forbids changes to backtest.py/execution.py, so the pre-registered pass rule for crypto is unexecutable.

THE VERDICT RULE CONFLATES INFORMATION WITH EXECUTION. Stage 1 kills an arm on e3.admissibility (scored >= 200, avg net > 0, p < 0.05 vs matched, positive every discovery year), an execution-and-cost criterion under one plan, and the INFO VALUE section then reads 0/3 as 'the whole daily-bar price-only detection family is closed on information grounds, not execution grounds'. A ranker with real direction (directional ratio CI > 1, gross close-to-close r5 above matched) can fail that gate through costs, the 5-session fixed exit, ARA locks or SKIP_LIQUIDITY (F1_ARA: 339 + 248 of 1,042 attempts). The detection-level quantities that would actually test information (AUC_U, AUC_D, directional ratio, pre-move split) are 'reported, not judged'. The proposal's own RISKS admit a null from one L2 rank-logistic 'is not a proof', contradicting the closure claim; and the information set is 15-17 hand-chosen features, not 'the entire daily-bar information set', so 'ceiling' overstates it.

DIRECTIONAL-RATIO BOOTSTRAP IGNORES CLUSTERING. Ranker scores built from vol20, dd60, age, logval20 are persistent, so flags cluster on consecutive sessions of the same name and across names on the same session; a 1000-resample bootstrap over flags treats them as independent and gives CIs that are too narrow. The same persistence, combined with overlap='skip', means ~900 IDX 2023 flags at 0.5% could collapse to a few hundred attempts and, after IDX liquidity/ARA skips (F1_ARA filled 420/1,042), to near or below the scored >= 100 floor; no de-duplication or minimum-attempt rule is pre-registered.

2023 IS ALREADY CONSUMED BY SIBLINGS USING E5'S OWN FEATURES. IDX 2023: E1 F1_ARA (ara) detection + two trading runs; US 2023: E2 G2_RET30 (ret1) + 9 repair reruns + US_BREAKOUT_v1 (brk60); crypto 2023: E2 (ret1) + E4 v2. The univariate 2023 trading outcomes of three E5 inputs (ara, ret1, brk60) and the 2023 r5 medians (-10.3% US, -11.5% crypto, from E2 validation result.json) are known to the designers and motivate the 'variance not direction' thesis and the symmetric D label; the proposal acknowledges the year is once-seen but still writes a FALSIFIER that treats a 2023 pass as falsifying the null. Not fatal for the expected null, but any pass is weak and the closure claim from a consumed year plus a bounded learner is overreach.

CAUSALITY DETAIL: 'features computed as in e1.py Study._signals' is not prefix-safe as written. Study._signals age = arange - first is negative (not NaN) for names not yet listed, and zero20 = rolling sum of present&~tradeable is 0 (not NaN) before listing; in rules.causal_signals the full-window call would rank those rows while the prefix call cannot see them, so per-session rank(pct=True) differs and raises LookaheadError. Must mask by present before ranking (fixable code detail; mentioned because the proposal says 'causal by construction').

VERIFIED (not refuted): gross vs net figures match trades.csv.gz exactly (IDX -3.67%/-4.06%, crypto -1.51%/-1.90%, US -3.19%/-3.65%, US fill B -0.10%/-0.97%); vol20 matched-set AUCs 0.679 IDX / 0.780 US / 0.556 crypto are in the signal_stats.csv files; E1-SIGNALS-v1 / E2-SIGNALS-v1 lists exist in the protocol.json files with the stated exclusions; RULE_FIELDS carries value, lock_up and open; audit.py accepts literal tuples; HEAD cli.py has --holdout-final for IDX only and no US/CRYPTO guard; F1_ARA 2023 flag rate 972/179,617 = 0.54%.
