verdicts.fix: Amend KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v1 before the protocol is frozen: (1) Replace the primary pass test with one that carries the rule's own variance: per-signal paired difference (rule trade net minus the mean net of its 200 matched controls, obtained in e5.py through execution.execute + controls.matched_draws, the ORACLE path), with a cluster bootstrap over signal sessions (or a date-clustered Welch test); report the harness p alongside but do not judge on it; set the per-market threshold at p < 0.0167 (Bonferroni over the 3 declared primaries) or declare IDX the single primary. (2) Allow one additive controls change: a VERSIONS['v3'] in controls.py with volatility quintile (or decile) ahead of market_cap, so a 0.5% tail is compared with its own volatility stratum; keep v2 reported for comparability. (3) IDX Arm B: define D in limit-relative terms consistent across regimes (e.g. 'min close <= close x prod of (1 - ARB_k) over the next 3 sessions, using the ARB in force at t', or 'locked down on >= 3 of the next 5 sessions'), or restrict the IDX Arm B validation window to 2023-01-02..2023-06-02 and accept the N loss, or drop IDX Arm B and make IDX Arm A the IDX primary with crypto/US Arm B the directional primaries. (4) Crypto sensitivity: pre-register a crypto panel build with unit_factor = 1 (no splits; a stated data step) so fill B can execute, or replace it with fill A at max_participation 0.05 and say so. (5) Split the verdict: an information verdict judged on pre-registered detection statistics (directional ratio cluster-bootstrap CI excluding 1, gross close-to-close r5 of the top 0.5% vs matched) and a separate execution verdict on net trading; drop the 'closes the family on information grounds' wording for a null from one bounded learner. (6) Pre-register a first-entry de-duplication (signal only when a name enters the top 0.5% after being outside it for >= 5 sessions) and the minimum attempt count, and mask age/zero20/all features by present before per-session ranking so the prefix-first check passes. (7) State explicitly that a 2023 pass is non-virgin and that the only consequence is a prospective paper policy, never a holdout touch.

reasons: Verdict mechanism conflates information with executability on the decisive market. The thesis-level verdict ('daily-bar T-0 information absent iff 0/3 Arm B pass') rests on the trading pass, but on IDX the fixed plan (buy the next close) refuses every flag whose next close is ARA-locked. research/E3/discovery/plans.csv, reference plan F1_ARA|fixed1|fixed|h5 under fill C on discovery: 529 SKIP_ARA_LOCK + 553 SKIP_LIQUIDITY of 1,831 attempts (59% unfillable); the recorded E1 2023 run: 339 SKIP_ARA_LOCK + 248 SKIP_LIQUIDITY of 1,042. A ranker that loads on ret1/ara (the strongest in-sample U predictors) inherits this outcome-correlated fill filter on the rule side only (matched controls lock far less often), so an Arm B failure on IDX cannot be read as 'information absent' and the INFO VALUE claim 'closed on information grounds, not execution grounds' does not follow from the protocol as written.

Exit-side liquidation is unmodelled and material for tail-event flags. execution.execute caps entry size at max_participation x volume but applies no capacity check on the exit: the full position is sold at the first sellable close at zero impact. Recomputed from results/runs/20261008T000401Z_MOONSHOT_E1_D1_v1.1/trades.csv.gz against the panel: 21.9% of scored IDX trades held more than 10% of the exit session's volume (p90 = 34%, 7.6% above 50%, 3.4% above 100% of that day's volume), averaging -6.4% net vs -3.4% for the rest; 64/407 exits rolled while ARB-locked or untraded (mean -13.8%, up to 23 sessions). US 060443Z: 9.0% of trades above 10% exit participation (mean -8.5% vs -3.2%); crypto none. A ranker sized at 10% of a volume-surge entry day and exiting after the surge is exactly the case this gap flatters; a 'pass' under the harness is therefore not evidence of executability, while the proposal forbids harness changes and names no exit diagnostic.

The directional (D) label is structurally asymmetric on IDX, so Arm B and the 'variance detector' diagnostic are uninterpretable there. During the whole IDX discovery period the lower auto-rejection limit was 7% flat (market.REGIMES: COVID ARB 7% from 2020-03-13 to 2023-06-04), so a -23% minimum close within 5 sessions needs at least four consecutive limit-down closes. Computed on the on-disk panel over 2021-01-22..2022-12-30 only: U = 5,789 of 310,596 eligible ticker-days (1.864%), D = 2,014 (0.648%), U and D co-occur in 0 ticker-days, the 0.1th percentile one-day return is -7.42% and no eligible day fell 20%. The proposal's mechanism ('P(+30%) rises together with P(-23%)') cannot manifest on IDX; logit_D is fitted on a different event (multi-day limit-down collapse), and the 2023 validation year spans three ARB regimes (7% to 2023-06-04, 15% to 2023-09-03, symmetric 20-35% after), so COEF_D fitted under 7% ARB is applied where a single session can lose 20-35%.

Rank-based top-0.5% flags are serially dependent, which breaks the admissibility and p-value logic. On IDX discovery a top-0.5% cross-sectional vol20 flag (the one pre-event separator the ranker will load on) repeats the previous session's name 81.5% of the time, covers only 172 distinct names in two years, and runs 5.4 sessions on average. With overlap=skip the same name is re-entered the session after each exit, so 'scored >= 200' and the 200-draw one-sided p (which redraws independent control names per trade) overstate the effective sample and are anti-conservative for the rule side; the protocol pre-registers no cooldown, per-name cap or name-level bootstrap.

Crypto entry is a zero-latency fill. In panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z over discovery, open(t+1) equals close(t) within 1 bp in 33.1% of rows and within 10 bp in 69.9% (median gap 4.4 bp): the 'next open' is the same print as the signal close. A cross-sectional rank over 683 pairs computed after the 00:00 UTC bar closes, followed by order placement in the most volatile 0.5% of names, cannot execute at that print; fill model B addresses capacity, not latency, and backtest.run takes entry_price from the profile with no RunConfig override, so the pre-registered sensitivity cannot bound this.

The ORACLE/p* diagnostic as specified cannot deliver the claimed 'closed-form reason'. A crude executable-oracle on IDX discovery (E30 truth at t, entry at close t+1 if traded and not ARA-locked, exit at close t+6 on the reference chain, no lots/fees/rolls) gives E[gross | E30, executable] = +39.1% (median +32.2%, 96.8% hit; 81.5% of E30 days executable) against -0.22% for non-E30 days and +0.40% for all eligible days. Universe-wide conditional means therefore put p* below 1%, far under the 23.55% precision F1_ARA recorded, so the FALSIFIER clause 'p* exceeds the highest E30 precision ever recorded' is numerically unreachable and the diagnostic would misstate why 15-23% precision loses (the loss comes from the flag population's own conditionals: fill selection against continuation and a post-flag median near -10%, E1/E2 validation r5_median).

Data and panel choices as written. (a) The pinned E3 panel panel-20261013T194245Z.csv.gz is not on disk and data/raw holds only Binance pulls (no idx_mirror, no yahoo raw), so rebuilding it requires a network clone of the mirror; 'available now: true' holds only for the fallback panel 9d3a0718 with ca_registry-20261007T230210Z (on disk, registry built for that panel), on which E3's reproduce stage recorded DEVIATES (rule side identical, matched mean differs at 1e-5). (b) The US fit panel panel_us-20261008T004105Z is panel-global-v1 built with the legacy future-informed spike deletion (177 rows) and physically contains 2024-2026 rows, while the repair panel (causal preprocessing, read_through 2023-12-29, no holdout rows, 23 spike rows kept as a flag) is used only for the fill-B leg; the protocol does not state quarantine=none for that leg although research/E2/repair_v3/SELECTION_NOTE.md shows the quarantine is outcome-correlated (-9.17% vs -1.75%), so a sign disagreement between legs could come from the population, not the fill model. (c) The crypto cost statement double-counts: profiles.CRYPTO applies 0.1% fee + 0.1% tier (the tier is the labelled slippage) = 0.2% per side, not 0.3%. (d) Fill model A as primary is a step back from E3, which already chose fill C because A is ex-post; E2 repair found A-only fills averaged -7.03%.

Claims that do check out (not refutation points): the gross-vs-net decomposition is accurate (recomputed from trades.csv.gz: IDX -3.67%/-4.06%, crypto -1.51%/-1.90%, US -3.19%/-3.65%, US fill-B -0.10%/-0.97%); backtest.py guards only the IDX holdout (line 253) so the explicit US/crypto --end is needed; rules/audit.py accepts module-level literal tuples; E2-SIGNALS-v1 lists valr, rngr, up5, zero20, age, logval20, gap and E1-SIGNALS-v1 adds ara; e1.Study._pool matches on price_band/liquidity/market_cap only; the referenced line numbers in e1.py, e3.py and rules/__init__.py are correct; the aggregate notional (about 4 IDX and 25 US flags per session) is not a capacity problem.
verdicts.fix: Amend KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v1 before freezing: (1) split the verdict: the information verdict rests on the Stage-1 detection block over the full flag set (AUC_U, AUC_D, directional ratio CI, and the fill-independent plan-window endpoint return of flags vs matched on the reference chain), the trading run is a separate executability verdict; report SKIP_ARA_LOCK/SKIP_LIQUIDITY shares and the counterfactual plan return of unfillable flags per arm. (2) Define D per market in exchange-reachable units (IDX: an ARB-aware label such as k consecutive limit-down closes or the discovery-period lower-tail quantile matching U's base rate; US/crypto may keep close_t/1.30), and split the IDX 2023 report at 2023-06-05 and 2023-09-04. (3) Add an exit-capacity diagnostic in e5.py from trades.csv.gz plus the panel (shares / exit-session volume, as-traded for US): the pass must hold on trades with exit participation <= 10% (or with a pre-registered exit penalty), and rolled exits are reported. (4) Pre-register a per-name cooldown after each exit (or a per-name cap), report distinct names, and compute a name-level block-bootstrap p alongside the 200 matched draws. (5) Add a pessimistic crypto leg entering at the close of t+1 via a profile variant (profiles.py is not on the no-change list), and report the share of entries where open(t+1) = close(t). (6) Fit and validate US on the repair panel with quarantine=none under both fill legs; use the legacy panel only for a comparability run. (7) Make fill C (IDX) and B (US, crypto) primary with A as the sensitivity, and state crypto costs as 0.2% per side. (8) Redefine the break-even diagnostic within the flag population (E[net | flag, E30], E[net | flag, not E30]) and drop the universe-wide p* clause from the falsifier. (9) Either schedule the mirror pull for panel-20261013T194245Z explicitly or pre-register the on-disk fallback panel 9d3a0718 + ca_registry-20261007T230210Z with E3's DEVIATES note on record.

refuted.title: E5 PRE-SPIKE TAPE (KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v1): accumulation, re-base and contraction detectors that fire WITHOUT a big up day, in IDX, US and crypto, with the KOD VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET definition as the frozen reference member

reasons: SERIOUS (US, detection stage): the matched-control pool that the validation pass criterion reads (detection p_one_sided_vs_matched < 0.05, lift > 1) is built by e1.Study with controls.features(m, 'v2', band_edges) at idxsig/e1.py:151, i.e. WITHOUT as_traded, and Market.from_panel (execution.py:169-188) never attaches unit_factor; _pool (e1.py:220-227) matches on price_band first. So on US the band is the provider-adjusted close, which embeds reverse splits that happen AFTER the session. research/E2/ERRATA.md:21-24 already records this as an erratum ('controls are matched on the wrong band for the same names'); the proposal's e1.py change list (format check, IGNITION guard, HORIZON) omits it. Scale on panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z: unit_factor != 1 on 20.95% of discovery and 18.47% of validation ticker-days; adjusted close >= 5x the as-traded close on 413,064 discovery and 173,167 validation ticker-days; 1,141 of 4,720 discovery names affected. Names with later reverse splits are the population that produces most E30 events (6.0% base rate under $1 vs 0.9% above $20; 60% of E2 flags), and they get matched against higher-band controls with lower base rates, inflating lift and lowering p. This is a look-ahead inside the control construction, not just a label error.

SERIOUS (all markets, '2023 is out-of-sample for this family' is overstated): research/E1/validation/episodes_E30.csv (569 rows), research/E2/US/validation/episodes_E30.csv (4,100) and research/E2/CRYPTO/validation/episodes_E30.csv (730) list every +30% episode of 2023 with ret1, ret5, ret20, volr, rngr, vol20, dd60, zero20, up5 at the decision close, plus flags.csv with r5/r5max/peak_k. The complete positive class of the proposed validation period, with the single-day analogues of every E5 feature (rngr for quiet, volr for creep, ret20 for not_repriced, vol20 for hivol, dd60 for C1), is on disk. The ZEALAND thresholds the proposal calls frozen 'before any moonshot outcome was seen' were committed at 1e1eef8 2026-10-08T12:28Z, after E1 discovery (29e32e4 00:00Z), E2 discovery/validation (e5a1be2/21345b1 00:55-00:57Z) and the E2 report (b76e201 06:12Z), and the ZEALAND protocol.json explicitly reuses E1-SIGNALS-v1 definitions. The protocol's leakage declaration ('knowledge of the 2023 base rates and of big-day behaviour') understates what is visible; a 2023 pass cannot be distinguished from a design that fits visible 2023 structure. No in-repo window can replace 2023 (holdout sealed), so only the prospective arm is clean.

MINOR (US volume is not 'base units'): research/E2/repair/conventions.json concludes 'volume is adjusted by the same factors: as-traded volume = Yahoo volume / F(t)'; global_panel.load_us stores Yahoo volume raw and unit_factor is a Market.REGISTRY_FIELD never shown to a RuleView (rules/__init__.py:22-23, 89-90). So creep = v5/v_base and volr are computed on a series rescaled by split records effective after the session wherever the 25-session window straddles an in-window split; the prefix-first LookaheadError check cannot catch it because the adjustment is static in the file. Scale: 425 discovery and 321 validation unit_factor change points (283 and 273 reverse); 10,449 of 2,766,059 discovery and 7,739 of 1,200,194 validation ticker-days lie within 25 sessions after a change point (0.4-0.6%, concentrated in the reverse-split population). Direction is not clearly favourable to the long, but the DATA block's claim is false for US and the RuleView doctrine ('exchange data only') is violated by the field itself.

MINOR (crypto panel has a future-informed deletion): panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z.json shows spike_rows_dropped 2 and no preprocessing_version, i.e. built with global_panel._finish_legacy_v1, which drops a row when the NEXT day's close reverts >3x; the dropped LUNA 2022-05-13 row sits inside the discovery window of the canonical 2022 collapse. The proposal inherits this panel 'as E2/E4's recorded runs'; a causal rebuild would make the precondition reproduce stage DEVIATE.

MINOR (reference row is not the KOD detector): kod-machine/kod/detectors.py:72-86 defines VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET as creep AND quiet; price_already_repriced feeds PRIMARY_DOC_BEFORE_PRICE (lines 59-69), not this detector. A1 adds not_repriced, so the 'population base rate for the KOD doctrine' row is a stricter subset, and the ZEAL.CO unit test ties the harness to price_facts.measures() facts, not to the detector's SIGNAL logic.

MINOR (IDX corporate-action artefacts, not leakage): IDX mirror volume is as traded (panel.py), while the level chain absorbs resets through `previous`; in TIER_1 2021-01-22..2023-12-29 there are 123 reference resets, 41 with ratio >= 2 (forward-split-like), each producing a real share-volume step with a quiet level chain, i.e. spurious creep/A4 flags for up to 25 sessions. Observable in real time, so not look-ahead, but the proposal masks nothing and ca_mode=registry only excludes trades HELD across a reset, not signals whose window contains one. Also verified: high/low are missing exactly on zero-volume rows (10.74% of TIER_1 rows in the window), so quiet/creep NaN coverage is as the proposal says.

MINOR (thesis claim about matching holds only at the trading stage): the detection gate is Wilson lower bound > the UNMATCHED period base rate (e1.py:322) and the detection-stage pool matches price band/liquidity/market cap only (e1.py:220); the v2 volatility/momentum/drawdown terciles exist only in backtest.run's controls (controls.py:71-74, backtest.py:326-331). A3/C1 pass detection on vol20 alone (AUC 0.68/0.78), so kill criterion (1) does not test 'structure beyond the volatility state'. Declared in the matched_controls block but contradicted by the THESIS paragraph.

NOTE (holdout wording): e1.Study (e1.py:104-107) and backtest.run (backtest.py:257-279) build Market from the full panel (crypto file runs to 2026-10-07, IDX to 2026-10-13) before slicing; no statistic is computed on holdout columns (all cumulative fields are causal), but 'the holdouts are never loaded' is literally false and HEAD has no GLOBAL_HOLDOUT guard for US/crypto (only origin/claude/e4-fade-short-side backtest.py:85,296 has one).
verdicts.fix: 1) Detection stage on US: in e1.Study, when the panel carries unit_factor, attach Market.with_units(dense unit_factor) and build self.buckets with controls.features(..., as_traded=True) (and use the as-traded close in row()/price_band), so the detection-stage pool matches on the band that was observable; write this into protocol.json and the e1.py change list before the freeze; report the adjusted-band result only as a sensitivity. 2) Re-label 2023: declare it a consumed period and name the stage 'post-discovery check', listing in the protocol's leakage declaration the exact files on record (E1/validation/episodes_E30.csv, E2/US/validation/episodes_E30.csv, E2/CRYPTO/validation/episodes_E30.csv, flags.csv, with their feature columns) and the ZEALAND commit time relative to E1/E2; make the 'validated pair' claim and any PAPER-POLICY-v5 eligibility rest on a pre-registered prospective ledger (minimum n of scored prospective trades, horizon, pass rule written now), not on 2023. 3) US volume: restate DATA (volume is Yahoo split-adjusted, not base units); in e5.py mask, symmetrically for flags and the evaluable/control set, the 25 sessions at and after any unit_factor change point for the creep/volr members (or report the straddling flags as a separate line); state that the prefix-first check does not cover provider adjustment. 4) Crypto: rebuild the panel with causal-close-v2 (or declare the two legacy deletions, naming LUNA 2022-05-13) and record DEVIATES in the precondition stage if the reference runs move. 5) Add A0 = creep AND quiet (the exact KOD-DET-v0 logic) as the reference row; keep A1 as the not-repriced variant; have the ZEAL.CO test assert both the facts and the detector status. 6) IDX: mask the 25 sessions after a registry-verified split or stock dividend for the creep members (symmetric), or report 'reset in window' flags separately. 7) Fix the THESIS wording: volatility is neutralised only in the trading stage; add a detection-stage comparison against the v2 (volatility-matched) pool if the claim is to be tested at detection. 8) Correct the holdout wording to 'loaded then sliced; nothing computed' and merge the GLOBAL_HOLDOUT guard first as the proposal already recommends.

reasons: CORE-MEMBER PRIOR EVIDENCE ALREADY ON DISK (proposal claims 'nothing in the repo answers these'): the recorded discovery episode/control tables (idx-signals/research/E1/discovery/{episodes_E30,all_E30_controls}.csv; research/E2/{US,CRYPTO}/discovery/ same files; 13,527 E30 starts, 67,813 same-session non-event controls matched on band/liquidity/mcap, i.e. the same pool e1.Study._pool uses for the detection gate) carry volr, rngr, ret5, ret20, vol20 at the decision close t. A read-only pass over them gives the single-day analogue of A1_CREEP_QUIET (volr>=1.5 & rngr<=1.0 & |ret5|<=2*vol20*sqrt(5) & ret20<0.30): P(cond|E30 start)/P(cond|matched non-event) = 1.11 (IDX, 6.7% vs 6.1%), 0.96 (US, 4.7% vs 4.9%), 0.95 (CRYPTO, 1.7% vs 1.8%). This is a proxy (day t vs 5-session medians), not the E5 statistic, but a 5-session median volume >=1.5x base forces most days in t-4..t, including t, to have elevated volr, so an enriched creep state would show in volr at t; the recorded AUCs (0.50/0.52/0.45) and these proxies bound A1's lift near 1. With lift ~1.1 and any plausible N, the E30 Wilson lower bound does not clear the base rate (e.g. 2.08% precision at N=10,000 gives lower 1.80% < 1.88% on IDX), so the reference member is expected to fail falsifier (1) in all three markets before a single harness run.

A1 IS A CONJUNCTION OF NEGATIVELY ASSOCIATED CONDITIONS: Spearman(volr, rngr) is 0.57/0.50/0.74 (IDX/US/CRYPTO) in the recorded control sets, so P(rngr<=1 | volr>=1.5) is only 22%/17-22%/8%. The lab's own single case confirms the shape: kod-machine/research/ZEALAND_PILOT_v1/03_card/price_facts.json shows creep TRUE (2.3x, 2.07x) with quiet FALSE (rngr5 1.69/1.52, ret5 -19.5%/-16.8%) at T-72H and T-24H; the accumulation the thesis describes arrived with range expansion and a drawdown, which A1/A2/A3 exclude by construction. Not_repriced is also anti-selective: E30 starts are already repriced (ret20>=30%) 13.3% of the time on IDX and 9.3% on US vs 5.5%/4.9% for controls.

DETECTION-GATE INFERENCE IS ANTI-CONSERVATIVE FOR STATE DETECTORS: e1.Study.detector_table (e1.py:306-323) and evaluate (334-363) treat every flagged ticker-day as independent (Wilson on N=flags; 200 independent matched draws per flag). A1/A2/A3 are 5-session-window states, C1/C2 10/60-session states and B1/B2 a 6-40-session window state, so flags run on consecutive sessions of the same name and share overlapping t+1..t+5 outcome windows; one move yields up to five correlated hits. Effective N is a fraction of the flag count, the Wilson lower bound is too tight and the matched-random null variance is understated, so p_one_sided_vs_matched is biased low. E1's F1_ARA flags were event-like; E5's are not. The proposal lists 'repeat flags' as a reported risk but keeps the gate unchanged; the trading stage is protected by overlap=skip (backtest.py:302-316), the detection gate and the validation detection criterion are not.

MATCHED-CONTROL ADEQUACY IS OVERSTATED: the detection-stage pool (e1.py:215-227) matches only price_band, liquidity, market_cap, not volatility/momentum/drawdown. A3 (hivol20) and C1/C2 (hivol60) therefore pass the Wilson-vs-base gate and the validation 'detection p<0.05, lift>1' criterion largely through the known volatility separator (vol20 AUC 0.68/0.78; G11_HIGHVOL_ACTIVE alone gave 9.75x on US, research/E2/US/discovery/detector_selection.csv). Only the trading stage uses controls v2 (controls.py:71-74), and there matching is by tercile: on US, where E30 rates rise steeply within the top vol tercile, within-tercile residual confounding remains, so 'a pass attributes to the volume/path structure' is not established by the design as written.

VALIDATION WINDOW CONSUMED AND DESIGN FEEDBACK UNDERDECLARED: 2023 episode-level pre-event feature tables (ret5, ret20, volr, rngr, vol20, dd60, up5 at t) exist on disk for all three markets (research/E1/validation/episodes_E30.csv, research/E2/US/validation/episodes_E30.csv, research/E2/CRYPTO/validation/episodes_E30.csv); the thesis itself cites 2023 validation numbers (r5_median -10.3%/-11.5% from E2 validation result.json); US_BREAKOUT_v1's 2023 plan-level result (stop-based 5-session longs lose) informs the fixed-exit, longer-hold grid; crypto 2023 has already been the one-shot test window for two families (E2 trading, E4 v2 validation, research/E4/v2/REPORT.md on origin/claude/e4-fade-short-side). 'The only leakage is base rates and big-day behaviour' is incomplete. A 2023 pass is a confirmation on a consumed window, not a validation, and the proposal's language ('validated executable plan', 'PAPER-POLICY-v5 could carry') overstates what it can establish.

MULTIPLICITY WITHOUT CORRECTION: 8 detectors x 3 holds x 3 markets = 72 discovery pairs selected by maximum average net return (winner's curse), then one test per market at p<0.05 (trading) and p<0.05 (detection, anti-conservative per above); with three one-shot tests and no pre-registered correction, the family-wise chance of at least one market 'validating' under the global null is roughly 14% on the trading criterion alone. The proposal acknowledges 'weak evidence' but does not pre-commit a Bonferroni level (0.05/3 is expressible at the 0.005 floor) or a two-market replication rule.

N / COVERAGE STRUCTURAL FAILURES: B1/B2 require ret1(s0) >= 0.30, but IDX ARA bands (idxsig/market.py:34: 35% <= Rp200, 25% Rp200-5,000, 20% above; ARA unchanged through 2021-22) make a +30% close-to-close day possible only in the <=Rp200 band, so the IDX re-base members are confined to penny names and will not reach 200 flags / 200 scored under the quiet+hold+retrace path; on crypto (683 pairs) C-members and the A1 conjunction (1.7% single-day coverage) are thin. These are predictable before the run.

US ARM CANNOT ATTRIBUTE: panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z is survivor-only (manifest: 'names delisted earlier are absent'). A detector that selects quiet, low-priced names with rising volume is the dilution/ATM-offering profile with the highest delisting hazard, so survivorship biases the flagged arm more than the matched arm; both the absolute 'avg net > 0' gate and the matched difference are uninterpretable on US. No protocol change fixes this without a delisting-inclusive panel (a network pull, outside scope).

MINOR: '~1.4M eligible ticker-days in three markets' is the IDX panel row count (panel-20261013T194245Z.json rows 1,429,316); discovery eligible days are 323k + 2.67M + 221k = 3.2M. The E3 precondition already records DEVIATES on the matched baseline (research/E3/reproduce/result.json), so E5's reproduce stage will need --accept-deviation; not a flaw, but the protocol should say so. The panel csv for the pinned IDX manifest is absent on disk (only panel-20261007T225823Z.csv.gz exists), as the proposal notes.
verdicts.fix: Rescue requires protocol changes before freeze, in this order. (1) Pre-screen without harness runs: add creep (5-session median volume / prior-20 median), rngr5, quiet, not_repriced, vol10/vol60 and the re-base state as weak-signal columns in a one-pass Study on DISCOVERY only per market (same matched-set AUC machinery as E1 signal_stats, e1.py:272-304) and pre-register a go/no-go: the 72-run grid runs in a market only if an A-member's matched-set lift has a 95% interval excluding 1; the single-day proxies already on record (1.11/0.96/0.95) predict a no-go, which would cut the 30h to a few hours and still give the KOD tape detector its population base rate and non-events. (2) Debounce detection flags for the gate (first flag per name after >= 5 flag-free sessions, mirroring e1.Study.start) and compute the Wilson bound and the 200-draw matched p on debounced flags; report a name-level block bootstrap as sensitivity. (3) Use controls v2 buckets (add volatility, momentum, drawdown, listing_age) in the E5 Study's detection pool, report the flag vs matched vol20 distribution, and add a vol20-decile-matched sensitivity on US; state that A3/C1/C2 detection lifts are not evidence beyond volatility. (4) Pre-register p < 0.05/3 per market on the validation trading criterion, or require replication in two markets, before any claim of a 'validated' pair. (5) Relabel 2023 as 'confirmation on a consumed window', list the concrete leaks (validation episode tables on disk, E2 r5_median, US_BREAKOUT_v1 2023 plan result, E4 v2 2023 crypto regime), and make the prospective paper ledger the validation arm with a pre-set count of scored prospective outcomes before PAPER-POLICY-v5 may underwrite a BUY. (6) Drop B1/B2 from the IDX grid or redefine the IDX spike as an ARA lock in the <=Rp200 band, and pre-declare expected coverage per member per market. (7) Run US as a labelled sensitivity only (survivor-only panel) until a delisting-inclusive US panel exists; IDX (mirror era, delistings present) and crypto (190 delisted pairs) are the markets on which attribution is possible.

reasons: NOT REFUTED under the execution-realism lens, but three serious defects must be fixed in protocol.json before freeze; none is fatal because each has a protocol-level rescue. Verified against code: controls v2 features (/home/user/KOD-Machine/idx-signals/idxsig/controls.py:71-74), overlap skip (backtest.py:302-316), fill models A/B/C and the close-entry-only restriction on conditional plans (execution.py:365-366), e1.Study format check (e1.py:100-102) and IGNITION lookup (e1.py:190), e3 admissibility (e3.py:99-115), profiles unchanged (profiles.py). origin/claude/e4-fade-short-side does lift the restriction (only 'unlock' stays close-only) and adds GLOBAL_HOLDOUT (backtest.py:85,296). The A1 definition matches kod-machine/research/ZEALAND_PILOT_v1/03_card/price_facts.py:56-72 and was frozen in 01_protocol/FREEZE.json (2026-10-08T12:28:33Z). Long only: carry, borrow and liquidation lenses are empty.

SERIOUS 1 - unmodelled closing-auction spread/impact on IDX is first-order for a quiet-tape family. The IDX cost model is 0.15%/0.25% fees with no spread or impact term (profiles.py; execution.py docstring; quality.KNOWN_LIMITATIONS lists only 'no intraday path'). The raw mirror (data/raw/idx_mirror/bc0ac7712ce5/Saham/Semua/*.csv) carries closing bid/offer and their sizes, which panel.py:66 (usecols) drops. Measured on the discovery window 2021-01-22..2022-12-30 only (329,271 traded ticker-days, bid and offer quoted on 89%): closing quoted spread median 0.81% of close; <=Rp200 band median 1.09%, p75 1.67%, p90 2.35%; among rows with daily value >= Rp100M (the scale at which a Rp10M order passes the 10% capacity gate) median 0.68%, and 82.5% of those rows have a quoted spread larger than the entire modelled 0.40% round-trip fee; the resting offer at the close is smaller than Rp10M on 22.6% of them (26.3% in <=Rp200). A quiet flag by construction selects compressed-range sessions where the spread is a larger share of the achievable return, and a pre-move detector's per-trade edge is intrinsically small, so the admissibility gate 'avg net > 0 and above matched random' can admit a plan whose real auction cost exceeds its harness edge; the matched controls omit the same cost on both sides and do not protect the absolute gate. The lab's own CORRECTION_01 (origin/claude/us-pipeline-v1:idx-signals/research/IDX_CAUSAL_CAPACITY_v1/CORRECTION_01.md) already withdrew FILL-C as a recommendation ('C plans causally but can score infeasible fills... whole-session volume is itself only an upper bound for a closing-auction fill... No IDX equivalent [contract] exists'); the proposal re-adopts it with only a diagnostic.

SERIOUS 2 - B1_REBASE/B2 are structurally confined to the <=Rp200 band on IDX. The spike condition ret1(s0) >= 0.30 cannot occur above Rp200 under the regular-board ARA bands 35%/25%/20% (market.py BANDS: a Rp300 reference caps at +25%). Verified on the discovery window: 588 traded rows with close/previous-1 >= 30%, all with previous <= Rp200, zero above. E1 used F1_ARA instead of a RET30 member for IDX for exactly this reason. So the two re-base members on IDX live entirely in the band with the widest spread (median 1.1%) and a Rp1 tick that is 1% of price at the median (2% at p90), and their 200-flag/200-scored gates are in doubt before any run; the protocol as written does not say so.

SERIOUS 3 - the capacity gate removes the population the thesis is about, making a negative IDX result ambiguous. E3's recorded IDX 2021-22 runs under FILL-C at Rp10M (research/E3/discovery/plans.csv) show SKIP_LIQUIDITY 4,207 against EXITED 4,561 on the fixed/fixed plans, i.e. about 48% of non-ARA-locked attempts were unfillable at 10% of the 20-session median volume. On the discovery window 36.4% of traded ticker-days (42.2% in <=Rp200) have daily value below Rp100M, the scale a Rp10M order needs; 67 of 827 names are untraded on more than half their sessions. The 'operator working a thin float' names sit disproportionately in that unscorable half, so 'detects but no admissible plan' cannot be told apart from 'edge unfillable at Rp10M'. The protocol has no notional sensitivity and no detection lift by liquidity quintile.

MINOR - long holds (h10/h20) on IDX: data_end_exit='last_close' sells a name that stops trading at its last traded close (KNOWN_LIMITATIONS) and INCOMPLETE drops unfinished trades; a suspension-then-delisting is the loss path for a pre-spike long in goreng names. On record this is small so far (EXIT_DATA_END 0 in the E1 2023 runs and across E3's 108 plans; INCOMPLETE <= 27 per 9 plans; exits rolled >= 1 session on 44 of 251 scored FILL-C trades, max 19 sessions), but h20 roughly quadruples exposure to it.

MINOR - IDX regime mismatch: all of discovery 2021-22 ran under the COVID ARB 7% regime (market.py REGIMES 2020-03-13..2023-06-05) while validation 2023 crosses to ARB 15% (2023-06-05) and symmetric 35/25/20 (2023-09-04); the sale rolls until a non-locked close in both, so realised loss is not truncated, but roll duration and the matched comparison differ by regime.

MINOR - US panel is survivor-only (panel_us_repair manifest: Nasdaq Trader snapshot of 2026-10-08); C1/C2 target 'volatile names that have not collapsed' (dd60 >= -0.5), exactly the set from which later delistings are missing, so the absolute avg-net gate is flattered on US; acknowledged in RISKS but not neutralised by matched controls.

MINOR - IDX creep uses raw volume, and a rule cannot see reg_factor (RuleView excludes registry fields), so a registry-verified split or bonus issue inflates volume (1:10 -> 10x) and fires a spurious creep with a quiet reference chain; `value` (Rp, in RULE_FIELDS) is unit-free and a rule can detect a reset itself from previous vs the last close.

Checked and NOT a flaw: the panel's IDX `volume` is regular-market only (the raw non_regular_volume exceeds `volume` on 3.7% of discovery rows and is a separate column), so creep and FILL-C capacity do not count negotiated-market crossings; crypto `value` is Binance quote_volume (global_panel.py:135,139), so the 'unverified meaning' caution is unnecessary but harmless; fill A for crypto is ex-post but labelled; US fill B and tier costs stand in for half-spread as declared; holdouts are sealed by e1.Study's cut and explicit RunConfig ends (plus GLOBAL_HOLDOUT once PR #7 merges).
verdicts.fix: Before protocol.json is frozen (all pre-registered, none after a number is seen): (1) IDX cost floor: either a labelled per-side cost of one tick on the entry and exit price (market.tick_size; about 0.5-1% in <=Rp200) added to the 0.15/0.25% fees for every E5 IDX run, rule and baselines alike, with admissibility requiring avg net > 0 after it; or, better, a panel-v3 build that keeps the mirror's bid/offer/bid_volume/offer_volume columns (panel.py:66) so the harness charges half the closing quoted spread per side and skips entries whose order exceeds the closing offer depth, with these fields kept out of RuleView; and record the diagnostic 'share of scored trades whose size exceeded the closing offer depth' beside the CORRECTION_01 diagnostic. (2) IDX spike condition for B1/B2: an ARA-locked close (lock_up is in RULE_FIELDS, as F1_ARA) or ret1 >= 0.20, with a per-band flag count reported; keep ret1 >= 0.30 for US/crypto. (3) Capacity: pre-register a notional sensitivity (e.g. Rp2.5M, lots still whole at Rp50) and the detection-stage E30 lift by liquidity quintile, so 'detects but unfillable at Rp10M' is a distinct, written outcome; state which notional is primary. (4) h10/h20: pre-register a data_end_exit='zero' sensitivity and report rolled_sessions and INCOMPLETE counts per plan; report IDX validation by ARB regime. (5) IDX creep on `value` (or exclude the 25 sessions after a previous-vs-last-close reset) so splits and bonus issues cannot fire A-members. (6) Label any US-only pass as provisional on survivorship until the prospective paper arm scores it. These are protocol changes, not re-tunes: no threshold is chosen on any outcome.

refuted.title: E5-PATH: delayed-entry long after the fade. A pre-registered entry-timing x horizon grid on the frozen G2_RET30 flag (crypto primary, US secondary) with matched controls under each plan

reasons: CRYPTO (primary) survives the leakage lens: Binance prices are not rescaled, 190 delisted bases incl. 2020-21 delistings (LEND, ERD, NPXS, STRAT, XZC, HC, MCO, STORM) are retained, sessions are UTC days with open == prior close (LUNA rows confirm), and backtest.run slices the study market at `end` (idx-signals/idxsig/backtest.py L264/L279: bounds side='right', so a 2023-12-31 end never loads 2024). The lag axis adds no new look-ahead: _baseline receives the same ExecConfig (L340), execute() uses sig_idx + entry_lag for fixed entries (execution.py L371), overlap-skip uses s + entry_lag (L306), INCOMPLETE/EXIT_DATA_END logic (execution.py L446-455) is deterministic, by_year is keyed by signal year (L354-356).

US (secondary) as pre-registered (units='panel') carries a corporate-action look-ahead in the matched controls that research/E2/ERRATA.md item 1 already documents ('the controls are matched on the wrong band for the same names') and that the +1.5%/side stress rule does not touch. Quantified read-only on the proposal's own panel (panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z, sha 8d3b7ce4) and window 2020-07-01..2022-12-31, no outcomes computed: 3,460 G2_RET30 flag rows; 59.6% are names that reverse-split >=2x AFTER the signal date (51.7% >=10x, 25.4% >=100x, 13.5% >=1000x); 55.3% of flags would be matched on a different price band under as-traded units than under adjusted units, against 16.2% of all discovery ticker-days, i.e. the control pool for the flagged population is selected by a split that happens after the signal, 3.4x more often than for the universe. 19.3% of flags were real sub-$1 names but only 3.3% are banded <$1 under panel units; 284 real sub-$1 flags and 726 real $1-5 flags are banded >$20, so their 'matched' controls are mostly genuine large caps. With holds of 10-20 sessions the real-population drift gap between those groups matters more than at h5. controls.py L98-101 confirms the band uses the adjusted close unless as_traded is set.

US: the same adjusted units silently exclude the worst collapsers from the rule's scored set, an outcome-correlated exclusion of the kind research/E2/repair_v3/SELECTION_NOTE.md already identified for the quarantine. 349 of 3,460 discovery flags (10.1%, vs 2.24% of universe ticker-days) have an adjusted close above the $5,000 notional and become SKIP_LOT (execution.py L412-416); 235 of them traded below $5 as traded and 58 below $1; these are exactly the names with the largest later reverse splits, which repair_v3 measured at -9.17% vs -1.75% (2023, lag-1/h5) for the quarantined subset. ERRATA #1 shows the asymmetry (rule 10% SKIP_LOT vs controls 4%). This flatters the long side, in the direction of the proposal's hypothesis, and grows with the fat right tail the proposal relies on. The proposal's justification for 'panel' units (2020-22 schedule unverified) conflates tier error (bounded, stressed) with band/lot selection (unbounded, unstressed).

US survivorship: the universe is the Nasdaq Trader snapshot of 2026-10-08 (manifest 'survivorship'), so every 2020-22 name survived >= 4 years. For longs in names of which half later reverse-split >= 10x, the truncation of the left tail is severe and differential against controls (which, under adjusted banding, are mostly genuine >$20 names). No protocol change on this panel removes it; the proposal declares it but still allows a US cell to be 'admissible' and a US validation 'pass' with a stated consequence (a new paper policy version). On leakage grounds a US pass cannot be decision-grade.

CRYPTO minor: the panel is legacy format panel-global-v1 (manifest), built before the causal-close-v2 repair, with future-informed spike deletion (_spikes uses the next day's close, global_panel.py L38-44); only 2 rows were dropped, one inside discovery (LUNA 2022-05-13). More relevant: ca_mode='adjusted' assumes no reference resets, but Binance reused symbols after halts/redenominations, producing 3 synthetic G2_RET30 flags in discovery out of ~1,495 flag rows: LUNA 2022-05-31 (previous 0.00032 old-LUNA, close 8.87 LUNA 2.0 after a 19-day gap, +2.77M%), COCOS 2021-01-23 (1:1000 redenomination, +129,440%, 4-day gap), DREP 2021-04-02 (1:100 swap, +10,558%, 4-day gap). Each becomes a delayed long on a different asset with no control counterpart (LUNA 2.0 fell 8.87 -> 2.86 within 10 sessions). The proposal's statement that 'redenomination-style prints are handled by the panel's spike drops' is wrong: the spike drop removed the 2022-05-13 row and left the relisting flag. Direction is against the hypothesis and magnitude ~0.1-0.2pp per cell, so minor, but it is an unhandled corporate action on the primary arm.

Holdout guard is procedural only on HEAD: backtest.py has the IDX HOLDOUT guard (L253) but no GLOBAL_HOLDOUT; `end = cfg.end or panel_meta['source_boundary']` (L252) resolves to 2026-10-07 for the crypto panel, so any driver path that omits `end` loads the sealed rows and the run is not refused. The GLOBAL_HOLDOUT refusal exists only on origin/claude/e4-fade-short-side (PR #7). The proposal notes this conditionally ('if PR #7 is merged first') rather than as a precondition.

Verified consistent with the proposal, no issue: recorded E2 configs (results/runs/20261008T005732Z_MOONSHOT_E2_CRYPTO_D1_v1: ca_mode adjusted, entry_lag 1, hold 5, start/end 2023; 20261008T100745Z_MOONSHOT_E2_US_D1_v1: panel 8d3b7ce4, units panel, quarantine none, fill A, 1,101 scored, -3.745% vs -0.624%); fill model A's ex-post entry-session volume (execution.py L419) is a declared, pre-existing limitation that at $5,000 notional rarely binds on Binance; Yahoo dates are normalised with gmtoffset (global_panel.py L104-105) and Binance klines are filtered to closed UTC days (L128); listed_shares is NaN for both panels so market_cap is a uniform unknown bucket; the rule module's features are prefix-causal under rules.causal_signals and G2_RET30 needs only close/previous.
verdicts.fix: Protocol changes before freezing research/E5/protocol.json: (1) US grid runs with units='as_traded' (the repair panel carries unit_factor; controls.features bands on close x unit_factor and execute() sizes, tiers and SKIP_LOT on as-traded prices), with units='panel' retained only for the reproduce precondition of 20261008T100745Z; if the 2020-22 split ratios are considered unverified, require admissibility under BOTH unit modes and keep the +1.5%/side stress on top; record per cell the SKIP_LOT share and the as-traded band distribution of flags vs controls. (2) Downgrade the US arm to descriptive-only (no admissibility, no validation, no paper-policy consequence) OR state in the protocol that a US pass is non-decision evidence because the survivor-only universe truncates the flagged population's left tail differentially; the paper-ledger prospective scoring is the only clean US path. (3) Pre-register one data-quality exclusion applied identically to rule signals and control draws on both markets: drop a signal whose previous bar is more than 3 sessions earlier or whose ret1 exceeds +500% (the LUNA/COCOS/DREP symbol-reuse cases), and note that the crypto panel is panel-global-v1 with 2 future-informed row deletions (one in discovery). (4) Make the code-level holdout guard a precondition: merge PR #7's GLOBAL_HOLDOUT lines (backtest.py) or port them to this branch, and add a test that e5.harness_config always sets end from protocol.json periods and that backtest.run refuses a US/CRYPTO detector window reaching 2024-01-01. (5) Keep the proposal's description of the crypto arm; no fix needed there beyond (3) and (4).

reasons: REDENOMINATION ARTIFACTS DECIDE THE CRYPTO GRID AS WRITTEN. The protocol asserts 'redenomination-style prints are handled by the panel's spike drops only' and declines a jump exclusion ('jump_ratio not applicable (long, 1x)'). Checked on the proposal's own panel (data/panel/panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z.csv.gz, discovery rows only): global_panel._spikes drops only one-day spikes that revert the next day; a permanent level change passes, and because `previous` is chained to the pre-redenomination close, Market.build's reset test (last_close/ref) sees ratio 1, so under ca_mode='adjusted' the harness scores the jump as a return. Four G2_RET30-flagged names inside discovery carry such jumps: COCOS (flag 2021-01-15; halted 01-20..01-22; 2021-01-23 close 0.9003 vs previous 0.000695, a 1000:1 redenomination E4 v1 already documented), DREP (flags 2021-03-05 and 2021-03-19; 2021-04-02 close/previous = 107.6x), SUN (flag 2021-06-03; 2021-06-18 close/previous = 0.0012) and VIDT (flag 2022-10-19; 2022-11-09 ratio 0.051). Gross per-trade ratios these single flags would contribute to the 15 crypto cells: COCOS +126,000% (lag1/h5), +94,000%/+80,000% (lag1 h10/h20), +97,000..+164,000% in every lag-2 and lag-3 cell, SKIP_NOT_TRADED at lag 6, real at lag 11; DREP 03-05: +22,881% (lag6/h20), +13,771% (lag11/h20); DREP 03-19: +9,200..+10,400% in lag1/h10, lag1/h20, lag2/h10, lag2/h20, lag3/h10, lag3/h20, and +9,558..+13,288% in lag6/h5, lag6/h10, lag6/h20. So 13 of the 15 crypto cells (all but lag11/h5 and lag11/h10) contain at least one non-trade of +9,000% to +164,000%; with ~1,200 scored trades per cell (~750 in 2021; E4 reference row: 1,244 scored, 748 in 2021) a +10,000% trade adds about +8pp to the cell mean and +13pp to the 2021 mean, COCOS about +100pp/+170pp. The admissibility criteria 'avg net > 0', 'avg net > 0 in 2021' and the selection rule 'highest average net return' are then determined by which cells happen to span a redenomination, not by the hypothesis; the matched draws are contaminated at random (E4's reference row shows matched p2.5 = -108% for the mirrored short), so the p<0.05 test is noisy too. E4 v2 fixed exactly this with jump_ratio=10 (EXCLUDED_DATA_JUMP, applied to rule and baselines alike, origin/claude/e4-fade-short-side execution.py L87/L532-540), which would catch all five jumps (ratios 1295, 107.6, 0.0012, 0.051). A protocol change rescues it, so serious rather than fatal; as proposed, the crypto discovery table would be uninterpretable.

THE DECISION STATISTIC IS A RAW PER-TRADE MEAN WITH 'HIGHEST MEAN' SELECTION ACROSS HOLDS UP TO 20 SESSIONS IN CRYPTO 2021. Even after excluding redenominations, E4's record shows real 5-session squeezes of +200% to +424% (GMT, WRX, DOGE, NKN, CHR, STMX) on these flags; at 20 sessions the right tail is fatter still. The selection rule will pick the cell containing the largest single realized winner, i.e. the noisiest cell, and 'avg net > 0 in 2021' is met by the tail rather than by drift (E4 v1: 0 of 144 short plans positive in 2021, i.e. every long-equivalent plan was positive in the bull year). E3's rule is kept 'for comparability', but E3 searched IDX holds of 2-5 sessions with price limits; it was not designed for unbounded 20-session crypto tails. No robustness co-criterion (winsorized/trimmed mean, or positivity after removing the top 1% of trades) is pre-registered.

THE FALSIFIER'S INFERENCE IS LOGICALLY INVALID. The hypothesis is relative ('flagged names drift up relative to matched names') but admissibility requires an ABSOLUTE positive average in every discovery year with >=50 scored, and 2020 (110 scored at lag1/h5), 2021 and 2022 all bind on crypto. 2022 is a -65% BTC year; E4's record shows 143 of 144 mirrored plans positive for shorts in 2022 at holds <=5, and a 10-20 session matched long in 2022 will itself be negative. A cell that beats matched by a wide margin in 2022 can therefore fail admissibility, after which the protocol declares 'the flagged names keep losing versus matched names at every entry timing' and closes the family. 'No admissible cell' does not imply 'losing vs matched'; the mechanism verdict rests on the wrong statistic, while the only relative-by-year quantities (backtest.by_year already carries random_matched_avg_net_return per year; the path map) are declared 'descriptive, non-decision'. The stated information value ('either way the repo pins the mechanism') is therefore overstated.

MATCHED-CONTROL ADEQUACY FOR DELAYED ENTRIES. controls.matched_draws matches at the signal session s (features at s; momentum is a broad top tercile of the 20-session return, not an extreme) and _baseline executes the controls under the same ExecConfig from s+k. By s+6 the flagged names have systematically faded (E2: median 5-session return about -10% vs 0% matched in both markets) while controls drifted randomly, so the two populations differ in a known way at the entry session (recent 5-session decline, realized volatility, drawdown). A positive delayed cell vs matched-at-s controls cannot separate 'retained information after an unwind' from a generic short-term reversal after a sharp 5-session decline, a third mechanism the proposal's unwind-vs-lottery dichotomy omits. Matching is also loose on crypto to begin with: in the recorded E2 crypto 2023 run only 30 of 270 attempts matched on all seven features, 16 on price band alone, drawdown was matched for 14% and listing_age for 11% of attempts. Fixable by a pre-registered second control arm re-matched at s+k-1 (same features plus the s..s+k-1 return), not by the current design.

US ARM: 'PANEL' UNITS EMBED FUTURE REVERSE SPLITS IN THE PRICE LEVELS THAT DRIVE FILLS AND MATCHING. On the repair panel's discovery G2 flags (3,460 flags, 1,224 names): 61% have unit_factor != 1, 43% have a later reverse split of >=10x, 24% >=100x; 10.1% have a panel close above $5,000 and are SKIP_LOT at the $5,000 notional, a skip determined by a reverse split that happens after the trade; 55% of flags sit in a different price/cost band in panel units than as traded, and the matched controls are drawn from that wrong band. research/E2/diagnostics/us_reverse_splits.json shows on 2023 that every SKIP_LOT (154 of 154) was a later-reverse-split name and that such names averaged -6.46% vs -0.33% for the rest: the SKIP_LOT filter removes the worst-outcome population using future information, an outcome-correlated exclusion of the same kind the proposal cites repair_v3 to avoid (quarantine). The pre-registered +1.5%/side stress covers cost-tier error only, not SKIP_LOT or band matching. Direction is flattering for longs, so a US discovery pass could be this artifact.

MULTIPLICITY AND CONSUMED VALIDATION (declared, but weak guards). 14 selectable, nested, highly correlated cells per market, 28 in all, each at p<0.05 with a 0.005 floor from 200 draws; the per-year rule is no null guard in bull years (2020H2, 2021 crypto: nearly any long is positive) and a market-regime filter in bear years. The single 2023 run per market cannot control the family-wise error of 14 selections, and 2023 has been consumed twice on the same 312 crypto flags (E2 lag1/h5 long, 264 scored; E4 v2 BEAR short subset, 34 scored) and at least 12 times on US; the proposal's own design reasoning cites 2023 numbers (E2 crypto -1.90% vs +1.42%, E4 v2 -1.50%) to reject the regime-gated alternative. The lag-1/h10 and lag-1/h20 cells, which are selectable, include the t+1..t+5 window whose 2023 outcome is known (a known handicap, not a flattering leak).

CLAIMS THAT CHECK OUT (not refutation): crypto open equals the prior close (median |open/prev-1| = 0.045%, 99th pct 0.73% on pre-2023 rows); sample size on crypto 2023 is not a problem: from the recorded 2023 signal dates alone (312 signals, timing only, no outcomes) every cell has 238-270 attempts and 199-264 trades that can complete inside 2023 (lag11/h20: 238 attempted, <=199 scored), so the stated risk of falling below 100 is overstated; the code claims are accurate (ExecConfig.plan maps a fixed entry's lag to entry_window; execute enters a fixed plan at s+entry_lag ignoring entry_window, so the proposed resolve_plan change is required and sufficient; overlap-skip uses s+entry_lag; e3.harness_config hard-codes entry_lag=1); E3 never delayed an unconditional entry beyond s+1 or held beyond 5; the E4 branch's GLOBAL_HOLDOUT and jump_ratio exist as described. One implementation caveat: the E2 crypto run's recorded config carries units/fill_model/quarantine = None, which execute() rejects if passed through verbatim, so the reproduce stage must coerce those to defaults (how the E4 branch achieved REPRODUCED was not traced).
verdicts.fix: Protocol changes that rescue the design (pre-registered before any statistic): (1) adopt E4 v2's jump exclusion on the long side, jump_ratio=10 (EXCLUDED_DATA_JUMP for rule and baselines alike, already in PR #7's execution.py), and record the excluded (ticker, session) list in the discovery output; (2) add a pre-registered tail-robustness co-criterion to admissibility (e.g. the cell must stay positive and p<0.05 after removing its top 1% of trades, or on a 1%-winsorized mean) so selection is not decided by one squeeze; (3) separate the two verdicts: trading admissibility (E3 rule) and the mechanism verdict on rule-minus-matched by year (by_year.random_matched_avg_net_return is already emitted), with the falsifier restated as 'rule minus matched <= 0 at lag 6 and 11 in every discovery year'; (4) add a second control arm re-matched at the entry session (features at s+k-1 plus the s..s+k-1 return) as the mechanism comparison, keeping the harness's matched-at-s arm for comparability; (5) for US, use units='as_traded' for sizing, cost tiers and the matching band (unit_factor exists on the repair panel) or drop the whole-share lot constraint so SKIP_LOT cannot depend on a future reverse split, keep the +1.5%/side stress, and report the share of flags whose status differs between panel and as-traded units; (6) consider p<0.01 on discovery given 28 correlated cells, and state explicitly that a US pass is a replay-year result. Also coerce None config fields to defaults in the reproduce stage.

reasons: CRYPTO (primary arm) as specified books same-ticker token redenominations as long price returns, and the mean-based selection is maximally exposed. The panel (idx-signals/data/panel/panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z.csv.gz) carries non-reverting unit changes under the same ticker with a 3-6 day suspension before them: COCOS 2021-01-23 (close 0.000695 -> 0.9003, +129,440%), DREP 2021-04-02 (0.0263 -> 2.828, +10,558%), LUNA 2022-05-31 (+2.77M%), and downward SUN 2021-06-18 (-99.9%), VIDT 2022-11-09 (-95%), BNX 2023-02-22, QUICK 2023-07-21. The proposal's stated protection ('redenomination-style prints are handled by the panel's spike drops only; no jump_ratio on the long side') is wrong: global_panel._spikes drops only one-day spikes that revert the next day, so none of these rows is dropped (verified present), and with ca_mode='adjusted' and previous == prior-row close (share 1.0000) execution.py's reset detector never fires, so nothing is EXCLUDED_CORP_ACTION.

Mechanical calendar enumeration on the harness's own rules (entry at s+k on the continuous daily axis, exit rolled to the next present session) shows 13 of the 15 crypto cells hold at least one G2_RET30 trade across an UPWARD swap: every lag-1/2/3 cell crosses COCOS (flag 2021-01-15, entry 01-16/17/18, exit rolled into the 01-23 print or later; +129,440% booked), and fixed6|h5, fixed6|h10, fixed6|h20, fixed1..3|h10 and fixed11|h20 cross DREP (flags 2021-03-05/03-19; +10,558%). Only fixed11|h5 and fixed11|h10 are clean. One COCOS trade adds roughly +90 to +130 percentage points to a cell's pooled and 2021 average over ~1,000-1,400 scored trades; one DREP trade ~+8 to +10pp. No matched draw can carry the same print, so p vs matched = 0.005 mechanically and the 2021 per-year criterion is satisfied by a non-trade; 'highest average net return' then selects a COCOS cell (lag 2/3 any hold, or lag 1 h10/h20) whenever its 2020H2 and 2022 averages happen to be positive, and the single 2023 validation would test a plan chosen for a token swap. The clean delayed cells (lag 11) are structurally disadvantaged against the contaminated ones.

The repo already hit exactly this on the h5 window: origin/claude/e4-fade-short-side research/E4/REPORT.md L35-36 ('The reference plan's average is one trade: COCOS, shorted at 0.000714 on 2021-01-16 and bought back at 0.9003 a week later, Binance's 1000:1 COCOS redenomination, not a move'), visible in E4/CRYPTO/discovery/plans.csv G2_RET30|fixed1|fixed|h5 (2021 avg -173.1% over 748 trades = -1,295 return units = one COCOS print). E4 v2 added ExecConfig.jump_ratio (close/prev beyond 10x inside (entry, exit] -> EXCLUDED_DATA_JUMP, both sides alike; execution.py L146-149, L532-540 on that branch). The proposal cites E4's reference rows as the lag-1 long cells by symmetry yet declines the guard E4 needed, and its precondition stage cannot catch this: the named reproduce target 20261008T005732Z_MOONSHOT_E2_CRYPTO_D1_v1 is 2023-only, where the only swaps (BNX, QUICK) are downward and were not crossed (status counts show no exposure).

US (secondary arm): units='panel' re-introduces an outcome-correlated, rule-vs-control-asymmetric exclusion that the repo's own ERRATA documents and the repair showed how to remove. In the proposal's own reproduce target 20261008T100745Z_MOONSHOT_E2_US_D1_v1 (R1c), SKIP_LOT is 156/1,503 rule attempts (10.4%) vs 12,184/300,600 matched-control attempts (4.1%); all 156 have split-adjusted opens > $5,000 while 77% traded under $5 and 38% under $1 (unit_factor down to 2.7e-8, i.e. cumulative future reverse splits up to 1:37,500,000; e.g. HUBC $0.07 shown as $2.6M, XXII $2.90 shown as $43M). These are the dilution/death-spiral names, excluded from the rule's population 2.5x more often than from controls by future information. research/E2/ERRATA.md L15-18 states this ('All 154 SKIP_LOT attempts are among [names that reverse-split later]... 4% SKIP_LOT vs 10%') and research/E2/repair/HANDOFF.md sec.4 shows as-traded sizing gives 'SKIP_LOT 0'. In 2020H2-2022 panel units, 8.2% of as-traded <$5 ticker-days and 11.6% of <$1 ticker-days are un-sizeable (adjusted close > $5,000), so the discovery universe is thinned the same way.

US matched controls are matched on the wrong price band for most trades: in R1c, 52.8% of the 1,101 scored trades sit in a different adjusted-vs-as-traded band, and price_band is the first matching priority (controls.py VERSIONS v2; features() bands on adjusted close when units='panel'). ERRATA.md L22-23 records this too. The proposal's +1.5%/side stress addresses only the cost-tier error (52.3% of scored trades had an understated entry tier, mean 0.42%/side, max 1.45%); it does nothing for the SKIP_LOT exclusion or the band mismatch. The justification given ('repair_v3 showed name quarantine is outcome-correlated') conflates quarantine with units: repair_v3/SELECTION_NOTE.md recommends keeping every name in provider (as-traded) units and bounding the tier, which is R1b's configuration (as_traded, quarantine none), not panel units.

Secondary realism inaccuracies in the protocol text: the crypto cost is described as '0.1% fee + 0.1% slippage per side plus the 0.1% tier' (0.3%/side), but the recorded E2 crypto config is fee_buy=fee_sell=0.001 plus the profile tier 0.001 = 0.2%/side (profiles.py L53-55; run config); encoding 0.3% would make the grid non-comparable with the reference row and the reproduce target. The descriptive path.csv (mean open(t+1)->close(t+j), j=1..21, by year) and the pre-stated falsifier pattern ('mean rule-minus-matched still declining from j=6 to j=21 in every discovery year') are also mean-based and would be dominated in 2021 by the COCOS/DREP prints unless the same jump guard is applied.

Claims that were checked and hold (not grounds for refutation): crypto 'open' exists and equals the prior close in practice (median |open/prev-1| = 0.041% pre-2024, 0.28% of days > 1%); no leveraged tokens or stablecoins are in the crypto universe (0 UP/DOWN/BULL/BEAR bases, only PAXG as a non-coin); the $5,000/10% fill floor almost never binds on crypto (0.24% of 2020H2-2022 ticker-days have value < 50k USDT); 46 pre-2024 pairs end before 2023-12-01 (EXIT_DATA_END, as E2 accepted); 11 pairs have 536 missing days inside their span (suspensions, exits roll forward); backtest.run slices the study market at `end` (L264, L279) so 2024+ rows are never loaded, and the E4 branch's GLOBAL_HOLDOUT guard exists as stated (backtest.py L85, L296-300); the US panel has tickers_ending_inside_window = 0 (survivor-only, declared); fill model A's ex-post entry-session volume applies to rule and controls alike at every lag (symmetric, declared); no carry/liquidation applies to 1x spot longs; sizing is whole units with lot_size 1 on crypto (only BTC-priced pairs SKIP_LOT, 0 rule attempts in 2023).

map.summary:
Map of what idx-signals (HEAD = claude/idx-signals-test-repo-ds0jw7, commit e635e22) can express, with PR #7 (origin/claude/e4-fade-short-side) and PR #3 (origin/claude/us-pipeline-v1) read via git show.

SIGNAL INTERFACE: a rule is a frozen module exposing compute(view) -> float array shaped (names x sessions) with values 1 (signal at that close), 0 (evaluated, none), NaN (not evaluable). The view (rules.RuleView) carries exactly 12 exchange fields: close, prev, high, low, volume, value, present, tradeable, lock_up, lock_down, listed_shares, open, plus tickers and dates; nothing from the corporate-action registry or unit factors. Causality is by construction: backtest calls compute once per session d on a view holding sessions 0..d and only names listed by d, records column d, then checks a full-window call agrees (LookaheadError otherwise). A static AST audit forbids any import beyond numpy/pandas/math/zlib/hashlib/itertools/statistics/idxsig.market, any I/O, module-level non-literals, classes, decorators, state; a PEP 578 sandbox blocks file/network/process/frame/heap access during compute. A rule CAN use the full cross-section at d (E1 uses the cross-sectional median return; E4 conditions on BTC's 50-session mean because BTC is a row of the crypto panel) but CANNOT emit scores, weights, sizes, stops or multi-leg instructions.

EXECUTION (HEAD): one independent trade per (name, signal session), fixed notional (IDX Rp10m, US/CRYPTO $5k), whole lots (IDX 100, else 1), entry at the close of s+entry_lag (IDX) or the open of s+1 (US/CRYPTO), exit at the close of entry+holding_days rolled forward while untraded or locked at ARB; IDX ARA lock refuses entry. Fill models: A (ex-post 10% of entry-session volume), B (FILL-B-v1, decision-time median volume, open entries, as_traded units), C (FILL-C-v1, decision-time, IDX close entries, registry-scaled). Costs: per-side fees (IDX 0.15%/0.25%; US 0/SEC fee + price-tier cost 1.5%..0.05%; CRYPTO 0.1%+0.1%), no price impact, no dividends, no carry on longs. Corporate actions: registry (IDX) scales only verified splits/stock dividends; rights issues and unresolved resets exclude the trade; US/CRYPTO use ca_mode adjusted. Plans (research/E3): entry fixed/confirm/pullback/unlock within an entry window; exit fixed/stop_ref/first_down; HEAD restricts conditional plans to close entries (IDX). Long only on HEAD.

E4 BRANCH ADDS: side short (open-entry markets only, refused under auto-rejection limits), exits stop_high/first_up, open-based conditional entries for US/CRYPTO longs and shorts, carry_per_session from the profile (US 0.3%/session borrow, CRYPTO 0.05%/day funding), optional isolated-margin liquidation on the session high, jump_ratio exclusion (EXCLUDED_DATA_JUMP), GLOBAL_HOLDOUT (2024-01-01 on) guard for US/CRYPTO, --side and e4-* CLI, tail statistics and hit-rate/tail admissibility. Recorded results: v1 0/144 admissible; v2 31/288 admissible, frozen pair failed validation on 2023 (34 scored, avg -1.50%, p 0.78, 3 liquidations).

MATCHED CONTROLS (controls v2): for each attempted signal, 200 draws on the same session from evaluable names in the same price_band, liquidity quintile (20-session median traded value), market_cap quintile (close x listed_shares; IDX mirror era only), volatility tercile, momentum tercile, drawdown tercile, listing_age bucket; relaxed from the last feature until >=5 names match; executed under the identical plan; plus a same-session uniform baseline. Not matched: sector, board, free float (no point-in-time data).

RECORDING: write_run refuses a dirty idxsig/ tree, creates results/runs/<UTC stamp>_<rule_id>_<version>/ with summary.json, trades.csv.gz, random_draws.csv, REPORT.md (exclusive-create, read-only), appends one line to results/RUNS.jsonl with file hashes, and git-commits; verify-runs and tools/check_append_only.py (pre-commit) enforce append-only. Experiment modules (e3.py, e4.py) read research/<E>/protocol.json (sha256 stamped), require a precondition reproduce stage, run a discovery grid (plan_grid x detector candidates) through backtest.run with a signal cache, write plans.csv/summary.json, apply a pre-registered admissibility+selection rule, require SELECTED to be committed into the rule module (so the rule hash covers the plan), then one validation run recorded via write_run.

PR #3 (us-pipeline-v1) is NOT in HEAD, branched before E3 (merge-base c09a27a), and its diff removes E3 plan code; it adds exec_us.py (EXEC-US-v1 per-trade stop/limit/risk sizing), contract.py (EXEC-US-v2.1 single cash Account with reservations, ADV priority, replay + forward_step) and fill model B2. The local claude/us-breakout-v1 branch extends it with breakout.py and research/US_BREAKOUT_v1 (standalone runner, result: no edge on 2023).

Signals are 0/1/NaN only (rules/__init__.py:163-170); no score, rank, weight, stop or size can be passed from a rule to execution. Sizing is a fixed notional per trade (ExecConfig.notional); position size cannot depend on the signal.

Conditional entries and exits on HEAD require entry_price == 'close' (execution.py:365-366), i.e. IDX only; open-based plans and the short side exist only on origin/claude/e4-fade-short-side (PR #7, unmerged).

Each trade is independent: overlap skip is per name only (backtest.py:302-316); there is no cash, position-count or cross-name priority constraint in backtest.run. The only account model (contract.py EXEC-US-v2.1) lives on the unmerged us-pipeline-v1 branch and is not wired to the matched-control baselines.

Daily bars only: no intraday path (quality.py:27). Stops on HEAD are close-based (stop_ref, first_down); E4's liquidation reads the session high; exec_us (branch) reads the session low for the resting stop. Nothing inside the session can be modelled.

Rule identity: the rule hash covers the rule text and the whole module source (rules/__init__.py:54-57); editing a rule module, including SELECTED or thresholds, is a new rule, and a frozen detector (E1 F1_ARA, E2 G2_RET30, E4 SELECTED) must not be re-tuned on data its outcomes were seen on (standing rule; E3/E4 copy detector code verbatim and search only plans).

Every stage refuses a dirty idxsig/ tree (results.py:219-220, cli.py:326/345/379); results/runs, research/, data/manifests, ca_registry-*, paper/ are frozen by tools/check_append_only.py; research stage directories are created with exist_ok=False (e3.py:169, 211, 273), so a stage cannot be re-run into the same directory.

Matched controls match on price_band, liquidity, market_cap (IDX mirror era only), volatility, momentum, drawdown, listing_age at the signal session (controls.py:71-74), relaxed to >= 5 names (MIN_POOL, controls.py:44); sector, board and free float are not available point-in-time (controls.py:66-70). A new experiment must not condition on features the controls cannot match unless it adds them to controls.features.

Registry mode (IDX) requires a registry built from the exact panel sha (backtest.py:266-273); ca_mode for US/CRYPTO is forced to 'adjusted' by the CLI (cli.py:283); fill model B/B2 need units='as_traded' and a repair panel with unit_factor; fill model C needs the registry.

Protocol discipline (research/E3/protocol.json, research/E4/protocol.json): selection on discovery only, one validation run per frozen pair, SELECTED committed before any validation statistic, consequence_if_failed = family exhausted; a further attempt is a new protocol with a new idea, not a re-tune (research/E4/v2/REPORT.md 'Status').
gaps: No code or tests were executed in this pass (read-only); the README's '222 tests' count and the test suite's state on HEAD are unverified.

What the crypto panel's `value` column holds (quote-asset volume in USDT or something else) was not verified; controls.liquidity and contract.adv_value rely on it.

Nothing is known about the kod-machine/ side (KOD cards, evidence, timestamps) beyond the root README; it was out of scope here.

KOD lab (kod-machine/) is a forensic ledger, not a scanner: a case = a hashed card (symbol, venue, call_type, decision_cutoff, three information sets at exactly T-30D/T-72H/T-24H, story, disposition, critic, frozen KOD-DET-v0 evaluations) anchored in git with RFC 3161 tokens; outcomes are a later append-only row. RETROSPECTIVE cards reconstruct past moves and never count; PROSPECTIVE cards must be STRICT-v3 (every non-null fact cites a recorded KOD-EVIDENCE-v2 object published by that set's cutoff, grade A-C, recorded before the open), opened within 1 hour of decision_cutoff and before a pre-registered outcome_window.start, with at least one TSA answering and the anchor commit pushed; they count only when AUTHORITATIVE (GitHub push-run receipt for the exact anchor commit dated before window start). Scoring: per-detector hit rate on both sides over AUTHORITATIVE closed prospective cases, hit = REPRICED_UP for four detectors, REPRICED_DOWN for NARRATIVE_WITHOUT_MECHANISM; calibration NOT_STARTED until 30 such cases; detector_table is always UNVALIDATED/promotable=false.
Current state (var/kod.db, read-only): 4 cases (NVDA, SMCI retrospective v1; ZEAL retrospective v3 PARTIAL; one SIMULATED), 0 prospective, 0 scans, 19 evidence objects (all ZEALAND: 15 B, 2 C, 2 D), 0 GitHub receipts, 96 tests. Detector source still hashes to the bound value (0a0e0a73...), doctrine 246deb4a..., so an open today is not refused on those grounds.
What an open today needs: evidence declarations recorded first (kod evidence, each needs source_url/type/publisher/document_type/publication_time+basis/retrieval_time/as_of_cutoff/grade/existence_method/content_method/provenance; bytes optional), a card from seeds/prospective_template.json with decision_cutoff = the run minute, set cutoffs exactly -30d/-72h/-24h, a future window, a critic note, disposition WATCH/REJECT (INVESTIGATE needs the critic), network to freetsa/sectigo, git push of the anchor commit, then GITHUB_TOKEN for `kod receipt fetch`, and commit var/kod.db. Nothing in code chooses the name: the card is operator-authored; the only machine link is scan_entry_id to a `kod scan` logged earlier with every name evaluated. Close = after window end, with card_sha and an operator-supplied outcome_label from {REPRICED_UP, REPRICED_DOWN, NO_REPRICE, UNKNOWN, CENSORED}; KOD codes no % threshold, so the outcome rule must be pre-registered in the card text.
Feed analysis: the idxsig paper scan (US 22:53Z after a 20:00Z close, 15 G2_RET30 candidates on 2026-10-13; crypto 00:25Z; IDX 10:26Z) fits KOD's timing gate (open within the hour, window = next session onward). But KOD's structure puts the +30% day outside every information set if the card is opened the same evening (T-24H ends before that session), so the detectors evaluate pre-spike facts and the spike is T-0 context in story text only; if instead the card is opened the next evening so T-24H includes the spike, PRIMARY_DOC_BEFORE_PRICE and VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET are NO_SIGNAL by construction (they require price not repriced / quiet) and the window skips d+1, where E2 found the median lead to peak is 1 session. The well-formed prospective ask is "does it reprice again (+30% from the signal close) within d+1..d+5", which matches the paper ledger's own E30 scoring and has historical reference only (E2 validation 2023: P(E30|G2) US 15.4%, crypto 18.5%; median 5-session return after a flag -10.3% / -11.5%). "Does a catalyst surface" is not a KOD outcome label (schema CHECK), only a T-24H input fact; a catalyst appearing after the open cannot be scored without a new migration and doctrine version. Doctrine 79-81 forbids a winner list without non-events, so the legitimate KOD-shaped integration is `kod scan` of the whole scanned universe (flagged = G2_RET30, facts optional, no evidence burden), which yields the FLAG:G2_RET30 lift row against a prospective base rate; opening 15 STRICT cases/day is infeasible on evidence throughput (ZEALAND took 19 objects for one name). A pre-repricing watchlist is needed to test the detectors as designed; its non-outcome-selected sources are dated-catalyst calendars (DATED_CATALYST_KNOWN), primary-document feeds such as EDGAR/IDX disclosures (PRIMARY_DOC_BEFORE_PRICE, NARRATIVE_WITHOUT_MECHANISM) and a tape pre-screen from the bars the paper scan already pulls, using the ZEALAND protocol's fact definitions frozen 2026-10-08 (ret20>=30%, 5v20 volume ratio>=1.5, rngr<=1 and |ret5|<=2*vol20*sqrt5) rather than new thresholds; each would be a new scanner id logged via `kod scan`, not an edit to KOD-DET-v0.
